Jeremiyah Love Headlines Loaded Cardinals-Cowboys Injury Report
full_text:
Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love headlines a loaded injury report ahead of the team's Week 8 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.
Love, who has missed the last two weeks with an ankle injury, returned to the practice field in limited fashion today.
Out of the 15 total Cardinals listed on Wednesday's report, nine did not participate.
Full reports for both sides:
Wilson was donning a yellow non-contact jersey during practice. It also appears the Cardinals are still dealing with a team illness that occurred last week.
It appears the Cardinals could get Love back into the mix, though head coach Mike LaFleur says impressive backup running back Bam Knight could still have a role.
“Yeah, Bam has been doing a really good job. He’s running the ball well and obviously brought an explosive element to the run game that was needed. Yes, Bam will still have a role but I’m excited to get Jeremiyah back, particularly at practice this week," he said.
A struggling Dallas defense could possibly get back on track against a struggling Cardinals offensive line, one that allowed 13 quarterback hits on Jacoby Brissett last week.
“It’s all-encompassing. It’s the plays I call too," LaFleur said of Arizona's struggles.
"You have to pick and choose your spots of when you’re going to run, those seven steppers (seven step drops) or the play (action) passes and stuff like that. We knew we were going to have to. You have to pick and choose our spots when we’re not going to get as many up and we’re going to help out with some of the ribs and licks and stuff like that — our chip mechanisms.
"Again, it’s all-encompassing but I know collectively as a group, we can all do better (at) coaching and playing.”
The Cardinals and Cowboys will practice twice more this week before revealing official game statuses on Friday.

title: Cardinals' Michael Wilson Gets Surprising Week 8 Practice Update
full_text:
ARIZONA — There were a handful of notable Arizona Cardinals missing from the team's Wednesday practice , and though Michael Wilson wasn't one, we did get a surprising update during the period open to reporters.
Wilson was spotted wearing a yellow non-contact jersey on Wednesday, which signals Wilson is dealing with an injury. In public knowledge he emerged clean from Week 7's loss to the Denver Broncos and didn't appear to be dealing with any injuries, nor did head coach Mike LaFleur mention anything about Wilson in his morning press conference.
Wednesday #AZCardinals practice report: HERE: Carson Beck, Jeremiyah Love, Andrew Wingard, Max Melton, Darius Robinson, NOT HERE: Walter Nolen, Budda Baker, Josh Sweat, Isaac Seumalo, Elijah Wilkinson, Tyler Allgeier A bit of a surprise… Michael Wilson spotted in a yellow… pic.twitter.com/IVB2Ri361Z
Players wearing this jersey signals to teammates that he cannot be blocked or hit.
While this doesn't automatically mean Wilson is in concussion protocol, players progressing through protocol are typically the ones that don the non-contact jerseys during practice. Reporters are not able to ask LaFleur about his status until Friday when he holds his next press conference.
The Cardinals travel to face the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Arizona will reveal their first injury report of the week later today, which will provide us clarity on what exactly Wilson is dealing with.
Wilson's production has slowed down a bit since Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded, which is something LaFleur was specifically asked about earlier this week:
“I think if you take away the stats from it, he’s running good routes and he’s separating. He has drawn quite a few penalties this year as well. I mean that got us going there on that third drive (of the game). With that being said, I know he can still make that play — for himself too, but (it’s) just kind of the momentum of making a play as opposed to a penalty," LaFleur said, reflecting back on his performance against the Broncos.
"I mean he (Broncos CB Riley Moss) held him. We told the official it was going to be a double move. He ran the double move. It was a really good route and the guy held him. That was clearly a penalty, but again, I know we can make that play. Then he drew another one a little bit later, but our pocket collapsed right away. To me, when we’re clicking on all cylinders, those are touchdowns. He ran right by the guy off the double move. He’s doing a lot of good things. He obviously hasn’t had the stats and that’s kind of what you’re insinuating right there.
"Again, all he can do is control what he can control — win his one-on-one matchups when the ball’s thrown to him, catch it, and then obviously try to stay grounded and make as much ‘YAC’ (yards after the catch) as he can.”
This would be a massive blow for the Cardinals' offense if Wilson isn't available.

title: Walter Nolen III Gets Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Cowboys
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals will not see Walter Nolen III practice on Wednesday, head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters.
Nolen is dealing with an ankle injury that kept him out of Arizona's Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos.
"He's doing good. He'll will be DNP today, but he's getting better," LaFleur said of Nolen.
The Cardinals will practice twice more (Thursday and Friday) this week before being required to declare Nolen as out, questionable or doubtful.
Arizona travels to face the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. The Cardinals are 2-5 while the Cowboys are 3-4.
Nolen, a second-year defensive lineman, has shown the ability to wreck offensive gameplans on a weekly basis. The one drawback? He's battled injuries since entering the league.
Nolen suffered a calf injury before training camp of his rookie season, which saw him miss the beginning of 2025 before returning halfway through the year. He played a handful of games and showed massive promise before suffering a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve, ending his year.
Nolen had surgery (later revealed to be a meniscus) but made a full recovery and was healthy for 2026's training camp, though he suffered a minor lower body injury during the team's time at State Farm Stadium.
Last week was the first regular season game Nolen missed for this year.
Nolen holds potential to be one of the best young defensive linemen in the NFL, and Arizona certainly needs it. Their defensive line pressure rate of 24.7% ranks dead-last in the league. In a front seven that's been largely uninspiring, Nolen's presence has been noticeable on a weekly basis.
The Cardinals, typically precautious with injuries, are going to be smart and hold Nolen out of action today. We'll see if that changes throughout the week, though it's clear the former first-round pick will be somebody to watch this week as things progress.
In six games this season, Nolen has 14 tackles, one sack and three quarterback hits.

title: Cardinals Set Asking Price for Josh Sweat as Trade Rumors Heat Up
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals sit at just 2-5 on the season, positioning themselves as prime selling candidates ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline.
Their recent deal that sent Marvin Harrison Jr. out to the Houston Texans for a second-round pick signaled Arizona would be willing to do business if the price is right for just about anybody, and if recent trade rumors have any merit, Cardinals outside linebacker Josh Sweat could very well be on the move.
Sweat being involved in trade discussions is nothing new. The beginning of the offseason saw Arizona's top pass rusher involved in chatter after the Cardinals fired head coach Jonathan Gannon, who played a big role in landing Sweat last offseason.
What would the Cardinals want for Sweat?
PHNX's Johnny Venerable tweeted out the following:
"The Cardinals are aware of Josh Sweat’s trade market and are believed to be seeking a high Day 2 pick for the veteran pass rusher, per source. Sweat previously requested a trade following the firing of Jonathan Gannon and is signed through 2028."
The Cardinals are aware of Josh Sweat’s trade market and are believed to be seeking a high Day 2 pick for the veteran pass rusher, per source. Sweat previously requested a trade following the firing of Jonathan Gannon and is signed through 2028. pic.twitter.com/LmOdKqKuwe
Sweat is in the second year of a four-year, $76 million contract that does not feature any guaranteed money in 2027 and 2028 — which are the final two years of his deal. He's reportedly looking for a new contract.
The new deal could play a big part in how teams approach Sweat and a potential trade. He's turning 30 next offseason and it appears as degenerative knee issue will be something that needs to be closely managed by Sweat wherever he's at in the coming years.
Sweat's production also hasn't been up to par. The Cardinals saw him tally 12 sacks last season but have rarely seen their star pass rusher get to the quarterback in 2026, bringing down the quarterback just twice.
A high Day 2 pick makes sense for Arizona's asking price, but will that be met?
The good news for the Cardinals is demand for a top pass rusher will only push Sweat's price tag up, especially after DeForest Buckner is now traded and off the market.
It's possible we see Sweat traded for a conditional third-round pick that could turn into a second based off various incentives, whether it be playing time, sacks, whatever the two teams strike a deal on.
There's serious trade buzz around Sweat, and if a desperate team wants to match Arizona's reported asking price, the Cardinals could very well do business.

title: NFL Insider Reveals 3 Top Teams in Cardinals' Josh Sweat Trade Talks
full_text:
ARIZONA — The NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline is rapidly approaching, and the Arizona Cardinals figure to be massive players.
With a 2-5 record and Marvin Harrison Jr. already traded, the Cardinals very much feel open for business within the next few weeks. Whether a deal can be struck remains to be seen, though Arizona clearly has some available talent if the price is right.
No name is bigger — or generating more buzz — than edge rusher Josh Sweat , who has been no stranger to dominating trade headlines entering 2026.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, the Dallas Cowboys , Chicago Bears and San Francisco 49ers are teams to watch for Sweat.
Josh Sweat is being linked to the Cowboys, Bears, 49ers ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline, per @JFowlerESPN . Should the Arizona Cardinals trade their most productive pass rusher? pic.twitter.com/UFqpqcnMZK
Sweat is in the second of a four-year, $76 million contract that doesn't have any guaranteed money in the final two seasons of his deal. He's reportedly looking for a new contract that will fix that.
After signing with the Cardinals in 2025, Sweat tallied 12 sacks and nearly was a Pro Bowl player before being snubbed. Arizona fired head coach Jonathan Gannon after the year, which reportedly prompted a trade request from Sweat.
The Cardinals ultimately held on to Sweat (despite intensified trade buzz heating up around training camp), though with Arizona now trending in the wrong direction, general manager Monti Ossenfort may find it the appropriate time to sell.
Sweat is expected to fetch a Day 2 pick on the trade market, which very well could be met by a team looking to push themselves over the top. Dallas, Chicago and San Francisco all match those molds.
However, the Cowboys are 3-4 on the season and truly need a turnaround to save their playoff chances. The Bears' interest in Sweat and other defenders is acceptable with hopes of balancing their offensive side of the ball while the 49ers would have to massively overpay for a trade to happen within the division.
Arizona already snagged a round two pick for Harrison — is a similar fate in store for Sweat?
Sweat's about to enter his 30s and has just two sacks on the season while he's clearly got some knee injury management that will slow him down. Sweat, after not practicing in any form this offseason, has only shown flashes of the typical damage he can do.
If that magically is fixed after being traded remains to be seen, though Sweat's one of the hottest names in the market right now.

title: Cardinals Big Losers in NFL Week 8 Power Rankings
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals dropped to 2-5 after their Week 7 loss to the Denver Broncos.
Ahead of Week 8, the Cardinals (expectedly) tumbled down various NFL power rankings:
Josh Weinfuss on Kendrick Bourne being the best offseason addition: "The veteran wide receiver, who signed a two-year deal this offseason, has been a reliable third or fourth option for quarterback Jacoby Brissett. That has been especially true after Marvin Harrison Jr. was traded away three weeks ago, as tight end Trey McBride and wide receiver Michael Wilson have gotten a significant amount of attention from defenses. Bourne has 234 yards on 25 catches in seven games. He's on pace for a career high in catches and the third-most receiving yards of his career."
Conor Orr : "Man, the Broncos defense will put you in a terrible headspace."
Pete Prisco : "The high of beating the Rams last week went by the wayside as they were blown out by Denver at home Sunday. They just lack the talent to compete week in and week out."
Nick Shook : "Arizona’s performance in Sunday’s loss to Denver was too predictable. The Cardinals once again became a chuck-and-pray offense on third down, gave up an inexcusable, 62-yard scramble touchdown to Bo Nix, and produced a calamity of errors in the clubhouse leader for worst goal-to-go possession of the year. I feel for Jacoby Brissett, who was brutalized by Denver’s defense. It’s tough to be a Cardinals fan right now."
Mike Florio : "It’s Carson Beck time."
Gary Davenport : "Beck probably isn't the long-term answer at quarterback, but he was a three-year starter at Georgia and then Miami. The Redbirds thought enough of him to spend a Day 2 pick on him.
"And if they're going to get him some game reps, now is the time. After the Cowboys' non-existent defense in Week 8, the Cardinals face Seattle, the Rams and Kansas City.
"This will be a 3-8 team (at best) by the end of November."
Chad Graff on their pass rush being spooky: "The Cardinals have the league’s third-worst passing defense in part because they struggle to generate pressure. The group ranks 27th in pressure rate and 26th in quarterback hits."

title: Cardinals Sign Familiar Face to Address WR Room Injuries
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are bringing back a familiar face.
After losing Jalen Brooks to injured reserve, the Cardinals are signing veteran receiver Zay Jones – who previously played for Arizona for two seasons (2024-25) before not being re-signed this past offseason.
After Brooks was officially placed on IR today following wrist surgery, Jones (who spent time with the Houston Texans in training camp before being cut) was signed to help a depleted receivers room that also lost Marvin Harrison Jr . due to a trade weeks ago.
In related moves today, Arizona officially re-signed offensive lineman Austin Deculus and safety Wydett Williams Jr. to the practice squad and has released safety Jerrick Reed II from the practice squad.
Jones has nine years of NFL experience with over 300 receptions and 3,000 receiving yards. His familiarity with Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort most certainly played a role in helping him get back to the desert.
While current head coach Mike LaFleur doesn't have prior working experience with Jones, former Arizona head coach Jonathan Gannon always sang Jones' praises when asked in press conferences.
“He does his job. He's in the right spot. He can play three spots. He's fast and he's explosive. (He’s a) really good, contested catch guy," Gannon said of Jones last season.
With Jones arriving to a new Cardinals offense under LaFleur, there is some continuity already established with personnel. Jones played with Michael Wilson and Trey McBride previously. Behind Jones, presuming he's eventually worked into Arizona's X receiver role, is fifth-round rookie Reggie Virgil and Simi Fehoko.
LaFleur, asked about replacing Brooks, told reporters it would be done by a committee approach.
“Next man up. I mean, the show goes on, right?" LaFleur said.
"(WR) Reggie’s (Virgil) got a few reps there versus L.A. Didn’t get as many yesterday, but a good week of practice by him. You can do it by committee. (WR) Kendrick (Bourne) can play some X too if we need that. Obviously, (WR) Simi (Fehoko) has done kind of both, but it’ll be by committee.”
The Cardinals, currently 2-5, are dead last in explosive play rates and yards after reception after seven weeks of football. While Jones' presence probably doesn't change those numbers, he does add another veteran presence to a young and overall inexperienced Cardinals' wide receiver room.
Arizona will play the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Jones could potentially be caught up to speed enough to be active for Sunday.

title: 7 Alarming Stats the Cardinals Must Fix Immediately
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are 2-5 through just seven weeks of football, and while stats don't always tell the story, it does sprinkle in some context into how a team is performing.
Take for example their latest red zone struggles , which has stalled their offense and overall ability to win games to begin the regular season. Seven weeks is more than enough to gather data and establish a foundation of what a football team is.
While there's a few good things the Cardinals are doing at this point in time, there's several categories where Arizona ranks near the bottom of the league — if not completely alone at No. 32.
Seven alarming stats the Cardinals have to fix, fast:
What it means : The average time quarterbacks spend in the pocket before throwing or moving out.
Why it matters : Jacoby Brissett is getting the ball out at incredibly fast rates, which does keep turnovers and sacks down to a minimum. However, this usually means teams aren't able hit big plays down the field and are often only hitting the first read... which is exactly what Arizona's offense has evolved into with Brissett under center.
What it means : The percentage in which the defensive line is pressuring a quarterback on dropbacks.
Why it matters : The Cardinals have seemingly only been able to manufacture sacks and pressure from exotic looks or blitzes from defensive coordinator Nick Rallis. Great defenses can rush four and drop seven, and Arizona has tried that with little success for far too long. This number only suffers the more time Walter Nolen III misses due to injury.
What it means : The average amount of yards a pass catcher gains after a reception.
Why it matters : If the Cardinals can't hit deep plays down the field, they have to rely on receivers making defenders miss after the catch — which hasn't happened. While Arizona has strong options in Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, neither are exactly known for making defenders miss in the open field. The Cardinals need a spark in their WR room.
What it means : The percentage of explosive plays an offense has. Ten yards for a rush and 20 yards through the air qualifies.
Why it matters : The Cardinals have been forced to dink-and-dunk their way during drives, failing to hit a big play more than any other team in the league. Arizona can't take the top off the defense, make defenders miss after the catch, or block well enough to spring big plays. This falls on a mix of execution and scheme from head coach Mike LaFleur.
What it means : The percentage of drives a defense allows the offense to score on.
Why it matters : The Cardinals' defense is allowing some sort of score on nearly half of their drives, operating in true feast or famine territory. Arizona's defense has unfortunately met low expectations this season by allowing the most amount of points through seven weeks at 208, which is 29.7 points per game. It's basically a coin flip to see if an offense will score against Rallis' unit, and that's not good.
What it means : The percentage of plays where the defense pressures a quarterback on a passing attempt.
Why it matters : Arizona simply isn't getting to the quarterback. Whether it be their defensive line as highlighted above, outside linebackers or whoever else, opposing offenses aren't being pressured nearly close enough  by Arizona's defense to make an impact. Rallis is solid at generating blitzes to manufacture pressure, he just isn't aggressive enough.
What it means : How often a rushing attempt is stopped at or behind the line of scrimmage.
Why it matters: The Cardinals can't run the ball. For what reason remains to be seen, though missing starters along the offensive line doesn't help while LaFleur hasn't found the recipe for success in terms of scheme. Bam Knight's found some success while Tyler Allgeier has been disappointing. Would love to see what Jeremiyah Love can do when he's fully healthy.

title: Cardinals Can No Longer Ignore Their Biggest Problem
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals tried their very best to downplay a problem that now is rearing its ugly head.
The Cardinals enter Week 8 ranked last in red zone efficiency, scoring touchdowns on just 42.86% of opportunities. Arizona has managed to string together long drives, though the difference between three points and seven in the NFL very much can be the difference between wins and losses in a league where over 60% of games come down to one possession.
After going 0-5 in the red zone in their Week 6 loss to the Detroit Lions, LaFleur said the Cardinals wouldn't overreact to one bad week — insisting Arizona had been fine in the red zone previously and the team just needed better coaching and execution.
Week 7 brought another tough week inside the 20s, as the Cardinals went 1-5 in the red zone against the Denver Broncos . Their overall 1-10 outing through the last two games has now tanked Arizona's stats to the bottom of the league, and the Cardinals — whether they want to admit it or not — officially have a problem.
“No, I don’t think it’s a total blowup because up until two weeks ago we were top 10 in goal-to-goal situations. I think we were 13th overall anytime inside the 20, now we’re dead last for obvious reasons," LaFleur told reporters ahead of Week 8.
Data shows the Cardinals were 16th in red zone efficiency at a 61% clip in Weeks 1-5. In the season's totality, Arizona's goal-to-go touchdown percentage (56%) and inside the ten-yard line touchdown percentage (53%) both are ranked second-to-last among NFL teams.
Alarm bells were officially sounded when the Cardinals were at Denver's one-yard line in Week 7, down by 14 with just under two minutes left. Arizona, admittedly altering their approach in hopes to save some clock, struck out on all four attempts to get in the end zone.
"Once we kind of got going a little bit and we were moving it, we weren’t finishing it. Against good teams  — we lucked out the week before because our defense played incredible. We hit six kicks, but you can’t do that every week (and) we know that," LaFleur continued on the red zone struggles.
"It’s like ‘Guys, we’re down there.’ It’s not like we’re not moving the football, but we have to finish. Again, I’ll look in the mirror first and say it starts with me.”
Play-calling changes when you get in the red zone. The field shrinks, and numerous plays/concepts you could normally run are thrown out the window. This places a greater emphasis on not only choosing the right plays, but also execution — which hasn't exactly been a calling card for Arizona's offense to begin the season.
"It’s always going to start with me and the play design. One, the play design and the clarity you’re providing to the guys. Then two, when you’re calling it. It’s always going to start with me," LaFleur said last week. "Then after that, the guys have to go execute it. Sometimes you call the right one and it’s not executed. Sometimes you call the wrong one and guys make a play, but that’ll always start with me.”
It's not as if the Cardinals' offense has been stagnant. They lead the NFL in ten-play drives and are top five in time of possession. They can clearly move the ball.
Yet when it counts, for whatever reason, the Cardinals can't convert field goals into touchdowns. Arizona's strong defensive performance against the Rams was an obvious outlier, one LaFleur and the offensive staff clearly can't rely on.
The Cardinals do know they have a massive problem on their hands, a complex dynamic that doesn't have an easy solution.

title: Cardinals Give Carson Beck Injury Update
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are potentially getting Carson Beck back on the practice field this week.
Beck suffered a back injury that ultimately landed him on last week's injury report. The rookie third-round pick rebounded from a preseason ribs injury that only saw him play one game, and with Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew ahead of him, Beck hasn't played in 2026.
While Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur refused to put a label on Beck's role moving into Week 8, he did say Beck was set to complete a workout today to guage where the Miami product is at.
“Not going to talk about role changes right now, but I’ll know more tomorrow. He’s going to do a workout tomorrow on our off day just to move in the pocket and stuff like that to see where he is in terms of — I guess you could say, ‘rep structure’ starting Wednesday, Thursday (and) Friday," LaFleur said during his Monday press conference.
How did the back injury even happen?
“It just kind of flared up on him honestly. He just had a little bit of a back spasm. Again, when you’re torquing the way these guys torque, that’s not fun. I don’t know if anyone’s ever had back spasms here, but they suck," LaFleur added.
Beck is still awaiting his turn at the wheel of LaFleur's offense, which figures to come down the road as losses continue to pile in Arizona.
When exactly Beck will enter the lineup remains to be seen. The Cardinals won't hand over the keys next week in Dallas after already committing to Brissett despite the team's 2-5 start.
However, we will need to see Beck at some point ahead of a massive 2027 offseason, where the Cardinals just might find themselves in position to take a top-rated quarterback in the draft.
If Beck can convince the Cardinals he's a possible solution at quarterback, Arizona would bypass those opportunities.
Many believe Week 12 is an optimal landing spot for Beck to play, as that would give him multiple games before a bye week and a short stint of easier games to finish the 2026 regular season.
For now, it appears he'll continue to be the team's emergency quarterback on game days. But before any moves can be made, Beck has to be healthy — and it appears we're in line to see him back on the practice field soon.

title: Where Atlanta Falcons Stand in NFC South Ahead of Division Clash with Buccaneers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have an opportunity to change the NFC South race over their next four games, beginning this Sunday with an important divisional matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Atlanta improved to 3-4 after defeating the San Francisco 49ers in Week 7. The victory provided a much-needed confidence boost, but the Falcons cannot afford to let that momentum disappear as they prepare for a challenging stretch.
With the Carolina Panthers currently leading the division at 3-3, the Falcons have ground to make up. Tampa Bay and the New Orleans Saints are both 2-5, leaving the division race open as the season progresses.
Atlanta’s next game comes against Tampa Bay on Nov. 1 at Raymond James Stadium. The Buccaneers are coming off a dominant 43-13 victory over Carolina, making this an important opportunity for the Falcons to gain ground in the division.
A victory would move Atlanta to .500 while giving Tampa Bay another divisional loss. It would also help the Falcons improve their divisional record.
The Buccaneers have already demonstrated their ability to compete within this division, and Atlanta will need another strong performance on both sides of the ball to leave Tampa with a victory.
Following that matchup, the Falcons travel to Madrid, Spain, to face the Cincinnati Bengals on Nov. 8 before hosting the Chiefs on Nov. 15. Atlanta then has its bye week before traveling to Minnesota to face the Vikings on Nov. 29.
Those three non-divisional games will be important for Atlanta’s overall record and playoff positioning. However, the Falcons must balance those challenges with the importance of their remaining NFC South matchups.
Carolina remains atop the standings despite its blowout loss to Tampa Bay. At 3- 3, the Panthers have the division lead, but their advantage over Atlanta is small enough that the race could change quickly. Carolina faces the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night. The Packers have won three of four since being blown out by the Falcons.
Tampa Bay’s victory over Carolina was significant because it improved the Buccaneers’ division record.
New Orleans, meanwhile, sits at 2-5 and has ground to make up. The Saints remain a factor in the division race, particularly with another matchup against Atlanta scheduled for Week 17. New Orleans is on a bye this week.
The Falcons will also host Tampa Bay in Week 16 before closing the regular season on the road against Carolina in Week 18. Those games could prove decisive if the division remains competitive.
The next four games will help determine whether Atlanta can turn its victory over San Francisco into a sustained push toward the playoffs.
With Carolina leading and Tampa Bay gaining momentum, Atlanta cannot afford to overlook the importance of its divisional games. Winning those matchups could ultimately determine whether the Falcons challenge for the NFC South crown or spend the final weeks trying to catch up.

title: NFL Stands Up, Takes Notice of Michael Penix Jr.'s Ascendancy
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are coming off one of their biggest victories of the season , and quarterback Michael Penix Jr. is receiving recognition for his performance against the San Francisco 49ers.
Penix was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week on Wednesday after leading the Falcons to a victory over the 49ers in Week 7. The honor marks the first time in his NFL career that Penix has received a Player of the Week award since entering the league in 2024.
The third-year quarterback delivered one of his most efficient performances of the season, completing 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns without throwing an interception. His 73.5 percent completion rate and 118.9 passer rating highlighted an impressive outing against one of the conference's top teams.
Penix's passer rating was his second-highest of the season. He also extended an encouraging stretch for Atlanta's young quarterback, throwing three touchdown passes for the second consecutive game. He recorded three touchdowns in the Falcons' Week 6 loss to the Chicago Bears before matching that total against San Francisco.
Penix was the only quarterback in the conference in Week 7 to record at least three touchdown passes without an interception while completing at least 70 percent of his attempts.
Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski praised Penix's ability to make smart decisions against a talented San Francisco defense.
“I thought Mike was really good throughout the day. You know, that's a very, very good defense. I mean they're excellent and they don't give up big plays. And we took our shots when we had them, and when we didn't, I thought Mike saw it really well,” Stefanski said after the victory.
His decision making helped Atlanta overcome an early deficit and secure a much needed victory.
After falling behind 14-3, the Falcons rallied and scored 26 unanswered points during a stretch that carried them into the fourth quarter. Atlanta's protection also played a significant role, allowing Penix to operate without being sacked against the 49ers.
The victory snapped Atlanta's two-game losing streak and provided a boost heading into a crucial divisional matchup.
The Falcons will travel to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8, with the opportunity to build momentum and strengthen their position in the NFC South standings.
For Penix, earning his first career Player of the Week award represents a significant milestone. His recent production gives Atlanta reason for optimism as the quarterback looks to carry his improved play into another important game.

title: Falcons Could Trade for Key Weapon in Colts Fire Sale
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are open for business, but could the Atlanta Falcons want in?
After Colts ownership fired Chris Ballard last week, the franchise has started selling off roster assets in quick succession. In a matter of hours, interim general manager Ed Dodds shipped All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks for a pair of picks (a 2027 third-rounder and a 2028 fifth-rounder) and All-Pro interior defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the 49ers for a 2027 fourth-rounder.
With Indianapolis tearing down its roster, teams across the league are looking to pluck a piece from a teardown franchise.
The Falcons could add wide receiver depth at the deadline, and Josh Downs immediately comes to mind.
At 25, the Georgia native is entering the final year of his rookie contract and has developed into a solid route runner. The Falcons would need to send a mid-round pick in 2027 for Downs.
Lining up mostly in the slot, Downs could replace Olamide Zaccheaus in the rotation, since the free-agent addition hasn't made a significant impact so far (four catches for 17 yards). The addition could make sense, but his presence would also impede rookie Zachariah Branch. Atlanta would also be competing with other wide receiver-needy teams (e.g., the Chiefs, 49ers, etc.), and the Colts would look to maximize their return.
If the Falcons looked deeper on the Colts’ roster, they could also target wideout Keenan Allen. He is no longer the elite threat he was, but the 14-year veteran would still be a red-zone threat for Michael Penix Jr. and a valuable locker-room addition for a young rotation.
Ian Cunningham has already shown a willingness to make trades, and the first-year general manager has already made four.
Over the offseason, he acquired Wanya Morris from the Chiefs, Sydney Brown from the Eagles, Gervon Dexter from the Bears , and Maason Smith from the Jaguars . These were aggressive deals by the Falcons, and three have worked out beautifully. Cunningham was intentional with these deals, some player-for-player and others straight draft capital, but each addressed a specific need the roster didn’t already have.
For now, the Falcons aren't in a position to be hyper-aggressive.
At 3-4, they are around the middle of the NFC and aren't expected to be contenders this season. They are also well-positioned to spend big in free agency in 2027 ($141.4 million in cap space, the most in the NFL) and, if they choose, could compete for these assets on the open market instead of giving up draft capital.
Downs would also be in the market for a lucrative extension. With the Falcons already paying three skill players big money, they are unlikely to pony up what it would take to retain him.
The Colts' sell-off could create opportunities, but Cunningham should only make a move if the price and long-term fit make sense. He's shown a willingness to be aggressive, but patience may be the better play.

title: Falcons Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Could Join NFL Royalty
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski is earning national recognition for his work in Atlanta, with ESPN analyst Ben Solak making the case that the two-time Coach of the Year winner deserves another award.
In his Week 8 column, Solak praised Stefanski’s impact on quarterback Michael Penix Jr., the Falcons’ rushing attack and a defense that has helped Atlanta remain competitive in the NFC South.
"I think ... Kevin Stefanski should win Coach of the Year," Solak wrote on ESPN . "Three coaches in NFL history have won the AP Coach of the Year award at least three times: Don Shula (3.5, as he shared a win in 1967), Bill Belichick (three), and Chuck Knox (three). I think Stefanski should become the fourth this season."
The endorsement follows Atlanta’s 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers in Week 7. The Falcons improved to 3-4 after overcoming an early 14-3 deficit, scoring 23 unanswered points to secure an important win.
For Solak, however, Stefanski’s candidacy goes beyond one impressive performance. He believes the coach has helped establish an offensive identity that maximizes Atlanta’s personnel.
One of Solak’s biggest reasons for supporting Stefanski is Michael Penix Jr.’s development . The quarterback has increasingly embraced a quicker passing approach rather than consistently relying on deep throws.
“That the Falcons have readily gotten Penix to think about football in a different fashion altogether is impressive,” Solak wrote.
Atlanta has incorporated more quick passes and designed rollouts to help Penix operate efficiently. Solak says that Penix leads the NFL in designed rollout rate, highlighting the coaching staff’s willingness to tailor the offense to its quarterback.
The Falcons have also established a productive ground game behind Bijan Robinson.
“His running game is getting the best out of Robinson that we’ve ever seen,” Solak wrote.
That rushing production gives Atlanta another way to control games and takes pressure off Penix as he continues developing.
Solak also praised Stefanski for retaining defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich, whose unit has contributed to Atlanta’s recent success. Against San Francisco, the Falcons forced four turnovers and limited one of the NFC’s strongest teams to 20 points.
Stefanski previously won Coach of the Year honors in 2020 and 2023 with Cleveland. A third award would place him among a select group of coaches to accomplish that feat.
Solak believes Atlanta’s position in the NFC South gives Stefanski a realistic opportunity to strengthen his candidacy. He pointed to a potential 10-7 finish and a home playoff game as a compelling case for another award.
The Falcons still have work to do at 3-4, but their victory over San Francisco provided encouraging evidence of their potential.
If Stefanski can maintain the offensive progress and guide Atlanta into the playoffs, Solak’s thought could become a reality.

title: Maason Smith Making Falcons Trade with Jaguars Look Even Better
full_text:
Maason Smith delivered one of his most productive performances of the season as the Atlanta Falcons defeated the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
Smith finished with two tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, one quarterback hit, and a forced fumble. His performance helped Atlanta generate pressure and create turnovers against a San Francisco offense that entered the matchup without a loss.
For Smith, the production was reminiscent of the work he has put in throughout the season and the defense’s commitment to executing its game plan. The Falcons acquired Smith in an offseason trade that sent 2024 second-round pick Ruke Orhorhoro to the Jacksonville Jaguars. It was a rare player-for-player swap, and it was even rarer that it was from the same position, from the same round, from the same draft.
“Just seeing everything fall into place, man. It felt good,” Smith said.
The Falcons emphasized winning the turnover battle entering Sunday’s matchup, knowing San Francisco’s defense also excelled at forcing takeaways. Atlanta’s defense answered that challenge.
“That was kind of one of the biggest keys to victory for us going into the game, man, just wanting to win the turnover margin,” Smith said. “We knew on the other side that they do a very good job about getting the ball out.”
Smith credited the defense for staying disciplined and attacking when opportunities were available.
“I think we did a great job of attacking the ball, man, and sticking to the plan that we needed to do to get the victory,” he said.
The performance was an encouraging step forward for Smith, who entered the game with four tackles through Atlanta’s first six games. His production against San Francisco brought his season totals to nine tackles, one sack, two tackles for loss, one quarterback hit and one forced fumble.
More importantly, the outing gives Smith something to build on as the Falcons look to establish consistency along the defensive line. His ability to generate pressure and contribute to takeaways could become increasingly valuable as Atlanta works to climb the standings.
Smith understands that Sunday’s victory must serve as a starting point rather than a finish line. The Falcons have experienced difficult stretches this season, but Atlanta will look to maintain that defensive intensity against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 8.
“Just use it as momentum, man, going into next week, getting back to the win column, and just continue to grow from there,” Smith said.
If Smith can build on his performance against the 49ers, the Falcons could have another underrated talent on their defensive front as they look to turn Sunday’s statement victory into sustained success.

title: Did Falcons Find their Franchise QB in Michael Penix Jr.? SI's Albert Breer Weighs In
full_text:
It's a popular refrain that the Atlanta Falcons have been in quarterback purgatory since trading Matt Ryan prior to the 2022 season. That's only partially true. Sure, Ryan was the unquestioned starter during his time in Atlanta, but he hadn't had a passer rating above 15th in the NFL since 2018.
The Falcons haven't either.
It's no coincidence that as the Falcons have been poor at the position for the better part of the last decade, the team hasn't had a winning season, and those losing seasons predate the Ryan trade.
The quarterback conundrum was still the biggest question entering the Falcons season under first-year head coach Kevin Stefanski. Between Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa, it was actually a two-part question. Did they have a quarterback who was good enough to be a franchise guy, and could he stay healthy long enough to become that guy?
After seven weeks, the first part of that question looks to have been answered. Penix is having a breakout season under Stefanski and offensive coordinator Tommy Rees. While the second part of the question will take time to answer, Sports Illustrated's Albert Breer thinks the door is open for Penix to lock down the long-term job.
"I’m not sure if Michael Penix Jr. is going to be the Falcons’ starter for (the) next five or 10 years, but that door is certainly opening," Breer wrote on SI . "And Sunday in Atlanta was a really good step in that direction. On the other side was a veteran 49ers defense that had held four of its six opponents to 17 points or fewer through a 6–0 start. A defense that, on this Sunday, was good enough to hold Bijan Robinson to 63 rushing yards on 20 carries."
Breer took note of Penix's numbers this season and was impressed. His passer rating is No. 4 in the NFL among quarterbacks with at least five starts. What he left out, though, is that four out of Penix's five starts have come against teams with a winning record: Packers (4-3), Ravens (4-3), Bears (5-2), and 49ers (6-1).
"That gives Penix a 3–2 record as a starter, following Atlanta’s 0–2 start without him, and this stat line through five games: 96-of-144 (66.7%), 1,157 yards, 9 TDs, 1 INT, 109.1 rating. Which is more remarkable when you consider he’s just two months and two days past his first 11-on-11 practice in Kevin Stefanski’s system, and coming off his third ACL surgery," Breer continued.
It's a far cry from how the season started. Cooper Rush was forced into action after being plucked off his couch at the start of training camp, and the Falcons predictably went 0-2. Tagovailoa couldn't make it to Week 1 without a series of soft-tissue injuries, and Penix was still recovering from surgery.
"At that point, Atlanta looked nowhere at the position. That’s not the case anymore," Breer concluded.
Penix has proven that he's good enough to keep the Falcons from selecting a possible replacement in the first round of next year's draft. Now it's up to him to put the injury concerns behind him and continue playing at a high level.

title: Falcons Big Winners in Week 8 NFL Power Rankings after Upsetting 49ers
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have already been on a roller coaster season. They began the season 0-2 and look like they're going to be in the running for the No. 1 overall pick in April's NFL Draft. Michael Penix Jr. comes back, and they look like a legitimate playoff threat.
They stumbled against the Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore Ravens team that was beatable, before getting their doors blown off by the Chicago Bears.
So naturally, they beat the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
I think we can wipe the first two games off the board while the team was playing Cooper Rush after signing him as an emergency quarterback the day training camp opened. If we do that, we see a 3-2 team that has shown signs of being really good with a competent quarterback under center.
So, it's no surprise the national media has been slow to get behind this Falcons team after a big win. This isn't a team that has handled the spotlight very well in the past.
But there are signs this year could be different with talent up and down the offense, and an overachieving defense that will be getting some key players back soon, including edge rusher James Pearce Jr. in two weeks.
NFL Network's Nick Shook is driving the Falcons' bandwagon. He's been a fan of this team from the beginning of the season and has moved Atlanta up from No. 19 to No. 13. He's just as apprehensive as any Falcons fan about the lofty ranking.
"Look, I’m with you: I don’t know who the Falcons are, either," Shook wrote . "They were an inspired bunch on Sunday, outplaying a strong 49ers. Michael Penix Jr. looks very comfortable in Kevin Stefanski’s offense, and Jeff Ulbrich’s defense played with a higher level of aggression. A win like this makes me believe in this team. Hopefully, it doesn't deliver the opposite this Sunday in Tampa."
The Buccaneers are coming off a strange blowout win against the Carolina Panthers. The score was 43-13, and Tampa has 64 passing yards.
SI gave the Falcons the biggest jump in the rankings this week, going from No. 23 to No. 16, first in the NFC South.
"Tommy Rees called one heck of a game against the 49ers, taking Michael Penix’s struggles against secondary blitzes and turning the offense into something that offered plenty of comfort blanket throws while also rolling him out of trouble," Connor Orr wrote on SI .
Pete Prisco may have felt burned earlier in the season after elevating the Falcons after a big win over Green Bay. He had the Falcons at No. 23 coming into the week and moved them to No. 19 after their win over San Francisco.
"Rallying to beat the 49ers is big for this team after losing two straight. The defense made the plays when they needed to be made," Prisco wrote on CBS Sports .
ESPN is the only outlet that doesn't provide any corresponding context for their power rankings. They gave the Falcons the smallest rise, going from No. 22 to No. 19, and they left the 49ers in the No. 1 spot.
The Falcons have seen these ups and downs before over the course of the last few seasons. The arrow is pointing in the right direction now, but in order to make believers out of more people, and more importantly, advance their playoff agenda, they'll need to beat a 2-5 Buccaneers team in Tampa on Sunday.

title: Kendal Daniels Wasn't Only Falcons Rookie with a Dramatic Return vs. 49ers
full_text:
After fumbling twice on special teams against the Chicago Bears, Atlanta Falcons rookie Zachariah Branch received encouragement from his teammates, including running back Bijan Robinson, who prayed with the rookie and helped him regain his confidence heading into the following week.
While linebacker Kendal Daniels got most of the attention for his big game , he wasn't the only rookie who bounced back in a big way on Sunday.
Branch responded exactly how the Falcons hoped, delivering a huge spark that gave Atlanta a much-needed spark in its 29- 20 victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday.
Rather than allowing his mistakes against Chicago to define him, Branch returned with renewed confidence and made an immediate impact. His explosive return on Atlanta’s opening possession after San Francisco scored its first touchdown gave the Falcons possession at the 49ers’ 36-yard line. The field position helped set up a 39-yard field goal by Nick Folk, providing an important response.
“Obviously, that big return got us going,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said.
The return was a significant moment for Branch, who remained in the team’s plans despite his costly mistakes the previous week. Atlanta’s coaching staff continued to express confidence in the rookie, allowing him an opportunity to learn from the experience rather than lose his role.
Bijan Robinson praised Branch’s response and talked about his importance.
“That’s how you become the player you want to become if you just keep that faith throughout the week, you keep working hard throughout the week, and then the results will be there when you do everything right,” Robinson said.
That message carried particular weight after Robinson supported Branch during the difficult aftermath of the Bears game. The veteran running back’s encouragement, along with the confidence shown by the coaching staff and teammates, helped reinforce that one bad performance would not determine the rookie’s future in Atlanta.
Branch rewarded that belief against San Francisco. His 61-yard kickoff return helped establish favorable field position, while Atlanta’s kickoff return unit finished with 126 total return yards.
Branch also contributed offensively, recording one reception for nine yards and an eight-yard rushing attempt. Although his offensive numbers remained modest, his impact on special teams demonstrated the explosiveness that initially made him an intriguing addition to Atlanta’s roster.
Special teams coordinator Craig Aukerman and the Falcons’ coaching staff have repeatedly expressed confidence in Branch’s ability to make plays. His speed and versatility give Atlanta a potential difference-maker in the return game, provided he continues protecting the football and making sound decisions.
The Falcons will need that progress to continue. Sunday’s performance was an important step for Branch, who turned a difficult week into an opportunity to help Atlanta secure a statement victory against an undefeated opponent.

title: How Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. Is Beginning to Find His Footing as an NFL Starter
full_text:
When the Atlanta Falcons desperately needed a win, Michael Penix Jr. delivered arguably his best performance as an NFL quarterback.
Trailing the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers 14-3 at the beginning of the second quarter, Penix helped Atlanta spark 23 unanswered points en route to completing a 29-20 comeback in Week 7 on Sunday, Oct. 25.
“Poise, calmness,” said Falcons wide receiver Drake London . “He’s the calmest one out there. He just deals. That’s just MP.”
Penix finished completing 25-of-34 passes for 213 yards and three touchdowns. It was his second consecutive three-touchdown performance, following last week’s 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears.
“Mike was really good throughout the day,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said. “That’s a very good defense; they’re excellent. And they don’t give up big plays. We took our shots when we had them, and when we didn’t, I think Mike saw it really well.”
A large portion of Penix’s successful afternoon was Atlanta’s offensive line play, which was nearly flawless in protection.
And that was against a 49ers defense that entered the game No. 4 in NFL total defense and in the top half of the pass rushing, led by defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, a former head coach of Atlanta.
According to ESPN’s Nick Wagoner, Penix was only pressured three times out of 34 dropbacks.
“It was unbelievable,” Penix said. “To see those guys, the work that they put in every day throughout the week, for them to come out this game, and I don’t get pressured much at all – it’s awesome to be able to see. Those guys work extremely hard, so credit to what they’ve been doing.”
“I don’t remember being hit too many times at all,” Penix added.
After an incompletion on his very first pass, clean pockets helped Penix complete 11 straight completions. Checkdowns, opportunistic shots downfield, and taking care of the football.
“Just making sure we didn’t make any mistakes and go out there and play our brand of football,” Penix said. “We’ve got guys around with the skillset to get open. So for me, I just got to find a way to get them the ball whenever that opportunity is there.”
After basically redshirting his rookie year and then partially tearing his ACL last year, Penix has posted a stat line of 1,157 passing yards, nine touchdowns, and a lone interception. His 109.1 passer rating is fourth in the NFL among quarterbacks with at least five starts this season.
“It’s been great,” Falcons running back Bijan Robinson said when asked about Penix’s development. “I think he’s been growing a lot as a player and doing a lot of great stuff for the offense. He wants to continue to get better. But his process has been really good. And I’m excited to keep playing with him every game coming up.”
Penix now has a full season’s worth of NFL starts at 17. He’s 7-10 as a starter, but more importantly, he's 3-2 this season.
And he’s starting to take command of what this Falcons offense is and what it could potentially be.
“We trust Mike,” Stefanski said. “I know he’s a young player in terms of starts in this league. I get that part. But we trust him.”
The Falcons next travel near Penix’s hometown of Dade City to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in an NFC South clash this Sunday at 1 p.m.
Gerald Thomas, III, is a national award-winning reporter contributing to Atlanta Falcons On SI. He has several years of writing and editorial experience, including covering college athletics under the USA TODAY umbrella.

title: Falcons Star Jessie Bates Proves He's the Heartbeat of Atlanta's Defense
full_text:
ATLANTA – The Atlanta Falcons stunned the undefeated San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. They forced four turnovers and locked down in the second half to win 29-20.
There was plenty to love in the win, but a familiar face led the way.
Falcons safety Jessie Bates III has been a menace to opposing teams since arriving in Atlanta, and he was again on Sunday. He snagged an acrobatic interception that likely kept points off the board for the 49ers, then delivered the game-sealing play in the fourth quarter, punching the ball away from tight end George Kittle to force another turnover.
This interception by Jessie Bates III is UNREAL. SFvsATL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/R4UDkkfGcb
“That interception is as good as it gets,” head coach Kevin Stefanski said. “We needed a play in that moment. The ball skills and the wherewithal and the awareness, the toe-drag swag, that's pretty damn good for a safety. So, really proud of Jessie for just being so aware of that football and making a play and then knocking it out later. I mean, he's playing at a high level.”
Bates’ ability to create turnovers isn't new, but his performance against San Francisco reminded everyone how valuable he can be to Atlanta's defense.
According to Tori McElhaney, only four players have recorded at least six career games with both an interception and a forced fumble. Five of Bates' six such performances have come in a Falcons uniform.
For his teammates, it was little surprise to watch him deliver.
“That’s who he is as a player,” quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said. “Obviously, as a person, he’s great as well. But what we saw out of Jessie (on Sunday) is who he is. That’s who we see every day: just a guy with a nose for the football who makes big-time plays whenever we need them. So it was awesome to be able to see him do that.”
Since 2023, Bates has 14 interceptions, including three returned for touchdowns, and 10 forced fumbles. No player has more combined takeaways in that timeframe.
The production has made Bates one of the NFL's most disruptive defensive backs, but his value to Atlanta extends beyond the raw numbers. He has served as a team captain every year as a Falcon and has been one of the defense's most dependable leaders.
That leadership mattered almost as much as his takeaways on Sunday, with Kendal Daniels wearing the green dot as the defensive signal-caller. The rookie linebacker was an incredible story, but he credited Bates as the calming presence he needed throughout the game.
“Jessie is everybody's role model,” linebacker Josh Woods said. “Just the way he prepares, how smart he is, how he handles himself day in and day out. You know exactly who you're going to get, what you're going to get. If I had to place a heartbeat on our defense, I would say it's Jessie Bates for sure.”
For a team still finding its identity under Stefanski, that influence matters even more, and it extends well beyond his on-field play. His preparation, football intelligence, and consistency have helped establish this standard.
Bates has been doing that since he arrived in Atlanta. Against the 49ers, he reminded everyone why the Falcons' defense keeps running through him.

Garrett Chapman is a sports broadcaster, writer, and content creator based in Atlanta. He has several years of experience covering the Atlanta sports scene, college football, Georgia high school football, recruiting for 24/7 Sports, and the NFL. You can also hear him on Sports Radio 92.9 The Game.

title: Ravens Week 7 Rookie Report: Vega Ioane Left Early With Injury
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's 35-13 home loss to the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 7. They are in an AFC North division in which every team's record is above .500, and after falling to 4-3, they now deservedly sit at the bottom of the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. The only rookies who were healthy scratches were fourth-round wide receiver Elijah Sarratt and undrafted quarterback Joe Fagnano, who still suited up as an emergency No. 3 option. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall wasn't activated from short-term injured reserve in his third week of eligibility and seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
The first-round interior offensive lineman's return to his natural position at right guard after playing the last three games at center was short-lived and cut short due to injury. After taking a knee to his right knee while making a block downfield, he left the game following that drive and did not return. It marked the first time all season that he missed a single snap on offense, as he only played 16 of the Ravens' 67 total snaps on that side of the ball. According to a report from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Ioane suffered a sprained MCL, and while it's not a long-term injury, he is expected to miss time. Head coach Jesse Minter alluded to the fact that he'll likely miss this week's massive matchup against the Buffalo Bills following Wednesday's practice.
"We'll see where it's at with (Vega)," Minter said. "If there's anybody that can do something crazy and overcome things, he's got the right mentality. We'll see how that goes, and we'll put the best guy out there that gives us the best opportunity for this particular game."
Despite the Ravens losing sack leader and stout run-defending fourth-year pro Tavius Robinson to a season-ending pectoral injury, the second-rounder didn't see a sharp or even slight uptick in playing time on defense, as many expected . His 21 snaps on that side of the ball were his second-lowest of the season and fewest since he played just a dozen in Week 1. He still helped the Ravens bottle up the Bengals' rushing attack to just 73 yards on the ground with an average of just 3.7 yards per carry. Young recorded his seventh solo tackle of the season on a solo takedown of running back Chase Brown after a four-yard gain to prevent him from moving the chains on a penalty-shortened first down.
The third-rounder picked up where he left off in his return from injury last week by picking up key first-down conversions on the first two of the three receptions that he made on five targets for 25 receiving yards. All three came on third down, with the first being a juggling snag he gained control of before backpedaling out of bounds for a gain of 10 yards on the Ravens' second scoring drive. Two plays later, he came up clutch again with a nine-yard snag on third-and-medium that he had to go low to pluck before it could hit the ground. His third catch came on the final play of the third quarter with the Ravens deep in Bengals territory, and had he not had to work back to the quarterback after getting sufficient depth at the top of his route, Lane likely would've been 3-for-3 on third-down conversions as he dragged down two yards shy of the line to gain.
Since his return from the wrist injury that delayed his impact as a rookie, Ja’Kobi Lane has looked impressive, becoming a popular third-down target. The Ravens struck gold in selecting him in the third round. Any questions over drafting him too early have all but disappeared! pic.twitter.com/BykC9TTRAy
Lane nearly had a mulligan on recording his first career touchdown catch on the Ravens' last possession of the first half on a third-and-short in the low red zone. Unfortunately, backup quarterback Tyler Huntley's pass was just out of reach of the long-limbed wideout, who got nice separation from the corner guarding him on the play.
The fourth-rounder played fewer than 30 offensive snaps for the first time in his last four appearances, but it was also his first game back after missing last week with an injury. Hibner wasn't targeted as a pass catcher and was one of multiple players at the position who struggled as blockers in run blocking, either whiffing or straight-up losing block attempts. With veteran Mark Andrews struggling the Ravens need to get the young tight ends more involved.
The fifth-rounder didn't see any playing time on defense for the second straight game, as the Ravens decided to deploy second-year pro Keyon Martin at the nickel spot over him again. Rivers' 13 snaps on special teams were the second-most among rookies and 52% of the team's total.
The fifth-rounder played his fewest offensive snaps since Week 2 with 15, yet that didn't stop him from having his second-most productive outing in that phase of the game with two catches on three targets for 35 receiving yards. He picked up 16 yards on the first play from the scrimmage of the game off a play-action pass from Huntley that he caught short and rumbled for the rest. His other 19 yards came on a tight end screen that moved the offense past midfield and into Cincinnati territory late in the third quarter.
First drive, double motion with Cuevas, then a chip and release to get him wide open while the defense is busy elsewhere. Good layup for Huntley that became absent one the game script became more established. pic.twitter.com/kLqZsJ4OTn
Cuevas was Huntley's intended target on the final play of that same drive, but he collided with a Bengals defender and was knocked off course just enough for the pass to fall incomplete on a fourth-down gamble by Minter, who bypassed another short field goal that would've given the Ravens the lead back.
The #Ravens failed 4th and 1. #RavensFlock pic.twitter.com/QHHOsYILtp
The sixth-round specialist had a solid yet non-spectacular day at the office with three punts for 145 yards, including an average of 48.3 yards per punt and a long of 57, his third-longest of the season. While Eckley didn't have any touchbacks, he didn't manage to pin the Bengals back inside their own 20-yard line once either.
The undrafted free agent helped fill the void created by Robinson's season-ending injury and did a great job in the effort. Burke tied his career highs with 17 defensive snaps and 22 on special teams, first among rookies and tied for the most on the team overall. He was impressive as an edge-setter against the run with how he stacked and effortlessly shed would-be blockers, and nearly notched his second career sack on Joe Burrow, who somehow managed to throw an incomplete pass before the Maryland native could bring him all the way down with possession. Burke's Pro Football Focus grade of 78.5 was the highest among all defenders on the team and second overall to only two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers, who had another monster game and earned a 90.7.
Ravens UDFA Ethan Burke Welcome back Brent urban pic.twitter.com/Xzmc5DMEZ8
