title: Tre'Davious White Projects When He'll Be Ready to Boost Bills' Subpar Defense
full_text:
Veteran cornerback Tre'Davious White is back in town with the Buffalo Bills for his 10th season as a pro.
The 2017 Bills' first-round draft pick has ditched his couch for one more run in Orchard Park. Buffalo signed White to its practice squad at the start of its Week 7 bye.
"This was a different kind of offseason for me. I've been sitting on the couch, drinking ginger ale and eating popcorn for a while," said the 31-year-old White as a guest on Eric Wood's Centered On Buffalo podcast .
White, a former All-Pro and well-liked locker room presence, provides leadership upon his arrival, but when will the grizzled veteran be able to contribute on field in a game situation for a struggling defense that ranks next to last against the pass?
"For me to be able to go out there and play in a NFL game at the position that I play, at defensive back, uhh, I got so much respect for the position, I'd disrespect the position just thinking I can just come off the couch and come out there and be Tre White," said White.
Naturally, White, who hasn't seen game action since Buffalo's divisional playoff loss last January, needs some sort of ramp-up period, especially considering he did not attend a training camp this past summer.
One has to think White will require at least four weeks of practice to get back up to speed in both the physical and mental aspects of the game.
"It's gonna be a process, which I know. We've been talking about it for a while. It's gonna be a process. I'm going to go into practice and just to go out there and move around a little bit. See where I'm at," said White.
Coming out of the bye, the Bills will hold their first Week 8 practice on Wednesday, October 28. It'll be White's first opportunity to get on the field in coordinator Jim Leonhard's defense.
"The best thing for me, I know these guys. I know a lot of these guys on the team," said White.
White's familiarity with multiple teammates coupled with his experience should speed up his acclimation period to some extent.
"The main thing with me is gonna be getting the reps with the guys, getting comfortable with who I'm around. Learning where my help is in this defense and learning where I can make some plays," said White.
If the plan is to give White at least four weeks of prep, then that means the earliest he would suit up is the Week 12 home game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. Of course, this is sheer speculation, and a lot can change after White returns to the practice field on Wednesday.
White is another year older, but he still had some gas left in his tank as recent as last season.
Initially brought back as cornerback insurance during Spring 2025, White wound up as the full-time starter opposite Christian Benford as first-round rookie Maxwell Hairston spent the first six weeks on Injured Reserve.
White maintained his starting role as the Bills began to ease Hairston into the rotation, and the grizzled veteran was more than serviceable throughout the year. Over 16 regular season starts, he made 40 tackles, 6.0 TFL, one interception and nine pass break-ups. Opposing passers averaged only 5.1 yards per attempts and completed 51.1 percent when targeting White.
While he has thrived playing zone coverage for most of his career, White is a true technician, and student of the game, with plenty of capability in an aggressive man coverage scheme.
"I'm just gonna be playing ball," said White.

title: Week 8 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Bills Move Up During Bye Week
full_text:
Week 7 was a well-timed bye for the Buffalo Bills . They're off to a 5-1 start, but they've been playing in multiple tight games. That's primarily been due to their defensive shortcomings.
Buffalo is currently first in the league in points scored , but their defense is 30th in points surrendered. They have been able to win despite this, but they hopefully found some answers during the bye week.
The Bills also saw their stock rise despite not playing. With the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers both losing, Buffalo is climbing up many NFL power rankings. Let's check out where they stand with our weekly roundup.
Connor Orr moved Buffalo up to No. 1, due to two of the undefeated teams losing. The Bills now have a chance to get fully healthy, but they also have a couple of tough games ahead of them with the Baltimore Ravens and Minnesota Vikings up next.
"Coming off the bye, the directive for Buffalo was simple: improve ball security, weaponize this defense and try to keep Josh Allen packed in a sheet of ice like a fish purchased from Pike’s Market to help him absorb a massive stretch of games in which he will have to be Superman," Orr wrote.
ESPN picked the best offseason addition for each team and for the Bills, it was DJ Moore. Nick Suss said they have survived without him as he's dealing with a shoulder injury, but added that Moore takes the offense to another level when he's on the field. That's encouraging since he has a chance to be back in Week 8 .
"No player this season is averaging more yards per route run (2.47) with as deep of an average depth of target (15.9 yards) as Moore. He was acquired from the Bears for a 2026 second-round pick this offseason," Suss wrote.
Chad Graff and Josh Kendall of The Athletic moved Buffalo up two spots as well, giving them the No. 1 position. Still, they're concerned about the pass defense, which has been suspect all season. They did bring back Tre'Davious White , which should help, but won't fix everything.
"There was hope for the Bills’ defense after they hired Jim Leonhard to lead the unit. But six games into the season, Buffalo has the fourth-worst pass defense in the league based on EPA per dropback and the third-worst defense overall. They’ve allowed more than 250 passing yards in five of six games this season,"
Kristopher Knox says the Bills needed the bye week as they have been fighting to win one-score games to start the season. This break could be exactly what they need to get the defense back on track, because as he said, winning with a porous defense is not sustainable.
"Allen and the offense have been more than capable of offsetting that suspect defense when playing mostly mistake-free football. However, the Bills' early-season formula may not be sustainable against top-tier teams in January," Knox wrote.
Pete Prisco ranks Buffalo second overall, but like most analysts, he's worried about the defense. There's a huge test coming up against Lamar Jackson, which is a chance for Jim Leonhard and his unit to prove themselves worthy.
"They come off the bye with a big one against the Ravens, who should have Lamar Jackson back. The defense has to be better than it was before the bye," Prisco wrote.

title: Fantasy Start or Sit Week 8: Bryce Young, Jalen Coker, and Chuba Hubbard
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers were a gold mine for fantasy football managers for the first six weeks of the NFL season. Despite largely flying under the radar, Bryce Young and all the skill position players were either good players or excellent value. Sometimes both. Even the defense seemed like a good play for a few weeks.
That all came crashing down in almost comical fashion in Week 7. The Panthers were chewed up and spit out by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Unless you had Darren Waller , who had a 50-yard touchdown, you probably regretted listening to our advice last week .
So, this week, the Panthers are on a short week. It's imperative to make the right decision because you have to decide early. So, should you start or sit these key Panthers?
The Bryce Young we knew and loved from the first five games crashed and burned. Part of it was a game situation and pass protection that were untenable for most QBs, but he also had his worst day of the year. That might strip his must-start status for now.
The Green Bay Packers are also pretty stingy against opposing QBs, allowing the fifth-fewest points to the position. That is, if you're wondering, one spot better than the Buccaneers. We expect Young to bounce back, but expectations have to be tempered.
Verdict: If you have no other option, start. Otherwise, sit him for someone else.
Because we expect Bryce Young to do better, that also means the two wide receivers, Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan, will do better. Coker has routinely received more targets than McMillan, and that could happen again this week.
Despite being stingy against QBs, the Packers are not stingy against wide receivers, ranking just outside the top 10 in fantasy points allowed to the position. Again, temper expectations, but Coker should have a much better day.
Verdict: Start, but perhaps as a flex
Finally, a good matchup. In 2026, the Packers are allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to running backs at 21.1 points per game. Chuba Hubbard, who has been excellent, averages 18 PPR points, so he could be in for a big day.
Given how things went last week and the general slow start to Carolina's run game this year, we expect them to make Hubbard a focal point earlier in the contest to take pressure off of the offensive line and Bryce Young. Hubbard is in line for a lot of usage against a bad defense. We'll take that.

title: Panthers Urged to Trade for Raiders' Kirk Cousins Amid Bryce Young Breakout
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers seem to have finally solved their quarterback crisis. While the most recent outing was pretty terrible thanks to a variety of reasons, Bryce Young has still been one of the absolute best quarterbacks in the NFL this season.
He's enjoying the rare year-four breakout, and he has probably locked up a long-term extension from the Panthers. The only question that really remains is how much he will cost this offseason. There aren't many other lingering concerns .
Apparently, that does not preclude the Panthers from being listed as a trade destination for quarterbacks. In the offseason, they were urged to trade for Mac Jones , but at least then, we didn't know what Young would look like.
Now that we do, why are ESPN's Matt Bowen and Jeremy Fowler saying they're a good spot for Kirk Cousins?
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that Kirk Cousins isn't necessarily available, but that he does make a lot of sense as a potential trade candidate ahead of the looming deadline.
"Cousins played well enough through seven games that he has trade value. So does his contract, which after being reworked features a $1.3 million base salary," Fowler wrote.
The Raiders aren't shopping him, but Fernando Mendoza's time is nigh and Cousins' value is pretty high. QB injuries happen all the time at a moment's notice, and a contender might benefit from having Cousins if that were to happen.
Matt Bowen added, "He lacks the mobility to make plays outside of structure at a consistent rate, but he can get to the edges on boot concepts, and he fits best in a system that incorporates play-action elements."
That all makes perfect sense. Cousins is far from a bad quarterback. What doesn't make sense is the two analysts listing the Panthers as a trade destination. They also listed the New York Giants and Minnesota Vikings, which make more sense than the Panthers.
Have neither Bowen nor Fowler watched the Panthers this year, or did they only tune in last week when the entire organization failed in a blowout loss? Young has been excellent this season, and he's likely to bounce right back this week.
And it's not as if Young needs a veteran mentor, either. The Panthers have Kenny Pickett to be that, and Young is in year four. He's not a newcomer. The Panthers moved on from Andy Dalton, so why would they bring in the 38-year-old Cousins?
The only reason is that Fowler and Bowen must believe that the Panthers, who are still in first place, could upgrade at quarterback with Cousins. He's playing well, but he would be ripped to shreds behind Carolina's offensive line.
Young is the quarterback of now and the future. Why we're still saying the Panthers need to trade for a quarterback is certainly beyond me.

title: 3 Storylines I'm Watching During Panthers' Trip to Lambeau Field
full_text:
I'm still trying to figure out exactly what the Carolina Panthers are.
I thought I was getting there before Sunday. Carolina had won two straight, Bryce Young was playing well and even a defense that had some rough moments earlier in the season seemed to be settling down. Then Tampa Bay came to Charlotte and beat the Panthers 43-13.
There wasn't one thing that went wrong, either. Carolina turned it over four times, gave up 258 rushing yards and allowed five sacks. By halftime, the Panthers were down 33-6 and the game was pretty much over. As I wrote in my three takeaways from the loss , the Panthers were bad on offense, bad on defense and even special teams got in on it.
Now they have to turn around and head to Lambeau Field on a short week. Maybe that's not the worst thing after a game like Sunday. I'm not sure sitting around thinking about that loss for seven days would've helped much anyway.
There are three things I'll be watching Thursday night.
Young had his worst game of the season against Tampa Bay, finishing 14-of-27 for 163 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. He also lost a fumble on a sack that Tampa Bay returned for a touchdown.
What made it so surprising was that we hadn't seen much of that from Young this season. He had thrown only two interceptions through Carolina's first five games before throwing two more Sunday.
I'm not putting all five sacks on him. The offensive line had a bad afternoon, too, and losing Taylor Moton to a broken fibula certainly doesn't make me feel any better about the group heading into Green Bay. But Young made some mistakes Sunday that he can't make again.
For me, this isn't about whether he throws for 300 yards or puts up some huge stat line at Lambeau. I want to see him take care of the football, make the throws that are there and not let one ugly game turn into two.
Young has played well enough for most of this season that I'm willing to look at Tampa Bay as one really bad afternoon. How he responds Thursday will tell us a little more.
This might be the one I'm most interested in because I thought Carolina had started to figure out its problems against the run.
The Panthers allowed only 213 rushing yards combined against Cleveland, Detroit and Philadelphia. Tampa Bay ran for 258 by itself. The Buccaneers ran it 49 times, tying the most rushing attempts ever by a Panthers opponent, and Baker Mayfield attempted only 11 passes because Tampa Bay never had much reason to stop running the football.
That's a pretty dramatic change from where things seemed to be headed. Before the Tampa Bay game, I wrote about how Carolina's run defense finally looked like it was turning a corner . The Panthers had held back-to-back opponents under 50 rushing yards.
Now Josh Jacobs is waiting for them in Green Bay.
I'd be surprised if the Packers don't test Carolina early. Why wouldn't they? Until the Panthers show that what happened Sunday isn't going to happen again, teams are going to make them prove they can stop it.
I don't expect Carolina to completely shut Jacobs down. I do expect the Panthers to make Green Bay work a lot harder for its rushing yards than Tampa Bay had to.
If the Packers can line up, hand the ball off and control the game without asking much from their passing game, Carolina is going to have a hard time winning at Lambeau.
This is the bigger question hanging over the game for me. I'm willing to give a team a bad week because it happens in the NFL, and Carolina isn't good enough yet for me to expect it to play well every time out.
But that Tampa Bay game bothered me because so many of the problems showed up at the same time. The turnovers came back, the offensive line struggled, the run defense disappeared and special teams made mistakes. It looked a lot more like some of the problems we saw earlier in the season than the team that had just won two straight.
That's why I came away from Sunday wondering if the Panthers had shown us who they really are . I'm not ready to go that far after one game, but I don't necessarily need Carolina to beat Green Bay to feel better about this team, either. Going into Lambeau on a short week is a tough assignment, especially with some of the injuries the Panthers are dealing with.
What I do need to see is a team that looks a lot more like the one we were watching before Sunday. Protect the football, don't let Green Bay run it whenever it wants and don't spend another first half digging a hole that's impossible to climb out of.
If Carolina goes to Lambeau and does those things, I can live with Tampa Bay being one of those games you throw away and move on from.
If it looks anything like Sunday again, I'm going to have a much harder time doing that.
Mark Livingston is a South Carolina native and recent Penn State graduate with a degree in Digital Media and Journalism. He previously wrote for Greenville Sports Media, where he covered various sports and teams across the Carolinas. His experience includes game coverage, feature stories and interviews.

title: The Panthers Have a Trade Deadline Decision to Make — And It's Not an Easy One
full_text:
If you had asked me before Sunday what the Carolina Panthers should do at the trade deadline, I probably would've told you to go get some help. They had won two straight, Bryce Young was playing well and the defense had started to look a lot better than it did earlier in the season. For the first time in a while, it felt like Carolina might actually have a reason to look for ways to improve the roster at the deadline instead of wondering which players it could trade away.
Then Tampa Bay beat the Panthers 43-13.
And yeah, that changed things for me a little bit.
One bad game shouldn't completely change how you feel about a team, but it was hard to watch that one and think Carolina is a player or two away. The Panthers turned the ball over four times, gave up 258 rushing yards and allowed five sacks. They were down 33-6 at halftime, and just about every problem this roster has showed up at the same time.
That's what makes this deadline interesting for Dan Morgan. The Panthers are 3-3 and still have plenty to play for, so I don't think you can just start selling players and looking toward next season. At the same time, this isn't a roster I'd be comfortable taking valuable draft picks away from just to make a run at the division.
I keep coming back to the injuries because Carolina is getting pretty thin in a couple of places. Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson are on injured reserve, and the Panthers have already had to dig deeper into their cornerback depth than they probably expected. Jaelan Phillips has been dealing with a hamstring injury, Thomas Incoom is on injured reserve and Carolina has also had to turn to Nick Hampton for help at edge.
Those are two positions where I'd be making calls if I'm Morgan. I wouldn't be looking for a star, and I'm definitely not giving up a second-round pick just because the Panthers happen to be in the division race. But if a team is willing to move a corner or pass rusher for a Day 3 pick, especially someone Carolina could keep around beyond this season, I'd be interested.
That's probably where the Tampa Bay loss changed my thinking the most. Before Sunday, I might've been willing to be a little more aggressive. After watching the Panthers get pushed around the way they did, I don't think one expensive addition suddenly changes what this team is. There are still too many areas that need work, and Carolina is going to need its draft picks to keep fixing them.
Taylor Moton's injury only adds to that. He's now on injured reserve with a broken fibula, and the offensive line just gave up five sacks against Tampa Bay. Morgan has already put a lot of resources into that group, so I don't know that I'd spend even more draft capital there unless the right deal practically fell into his lap.
The other side of this is pretty simple for me. Carolina is 3-3, and I'm not ready to start moving useful players off the roster because of one terrible Sunday.
This team has played better than what we saw against Tampa Bay. Young has put together some good games, the defense had been playing better and Carolina has won games I'm not sure many people expected it to win. If the Panthers were 2-5 or 1-6, this would be a completely different conversation. They're not.
That doesn't mean Morgan should pretend this team is closer than it really is. If somebody calls with an offer that's too good to pass up for a player Carolina doesn't see as part of its future, you listen. But actively shopping useful players while you're still in the division race doesn't make much sense to me.
I'm buying. I'm just not going crazy doing it.
Find some depth at corner. See what an edge rusher costs. Carolina could probably use someone like D.J. Wonnum right about now . If there's a younger player available who can help now and still be part of this thing next season, even better. What I wouldn't do is chase a big name just so it looks like Carolina is going for it.
The Panthers have finally reached a point where the trade deadline isn't only about the future. That's progress. Morgan just needs to make sure whatever he does at the deadline doesn't hurt what they're trying to build beyond this season.

title: NFL Week 8 Expert Picks Paint Clear Picture of Panthers' Chances vs. Packers
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are understandable underdogs on the road against the Green Bay Packers. They're coming off an abysmal loss. By most metrics, the 4-3 Packers are a better team than the 3-3 Panthers.
That doesn't always matter, but it seems to this week. At the time of writing, no one is picking the Panthers to win this contest on Thursday night.
CBS Sports Pete Prisco picked the Panthers to lose every week until last week, and he's not making the same mistake again. He picked the Packers to snag a 31-24 win at home. His CBS colleague John Breech thinks it will be 30-23 Packers.
"These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up, and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going," Prisco wrote.
Arizona Republic's Jeremy Cluff picked the Panthers to lose 27-23. "Bryce Young and the Panthers are 3-3 and lead the NFC South. The Packers are 4-3 and are last in the NFC North. Green Bay's defense will make some key stops against Carolina and Josh Jacobs will make a big impact to give the win to the last-place team," he wrote.
SI's Ian MacMillan believes the Packers will cover the 3.5-point spread. "I'm still out on this Panthers team, as they seem like a significant regression candidate after a strong start to the season. Bryce Young, up until last week, had been playing leaps and bounds better than he had the previous three seasons, and I'm of the belief that it's more of a sign of an abnormally strong start against some bad defenses as opposed to a quarterback who improved by tenfold in a single offseason," he wrote.
Sporting News' Bill Bender is taking the Packers, 27-22. "The Panthers have been wildly unpredictable this season, and it hinges on whether Bryce Young can bounce back from a bad outing against the Buccaneers. Green Bay has the worst rushing offense in the NFL (59.9 ypg). The Panthers have the worst rushing defense (153.3 ypg). Will Josh Jacobs get that running game on track?" he wrote.
This means the Panthers are the ultimate underdogs here. Not only are they not favored, but no one's picking them to win. It's rare, but that does happen, even for a team that is probably solid like the Panthers.
That could be where the Panthers operate best, as they usually win when they're not supposed to or are counted out. But after what we saw last week, it's not hard to see why they are universally being picked against.

title: Abysmal Outing Causes Panthers' Bryce Young to Slip in QB Power Rankings
full_text:
Prior to Week 7's ugly loss, Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young was rightfully in the MVP conversation. He was facing immense pressure behind, let's face it, the worst offensive line in the NFL. That's not exactly hyperbole. Check this chart out.
seemed pretty freaking good until today despite this pic.twitter.com/zzOvCZKBAA
Unfortunately, he's going to have to do a lot of hard work to get back into the MVP conversation after an ugly contest . His brilliant start to the season has been muddied. Or has it? Was one game where literally everything went wrong truly enough to push him that far down?
Maybe not. The Athletic's Mike Jones does a weekly QB stock report. Young surged to a high of nine on that list after beating the Philadelphia Eagles. Some lists have had him higher than that, which suggests that this list is not as topsy-turvy or reactive as others.
Where Young is now backs that up. Jones dropped Young from ninth to 11th, so he's still essentially a top-10 quarterback. He's still one of the best in the NFL, even when you factor in a really poor outing. Young made mistakes and missed throws.
What Jones' list is saying is that these days happen. Almost every quarterback in the NFL has a bad game on their resume already, and it's Week 8. Even Josh Allen, the potential MVP, has a game with zero touchdowns and two picks with a 54.0 RTG.
In other words, it happens. The Buccaneers' defense was in rare form on Sunday, and once things got out of hand (thanks mostly to an egregiously porous run defense by the Panthers), they pinned their ears back and went after Young.
It was a difficult situation to be in from the third drive onward, and it never got better. Those kind of games are going to happen, but they don't dull Young's shine.
We suspect other QB rankings will be much harsher to Young. But it bears mentioning that a list from The Athletic isn't docking Young all that much. It's telling that the overall consensus on Young hasn't changed after one bad outing in which the Panthers were outclassed at virtually every position on the field.
Gone are the days when a bad game would imply that the Panthers need to make a change, it seems. Gone are the days that a Young benching for his own safety in a blowout comes with fans clamoring to see the backup start instead. This is growth for everyone.

title: 4 Bold Predictions for Panthers vs. Packers That Just Might Come True
full_text:
For the second straight year, the Carolina Panthers will head into the wintry confines of Lambeau Field. For the second straight year, they will do so as underdogs after an abysmal loss in which they allowed 40 points the week prior. It's a little uncanny how that happened.
It should be a fun contest on Thursday night no matter what. Here are some bold predictions that could, under the right circumstances, come true this week.
The Panthers made life difficult on Jordan Love last year, and the defense has more talent this year to do the same. However, without Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, one would expect the Panthers to struggle in coverage.
Akayleb Evans is everyone's favorite punching bag, and sadly, he's likely to be picked on again (assuming he plays after being dinged up on Sunday). But Love is prone to being a little too aggressive at times, so we're predicting that Evans will finally punch back against an opposing offense and snag a takeaway.
It hasn't been a banner start to Jaelan Phillips' Panthers career. He does have 2.5 sacks in 4.5 games, which translates to a full season of over nine sacks. That's not that bad, although it's not what Carolina is paying for.
The Panthers should get Phillips back after missing last week, and the Packers, like the Panthers, have struggled to protect their quarterback. If anyone can make life difficult on that offensive line, it's Phillips, who can break out with two sacks of Love. And if Phillips can't go, then Princely Umanmielen should be able to wreak havoc, too.
Jalen Coker set his career high with 138 receiving yards in Week 1 this year, and the Packers' defense is pretty stout. However, they're allowing the 12th-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers this year.
Coker's been a little slow (not entirely his fault) since returning. A motivated Bryce Young against that secondary should lead to a solid day. Coker, because he will not see as much of Green Bay's best defender, should be able to set another career high.
The Panthers have no business winning this contest, which makes it the boldest prediction of all. They are and should be underdogs, and this is deservedly a game everyone expects them to lose. That was probably true before the Tampa Bay Buccaneers made mincemeat of Carolina as well.
They can't follow the same formula of controlling the game with the ground attack and limiting possessions. That won't work this time. But they do have the aerial firepower to go band for band with Green Bay, and the Packers have lackluster pass protection. There is a path, albeit narrow, to victory.

title: The Panthers Let a Key Player Walk in Free Agency. They Probably Regret That Now
full_text:
When the Carolina Panthers let D.J. Wonnum walk in free agency, I didn't think much of it.
Wonnum was coming off a season with only three sacks, and the Panthers had plenty of other things to worry about. He eventually signed a one-year, $3 million deal with the Detroit Lions, and at the time, I could understand Carolina deciding to move on.
Seven weeks into the season, I'm not so sure about that anymore.
Wonnum already has five sacks in six games for Detroit, which is two more than he had in 16 games for Carolina last season. He even got one against his former team when the Panthers played the Lions earlier this season.
This isn't me saying the Panthers made some terrible decision by letting Wonnum leave. If I didn't think it was a big deal at the time, I'm not going to sit here seven months later and pretend Dan Morgan should've known exactly how this would play out.
But look at Carolina's edge room right now. Jaelan Phillips has been dealing with a hamstring injury, Thomas Incoom is on injured reserve with a calf injury and the Panthers have already had to elevate Nick Hampton from the practice squad.
That's where the $3 million starts to bother me a little bit.
Wonnum wouldn't have come back as someone Carolina needed to build its defense around. He would've been another veteran pass rusher who could give them snaps, get after the quarterback and keep the Panthers from having to dig so deep into their depth when injuries hit.
And it's not like his production in Detroit came completely out of nowhere. Wonnum had eight sacks during his final season with Minnesota and then had four in only eight games during his first year with Carolina. Last season wasn't particularly good, but we've seen him produce when he's healthy.
Maybe things would've played out differently if he had stayed in Carolina. Maybe he doesn't have five sacks right now. There's no way to know that, and that's why I'm not going to call letting him leave some massive offseason mistake.
I just know the Panthers could use another healthy edge rusher right now, and a guy they let walk for $3 million is sitting in Detroit with five sacks.
Yeah, I bet they'd like to have that one back.

title: Fantasy Football Projections for Panthers' Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard & More
full_text:
It's a short week for the Carolina Panthers as they look to rebound from an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . The 43-13 decimation of the Panthers is raising major questions on both sides of the ball, especially the defense .
As in Week 1 against the Bears, the run defense was atrocious, allowing Tampa Bay was able to score 43 points despite Baker Mayfield throwing for just 64 passing yards.
As for the offense, Bryce Young, Chuba Hubbard, Tetairoa McMillan, and the rest of the roster performed poorly. Despite losing to the Detroit Lions in Week 7, the Packers have played at a high level for the last three weeks.
From a Fantasy Football perspective, Carolina faces another tough test, as the Packers are a top-10 to top-12 fantasy defense in the NFL. That said, Carolina can still put together decent performances. Here are the Week 8 projections for fantasy-relevant Panthers.
Coming off his worst game of the season, Bryce Young should be able to improve on his three-turnover performance. Against the Buccaneers, Young posted just over 5 fantasy points. Now going up against the Packers, don't expect a game-breaking performance, but an average or slightly below average game.
The Packers' defense ranks fifth against QBs this season, which should make fantasy managers a reason to hesitate to start Young on Thursday night. Even so, Young has still posted over 19 points in four of Carolina's six games; he's clearly more reliable than he has been in years past.
Unlike Bryce Young, Hubbard faces a favorable fantasy matchup this week. While the Packers' defense overall ranks in the top half of the league overall, it's currently 27th to 28th against running backs.
This doesn't mean that individually Hubbard will go off on his own, but there's certainly a chance he scores the most points among the Panthers this week.
Hubbard is Carolina's safest starter and has been all season. Through six games, Hubbard hasn't scored fewer than 10 points. That trend won't end on Thursday night, Hubbard is still a high end RB2
Another matchup that should be somewhat favorable. Both Coker and McMillan were ineffective against the Buccaneers, combining for fewer than 10 fantasy points and fewer receiving yards than Darren Waller, who caught one pass.
With Bryce Young having a tougher matchup, the receivers could suffer. Both Coker and McMillan have 30+ point performances, but outside of those games, neither has scored more than 16 points this season.
This feels like a game where both can produce, but not win someone's week for them.
Tetairoa McMillan final projection: 14.4
Jalen Coker final projection: 11.2

title: Pete Prisco's Bryce Young Take After Crushing Loss Shows How Far We've Come
full_text:
Two things can be true at once: the Carolina Panthers got outclassed in every way by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and Bryce Young had his worst start of the season . The two facts are undeniably related, but they're both true statements .
In the past, Young would've been blamed for the disaster. Why did he fumble and throw two interceptions? That's probably why they lost, right?
That was the running narrative for Young's first three years. If the Panthers lost, it was because they didn't have a good quarterback. Now, though, it's abundantly obvious that they do have a good quarterback.
So, while the temptation to blame the quarterback is there, even Pete Prisco, who notably has been slow to praise Young ever, believes it wasn't Young's fault in particular.
Pete Prisco admitted earlier this year that he was wrong about Bryce Young and that he deserved to be in the MVP conversation. It was honestly the first bit of praise for either Young or the Panthers from the CBS analyst in a long time.
Until Sunday's contest, Prisco had picked the Panthers to lose every single matchup. He was wrong this time, so perhaps he'll be back to it, but obviously, he's never been a big fan of the Panthers or Young. Even he can't deny how bad the team failed on Sunday.
"I'm not going to sit here and blame that loss on Bryce Young. The bottom line is that was a team loss." @PriscoCBS #NFLPostgame pic.twitter.com/2fFSJISkvE
Prisco said, "I'm not going to sit here and blame that loss on Bryce Young. By no means was that on him... He didn't play well, he threw interceptions, but the bottom line is, that was a team loss."
The analyst rightfully took aim at the Panthers' run defense, which was once again porous. "You can't play and win playing that style of football," he said.
Young, as Prisco said, was not great, but things got out of hand almost immediately. Bad protection by Robert Hunt led to the fumble returned for a touchdown that made it 17-0. From then on, the Buccaneers knew he would have to pass.
He managed to hit Darren Waller for a 50-yard touchdown to spark some hope, but the special teams allowed a blocked PAT to be returned for two points, deflating things even further.
From then on, the stout Tampa defense knew what the Panthers had to do, so they pinned their ears back and went after Young to the tune of five sacks. By that point, the game was over, so Young's mistakes didn't really cost them the game.
He'll tell you he needs to be better. He does, and he has been this year. But Sunday's ugly showing was more than a QB problem. It was an organizational failure from the top down.
The silver lining to this loss is that it isn't coming with calls for Young to be benched. Everyone seems to be in agreement that of all the things going wrong for Carolina this year, quarterback isn't one. How far we've come.

title: Caleb Williams Showing Ben Johnson Exactly What Bears Need From a QB
full_text:
So far Caleb Williams has proven himself against some pretty good defenses but now it would appear he'll test himself against the best.
The point where Williams must display talent sufficient with being a successful NFL quarterback passed long ago, when he proved it with seven fourth-quarter comebacks and then won a playoff game over the rival Packers. Now, he's trying to prove his team and himself are not just playoff caliber but potential Super Bowl winners. There's no better way to do it in the regular season than by taking out the champions and getting the best of Seattle's "Dark Side" defense.
“They don't allow deep plays, so you’ve got to be as patient as possible and that's obviously hard," Williams said "The whole game trying to be patient, it's a challenge for me.
"It's a challenge for our offense being able to take the dirty yards, protecting the football. They do a good job with punching the ball out and interceptions."
“I think that [Caleb Williams] is going to lead Chicago to a Super Bowl championship within the next two years.” — @stephenasmith on just how dangerous the Bears have become 😤 pic.twitter.com/VYK6ledTXx
Mike Macdonald's defense is first in yards allowed, second in takeaways with 12, but also completely shuts down offenses. With Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy, Devon Witherspoon, Julian Love and Ernest Jones showing the way, the Seahawks haven't allowed more than 176 yards passing in a game this year.
Williams and the Bears' passing game will be every bit as challenged as their running game will be, because the Seahawks have allowed less than 110 yards rushing to every team except the Chargers (147).
“Still watching, but obviously that's the best defense in football right now; stats-wise and players and scheme," Williams said. "It's going to be fun for us. It's going to be a challenge for us and we accept that challenge."

Jay Cutler - 9 Justin Fields - 14 Mitch Trubisky - 20 Rex Grossman - 16 Caleb Williams - 38 pic.twitter.com/MG7O9vHjpS
Williams says this coming off of what might have been his most complete game in outdueling Drake Maye and the Patriots.
“There were a few passes that I maybe didn't pull the trigger on," Williams said. "I may have found a check down or I may have run or something like that. Just small things, like there was one that my footwork was off and we ended up missing. It was the first third-down to Kalif (Raymond) on the right side. I believe it was the first third-down that I missed to Kalif. My footwork was off.
"Just small things like that, that show up in those moments, and when you play versus a good team like we played, and then when you play versus a good team like we're about to play, you’ve got to be on, and you’ve got to be at your best."
“Drake is really physically gifted. Caleb’s just a little bit more physically gifted. Drake’s in a really good situation, Caleb’s in a better situation... Drake so far has been a bit more of a rollercoaster where as Caleb’s improvement has been incremental.” — @DannyParkins pic.twitter.com/R1cbgNVDsD
With a 105.6 passer rating, league-high 79.6 QBR and 71% completion rate, Williams has never been at a better point to test so strong of a defense. It might help him to have his full complement of running backs, because Kyle Monangai remains out of practice heading into Friday -- the Bears have a day off Thursday.
“Here's what I love: I love just where he is mindset-wise right now," coach Ben Johnson said of his QB. "No one's more critical of him than himself at this point, and as good as he's done taking care of the football and certainly the higher completion percentage and all those things, we would come in and there's a lot more to be had last week.
"He's the first one to say it, and we go through it and work it and improve while still highlighting the improvements we've already made along the way. I thought he had some of the more accurate run-after-catch throws, ball locations last week, and it continues to get more and more each and every week, and we need that."
CALEB WILLIAMS LASER ON THIRD AND LONG. NEvsCHI on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/HLNowyCVnN
It's not perfect. Williams knows it.
"I think that's what I love the most about him right now is he loves that criticism," Johnson said. "He loves to take that, and he chews on it; gets a little time out of the building, chews on it, and then he comes back."
Better awareness in the pocket, a better sense of when to get out of it, and the more accurate throws are part of why Johnson says he sees the maturation process taking root with his QB.
𝗧𝗥𝗘𝗡𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚: Bears fans are SHOCKED that QB Caleb Williams does not have a police escort home after every game. Caleb instead sits in traffic for hours with regular people, potentially putting his safety at risk. This is unacceptable 🤦‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/70Ow7dn5BW
"He's just matured a lot in that regard, taking a game plan, downloading it, and being able to bring it to life on a fairly quick basis here," Johnson said.
The best defense Williams faced this year besides the Seahawks was Minnesota and until he injured his hamstring it appeared he was going to find a way to beat them.
Finishing this one intact, and with wins over both Super Bowl LX teams is the next goal for a quarterback who seems to be ascending each week before the league's very eyes.

title: Defiant Caleb Williams Plans to Keep Wearing Unauthorized Cleats
full_text:
Caleb Williams isn't necessarily being a Jim McMahon rebel type, defying the league by wearing a headband bearing messages not certified by the NFL.
However, he has been wearing cleats not a part of the NFL apparel code for games, and as such was fined last week. This could get expensive because does not plan to give up those shoes.
The Bears QB is wearing Caddix cleats instead of a brand with an NFL certification, like NIKE, adidas or Under Armour. It cost him $11,941.
"As we’ve known for the past couple of years now, I’m huge into my body, I’m huge into trying to stay on the field," Williams said. "I’m huge into trying to be healthy. It’s a rough game and things like that.
"So the cleats, they’ve been great. They’ve been super comfy and they’ve worked. They are a science type of cleat. It’s something that focuses on when you plant, on the hard plants on turf or grass, they call them SmartStuds, and they move when you move in these hard plants. They take tension off of your tendons, your joints and all of that. So over the course of a long career or over the course of a long year, when you can take some percentage — it could be one, it could 50, it could be 12, it could be whatever, you know. When you take that percentage off consistently over a period of time, you know, you get to have the chance, a higher chance of being healthy."
The problem with Williams' explanation is he was injured for the first time in his career this year in Week 2 and sat out three games with a hamstring issue suffered while making a cut.
Williams admitted he can't say how much it helped him avoid being hurt worse on the cut he made or if it even had an impact.
"Obviously, if I had that answer, I’d be a trillionaire and sitting somewhere nice," he said. "So yeah, I don’t know that, but I think it does (help). I think my joints, my ankles and my knees and my feet haven’t bothered me as much from the other cleats that I’ve worn, that you’ve seen me wear throughout the week or throughout games and throughout the weeks of games where you’re consistently playing and you get up one day and your knees hurt or your ankles are hurt and your feet hurt or anything like that.
Caleb Williams was fined by the NFL over $11K for his Caddix cleats he wore against the Atlanta Falcons for being in violation of the NFL Uniform and Equipment Rules. 📸: Getty pic.twitter.com/wf2F5VeRRu
"Like I said, they’ve worked for me and I feel that I feel a difference. That’s my opinion, and somebody else can have another."
He is going to keep wearing them regardless of what the league thinks.
"Yeah, like I said, focused on my health, I’m focused on being able to be out here for the guys," Williams said. "And if that can give me a small percentage up and it works, then that’s what I’m gonna do.
"And so that’s what I focus on. I try to be healthy. They’re smart cleats. They’re science cleats, and they’ve been working for me. A bunch of other guys wear them in the league, and they’re forward-focused on making sure players stay on the field, and that’s what I’m always focused on."
How long? pic.twitter.com/Ky7igKhnJg
The league has long focused on trying to restrict players, coaches and others too much. Too much scrutiny for a player's apparrel is ridiculous. They legislate celebrations and restrict anyone's creativity. The  league should focus more on its own problems, like why the officiating seems to draw more and more criticism each year and get worse and worse while the rules seem to become more confusing by the season.
A fine for a pair of shoes that aren't bearing some sort of a statement or message contrary to the values of the country or the league is a case of overjurisdiction. In other words, they need to lighten up. Williams isn't even going to pay the fine, anyway. The shoe company says it will do it.
So the league should use it as a means for doing away with fines for things like this.
Caleb talking about Caddix: They protect my feet from injury better than existing shoes. NFL: NOT ON OUR WATCH! pic.twitter.com/8bF8wJG2zS

title: Jeffery Simmons Isn't the Only Titans Star the Bears Have Rumored Interest in
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts have already begun offloading a few valuable players , and most believe the 1-6 Titans aren't far behind them.
Unsurprisingly, the Chicago Bears have reportedly shown interest in star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . However, they'd undoubtedly have to pay an arm and a leg (Tennessee reportedly would only consider offers that include a first-round pick) to land him.
The four-time Pro Bowler isn't the only member of Tennessee's defensive line who might interest Chicago, though. The Bears are one of two teams (along with the Browns) that ESPN's Jeremy Fowler listed as a potential fit for edge rusher Jermaine Johnson II.
"Teams in the market for an edge rusher believe Johnson could be available at the right price," Fowler wrote. "The Titans are reeling at 1-6 and are still in rebuilding mode, which necessitates adding more draft picks. Johnson is a Robert Saleh favorite from their Jets days together and just got to Tennessee via an offseason trade. But enough interest in the edge-rush market could make him a factor."
If you're experiencing Déjà vu based on the Bears' rumored interest in Johnson, that makes sense. NFL insider Jordan Schultz confirmed they were also interested in trading for him last season , but weren't willing to part with a second-round pick to poach him away from the Jets.
Instead, the Bears pivoted to Joe Tryon-Shroyinka , whom they acquired from Cleveland via a late-round pick swap. Johnson stayed put in New York, and the Titans acquired him in exchange for defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat in the offseason.
It feels safe to assume Johnson could be had for much less than a second-round pick now. He had a down 2025 campaign, putting up only three sacks and six QB hits over 14 games for the Jets. To his credit, he's already matched both figures through the first seven games this season, but he's still playing out the final year of his deal.
Whichever team trades for him would do so knowing he'd either be an eight-game rental (plus playoffs) or they'd have to commit to re-signing him. Seeing him be dealt for a fourth-round pick seems more likely based on that fact.
With Montez Sweat's guaranteed money voided after his two-game suspension for violating the league's substance abuse policy, they would be able to easily cut/trade him this offseason. That would grant them flexibility to lock Johnson into a short-term extension if they wanted to go that route.
If there's one thing about Bears general manager Ryan Poles, it's that he's not going to sit on his hands.
The Bears have made six in-season trades since Poles became the team's GM in 2022. They've shipped out Roquan Smith, Robert Quinn, and Khalil Herbert, and have acquired Chase Claypool, Montez Sweat, and Tryon-Shroyinka.
With the Bears sitting at 5-2, it should come as no surprise to hear that they're suspected buyers at the trade deadline . They're looking to capitalize on their hot start and believe they're poised to make a run.
If they believe Johnson can boost their pass-rush efficiency up front, then they'll definitely bring him in if the Titans aren't firm (or at least as firm as the Jets were) on their asking price.

title: Reading Between the Lines of Ben Johnson's 'Vague' Injury Update for Coby Bryant
full_text:
The first week of Chicago Bears training camp back in August was a rough one. The Bears' biggest free agency acquisition, safety Coby Bryant, left practice with a leg injury that ended up requiring surgery. Bryant was given a four-to-six-month recovery timeline, meaning a best-case scenario would see him return to the field sometime in mid-December.
On Wednesday afternoon, head coach Ben Johnson gave an update on Bryant's recovery to Bears media, saying, "He's on track. I think in the near future we're going to start with some on-land running, but we're still a little ways away from him doing the change-of-direction stuff. That's really going to be the stress test with him."
In response to a follow-up question, Johson insisted that any updates to Bryant's return timeline would be intentionally vague, though he did divulge that his rehab over the next month will be the most crucial part of his recovery.
At first blush, there's not much to gleen from this injury update. Bryant has apparently progressed as expected thus far, no more and no less than that. However, by reading between the lines a bit, I think there's reason for Bears fans to be optimistic that Bryant's return will come towards the early side of projections.
Bears fans will remember the crushing feeling when left tackle Ozzy Trapilo was revealed to have ruptured his patellar tendon back in January. There was a very real chance that he would miss the entire 2026 season. Instead, Trapilo's improbable return from injury saw him taking practice reps well ahead of schedule, and he made his official return to the team in Week 6 when he took a limited number of snaps against the Atlanta Falcons and the New England Patriots in Week 7.
Those positive updates for Trapilo came largely out of the blue at the time, which means the Bears were keeping Trapilo's progress in rehab under pretty tight wraps. They could be doing the same thing now for Bryant, in which case 'no news is good news' should be the watchword for Bears fans.
After all, we know that Ben Johnson likes to dabble in gamesmanship, and he wants to keep opposing coaches guessing. We saw him do this with Caleb Williams' injury, not ruling him out of their Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles during his first injury update for Williams . In regards to Bryant, what would Johnson gain by announcing to the world that potentially his biggest weapon on defense could return ahead of schedule?
Most importantly, Johnson's message that the month of November would be critical in determining Bryant's return struck me as optimistic in tone. This is purely conjecture, but that suggests to me that they feel good about where Bryant is in his recovery and that, as long he stays on track, he should be good to go for December. However, the team understandably doesn't want to put that kind of hope out there and risk having it blow up in their faces should there be a setback.
To reiterate, I'm not operating with any insider knowledge of the situation. This is just my interpretation of Johnson's injury update for Bryant, one that he admitted was vague by design. Others may read his words and come to a more pessimistic conclusion, and they could be right.
That's not the way I see it, though. Optimism seemed to shine around the edges of Johnson's guarded words, and that, combined with Bryant's cryptic post on social media earlier this month, has me believing that the Bears could be getting a major defensive weapon back just in time for a playoff push.
A former Marine and Purdue Boilermaker, Pete has been covering the Chicago Bears since 2022 as a senior contributor on BearsTalk. He lives with his wife, two kids and loyal dog.

title: Kyle Monangai Injury Update From Practice Confirms Minor Progress For Bears RB
full_text:
We have a sign of progress for Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai, who is working his way back from injury.
Monangai has missed the last three games due to turf toe and he has not practiced in that span, either.
While he was once again a non-participant during practice on Wednesday after sitting out Tuesday's session , also, Monangai showed some minor progress by getting in stationary bike work, according to Adam Jahns of CHGO Bears .
"Bears back at practice today. We saw Kyle Monangai on the bike during warmups, but he wasn’t on the field during the open period," Jahns wrote.
The progress comes from the fact that this is the first semblance of work Monangai has been seen doing since his injury. It's not much, but we'll take it.
And it's the latest positive sign for Monangai's chances of suiting up. Earlier in the day, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai is closer to playing this week than he was last.
"Bears running back Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has missed the past three weeks, but his chances are better of playing this week," Fowler reported .
The Bears do not have to release an injury report until Thursday because their Week 8 contest against the Seattle Seahawks is Monday night.
Because the Bears practiced on Tuesday and Wednesday, the first injury report will be an estimation. If Monangai is estimated as a limited participant, that will be good news for his chances of suiting up against the Seahawks.
We're still fairly skeptical that Monangai is going to suit up in Week 8, and that's for a few reasons.
We're already halfway through the week and Monangai hasn't been able to take part in practice in any capacity. The bike work is good to see, but it's not enough to offer much optimism.
The Bears also made the decision to promote a running back to the 53-man roster in Zavier Scott, who has been taking on the Bears' RB3 role while Monangai has been sidelined.
Scott was out of practice squad elevations, so the Bears had to promote him in order to have the ability to use him again. That's an indication the Bears think they're going to need him this week, which means they don't expect Monangai will go.
But there are still multiple days left before the Bears drop their final injury report of the week, hence, there is still hope.

title: Ben Johnson Delivers Message for Jaylon Johnson and Bears Defenders
full_text:
Bears coach Ben Johnson is a patient man and it seems lately like his defensive backs are testing his limits.
Johnson has been elated with the play of edge rusher Daniel Hardy, particularly with last week's 1 1/2 sacks as the Bears sought to make up for the loss of Montez Sweat due to a two-week PED violation and suspension.
In fact, Johnson suggested Hardy might warrant more playing time as a result of the production boost he provided. Hardy largely had been a special teams player in the past.
"I like to highlight Daniel Hardy," Johnson said on Wednesday. "I think he has done as good a job as anybody affecting the passer these last two weeks and he’s a guy who certainly warrants a little bit more playing time on defense as well."
Jaylon Johnson is a massive problem, and that’s an understatement. The missed tackle % is enough to make you vomit. pic.twitter.com/ycvFoFizaH
However, when it comes to pass coverage, the Bears struggled three straight games and last week cornerback Jaylon Johnson did in particular.
So where does Jaylon Johnson stand with his coach heading into the Seattle game as they try to stop wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba? When asked specifically about Jaylon Johnson's play , Ben Johnson responded with more of a threat or promise when asked about this situation.
"There's been some ups and some downs, and so just like everybody we're evaluating at the end of each game, winning performance versus losing performance," Ben Johnson said. "And like I alluded to with Daniel Hardy, he's a prime example, guys that are stepping up in their opportunities, they warrant more playing time.
"And so that's the case that we do offense, defense, and special teams each and every week, and we'll continue to do that."
That sounds a lot like Jaylon Johnson's playing time is either getting cut back or they're on the verge of it if he comes up with another poor effort.
Jaylon Johnson man 🥺🥴🥲 pic.twitter.com/KbrO40wdUJ
Johnson whiffed on two touchdowns by the Patriots, once when quarterback Drake Maye faked him out on a run and the other when Rhamondre Stevenson took a short pass and turned into a 48-yard TD catch and run rather than attempting a Hail Mary pass.
Perhaps Johnson's playing time stays the same this week because cornerback Malik Muhammad has missed two practices Tuesday and Wednesday with a toe injury and he could have been a replacement.
Then again, they also have Clark Phillips available. Phillips got in for three plays against the Patriots, but according to Pro Football Focus he was the only Bears player with a worse pass coverage grade than Johnson. They had Johnson at 38.6 and Phillips at 35.0. Pro Football Reference has Johnson allowing a passer rating against of 100.4 or worse in every single game this year and a 129.4 for the season. They also have him at seven missed tackles, a team high.
Jaylon Johnson... pic.twitter.com/sD2DyH9WNq
The idea of cutting back Johnson's playing time is fine if the Bears actually have someone to replace him.
However, until they have Muhammad back, they don't really have a satisfactory replacement. Also, the other cornerback needs to be looked at and that's Tyrique Stevenson. His performance has been spotty, sometimes strong but other times even worse than Johnson's.
Don’t forget pic.twitter.com/LlYhu5hHYi

title: The Chicago Bears Need to Take a Flier on Recently Released DT
full_text:
Rarely do you see players coming off a breakout campaign get released in-season the following year, especially when they're still on their rookie contracts.
Nevertheless, that situation occurred when the Raiders cut ties with third-year defensive tackle Jonah Laulu on Tuesday. Las Vegas claimed the former seventh-round selection off waivers ahead of the 2024 campaign, and he started seven games for the Raiders during his rookie season.
Laulu then took his game to the next level last season. He started 15 games and tied for third on the team in both sacks (4) and TFLs (8). He also played 68% of the defensive snaps (764) and looked like an ascending player in his age-25 campaign.
Unfortunately, Laulu has failed to build on his impressive 2025 campaign to start this season. He played only 110 of 473 (23%) of the Raiders' defensive snaps and was a healthy scratch in two games.
He played the fourth-most snaps among Raiders defensive tackles and was effectively phased out of defensive coordinator Rob Leonard's scheme. The latter fact was a bit surprising considering Leonard was promoted from the team's defensive line coach.
While Laulu's ascension might've gotten firmly halted, he's still only 26 years old. He has some untapped potential and could make an impact elsewhere if he lands in the right scheme. There's reason to believe the Chicago Bears could be a perfect landing spot for him.
The Bears' defensive line has performed better than expected to begin the season . It was widely considered their most glaring weakness, but they've held their own over the first seven weeks. They're tied for seventh with 19 sacks, although some resulted from defensive coordinator Dennis Allen sending extra rushers from the secondary.
However, many believe Chicago will be in the market for a new defensive lineman ahead of the November 10 trade deadline. A big splash would put them in a position where they wouldn't have to send any extra rushers to get home.
While Laulu might not be as impactful as his former running mate Maxx Crosby, he still showed plenty of promise last season. Notably, the Bears wouldn't have to give up two first-round selections (or any draft picks, for that matter) to get him in the building.
You could also make a strong case that Chicago's need for juice on the interior outweighs their need to add more bodies at defensive end. Montez Sweat will return from his two-game suspension on Monday night, and Daniel Hardy played well in his absence . Meanwhile, they're still looking for some consistency on the interior next to Grady Jarrett.
One team's trash often becomes another team's treasure. Laulu could be that for the Chicago Bears, and they'd be wise to take a flier on him to find out.

title: Kyle Monangai Injury Update From ESPN Gives Bears RB Shred of Hope For Week 8 Return
full_text:
On Tuesday, there were nothing but bad signs for the Week 8 status of Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai, but on Wednesday, we have at least a shred of hope.
According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Monangai has a better chance to play this week than he has in weeks past.
"Bears running back Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has missed the past three weeks, but his chances are better of playing this week," Fowler reported.
Now, to be clear, it doesn't take a rocket scientist to figure out that Monangai has a better chance to play this week now that he's three weeks removed from his injury.
However, at least Fowler's reporting doesn't have any semblance of a pessimistic outlook for Week 8, so that gives us at least a bit of hope amid the bad signs we received on Tuesday.
The Bears were on the practice field on Tuesday and Monangai was not taking part, according to beat writers on the ground.
"During the open portion of practice, we did not see RB Kyle Monangai or CBs Malik Muhammad or Tyrique Stevenson," The Chicago Tribune's Sean Hammond reported.
We were hoping to see at least some action from Monangai to begin the week, which would have put him on track to return, but that did not happen and now he's trending in the wrong direction once again this week.
On top of that, the Bears decided to promote running back Zavier Scott to the active roster, which could be a sign that the Bears are planning for Monangai to sit out again. Scott has been the Bears' RB3 behind D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson during Monangai's absence.
We should point out Scott was out of practice squad elevations and has been a plus special teams contributor, so that might be behind why the Bears made that move.
However, when you combine that with Monangai's lack of practice participation, it lends to the idea that Scott was promoted in anticipation of Monangai sitting out yet again.
Let's go glass half-full, shall we?
The Bears said from the outset that they didn't plan to place the second-year running back on injured reserve , which was a hint they didn't think Monangai would miss more than three games because, as we know, IR stints require a four-game absence.
"It wasn't something we felt required an IR stint. It remains a week-to-week situation, but as far as I know, he's continuing to trend in the right direction," Head coach Ben Johnson said on Oct. 16.
Along with that, Monangai has an extra day to get himself right this week with the Bears' game versus the Seattle Seahawks taking place on Monday night.
Those two factors along with Fowler's reporting is about all we can offer right now when it comes to optimism surrounding Monangai's Week 8 status.
We'll just have to wait and see how things shake out when Chicago drops its injury reports starting on Thursday.

title: NFL Insider Projects Khalil Mack Trade Price For Bears as Rumors Continue to Swirl
full_text:
Where there's smoke, there's fire, and we are seeing plenty of smoke about the Chicago Bears possibly making a play for Los Angeles Chargers edge rusher Khalil Mack.
Several NFL insiders have linked the Bears to Mack recently , and now ESPN's Jeremy Fowler is getting in on the fun.
Not only is Fowler linking Mack to the Bears, he projects the trade cost for Chicago as a "quality Day 3 pick" to bring the fan-favorite home.
"Returning to the Bears is a natural fit for the equivalent of a quality Day 3 pick. The Chargers have held off trading pieces such as Mack up to this point, though," Fowler said.
There have been no shortage of insiders connecting Mack to the Bears.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported that the Bears are "expected" to have interest in the nine-time Pro Bowler.
FOX's Jay Glazer reports the Bears "have already talked to" Los Angeles about a trade for Mack, and NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Bears have been "connected to several defensive players," including Mack.
Along with Mack, Schultz named Arizona Cardinals EDGE Josh Sweat as another player. He also mentioned DeForest Buckner, but Buckner has since been traded to San Francisco.
To us, a quality Day 3 pick is likely a fourth-round selection, and possibly a fifth, at worst.
According to Spotrac , the Bears have their fourth-round picks in each of the next three drafts, and they have a fifth-round pick in each, also, with their 2027 fifth-rounder coming via the Atlanta Falcons from the Gervon Dexter trade .
So, the Bears can easily afford a trade for Mack.
As Fowler noted, the Chargers have not shown interest in selling at the deadline, but they are also 0-6 and have no hope to make the playoffs at this point. As a result, despite their public posturing, Los Angeles has to at least be considering unloading players.
Of all the players on the Chargers' roster, Mack makes the most sense as a trade candidate. Not only is he a free agent in 2027, there's also a chance he decides to retire, something he has contemplated before .
If the Chargers don't trade Mack and he rides off into the sunset, Los Angeles will have nothing to show for it.
Another motivation to trade Mack might come from the player himself. At this stage in his career, Mack probably isn't keen on riding out what could be his final season with a team that isn't going to the playoffs. As a result, he could request a trade.
The Bears' pass-rush hasn't been all that bad this season, but that doesn't mean Chicago couldn't use more help. After all, we've seen just how quickly things can change in recent weeks after the injury to Dayo Odeyingbo and the suspension to Montez Sweat left the Bears in a precarious spot.
Odeyingbo is going to be out at least two more games as a result of his four-game injured reserve stint , and we're still not sure if he will need more time beyond that. Not to mention, Sweat has been disappointing with his two sacks.
Mack can offer the added depth the Bears need, and he wouldn't just be a body, either, as evidenced by his three sacks this season. Having Mack would also enable the Bears to give Odeyingbo more snaps on the interior, where he has thrived in 2026.

title: How Demands for Bears Defensive Line Trades Miss Their Real Problem
full_text:
The great fan outcry per social media and elsewhere is for the Bears to acquire a defensive lineman, so the Colts' trade of DeForest Buckner to San Francisco for a fourth-rounder was viewed as opportunity lost.
Indeed, analysts for various media outlets have also been falling all over themselves to match the Bears up with a trade for a defensive lineman, whether it's former Bears edge Khalil Mack or defensive tackles like Washington's Daron Payne or even Tennessee's Jeffery Simmons. Why the Titans would be willing to part with Simmons after dumping a boatload of cash on him in the offseason is never explained by those trying to establish this link.
Bill Barnwell of ESPN even suggested the Bears trade a late draft pick for Anthony Nelson, a sub with Tampa Bay. That one has Joe Tryon-Shoyinka stamped all over it.
Edge rush, interior rush, run stoppers, it's all defensive line talk.
#Bears fans, would you trade 2 first round picks for Jeffrey Simmons? He's 29, under contract through 2030 at roughly $35 million/year, and is one of the best defensive lineman in football.
Taking this into consideration, What's wrong with the following picture:
This Jaylon Johnson? pic.twitter.com/z6y1kavhNY
Jaylon Johnson… pic.twitter.com/Cl3yH7J9lN
Now, what's the reason again why the Bears must trade for a defensive lineman?
It's fairly obvious from all of these numbers that Chicago's big weakness is its secondary, especially at cornerback, but at one of the safety spots as well. Coby Bryant isn't coming back soon, so safety must be regarded right there with cornerback. The reports on Bryant's injury said four to six months. At five months, he's missing the rest of this season unless they get in the Super Bowl.
This is an ugly rep for Tyrique Stevenson. Coker doesn’t do much just runs right past him. Way too easy. #DaBears #ChicagoBears pic.twitter.com/aOD4E2o5kM
It never hurts to have more pass rush help, but  rush and cover requires cover.
As Barnwell pointed out, the Bears do have a 9.8% sack rate when they rush four or less, one of the best rates in the league. The Bears are at 53% in ESPN's pass rush win rate, ninth best in the league. Pro Football Reference has the Bears at 28% for pressure rate. That's fourth best in the league.
They are two sacks away from leading the NFL.
Nah watch #24 Malik Muhammad. Runs away from the play. Rigged? pic.twitter.com/vebDAuBbul
Now who is it that's not getting the job done and what do they need?
There is more to the defensive front than pass rush. There is stopping the run. They're third in rushing yards allowed.
And it's the line and not the secondary where they need help?
Considering the Colts are leading the way in fire sales, Charvarius Ward is a Colts cornerback considered as trade fodder. They also have Sauce Gardner but he makes so much money a team with a huge amount of cap space would have to be the one trading to get him, and that's not the Bears. Also, his passer rating against is even worse than Jaylon Johnson's and only slightly better than Stevenson's.
Tyrique Stevenson can't let this happen pic.twitter.com/bS1C8S3ssl
Tennessee's Alontae Taylor makes sense, although he's not a free agent next year and his current deal with $14 million in a cap hit this year and $25 million next year looms as a stumbling block.
The Chargers' Donte Jackson has a career filled with consistent and strong performances, and is mentioned often as a possible trade candidate. However, he has a hamstring injury at the moment.
The Bears already traded and acquired one cornerback, Clark Phillips of the Falcons. He's only been on the field for 27 defensive snaps.
Cam Lewis’ PFF grade for this game should be in the negatives. The man is taking the worst possible angles on tackles that he should be investigated for point shaving. Legitimately one of the worst halves by a player I’ve ever seen.
Considering everything, the fact they're last in the NFL in net yards allowed per pass attempt, and that they have found ways to mount a strong enough pass rush to rank in the top 10 in sacks, maybe it's time to dip into the defensive back market again but to do it in a serious way this time.
Perhaps it's time someone realizes the pass coverage and not the rush is really their chief need.

title: Bengals Defense on Track to Fix Massive Weakness During 2026 Season
full_text:
Missed tackles have plagued the Bengals' defense for years.
Six games into the 2026 season, it appears they have made progress in addressing that weakness. SumerSports confirmed that the Bengals currently rank seventh in the league with only 45 missed tackles on 404 attempts for a missed tackle rate of 11.1%. That is only 3.4% worse than the Lions, who rank as the best in the league with a 7.7% missed tackle rate.
Barrett Carter and Demetrius Knight Jr. led the way last season with 35 missed tackles combined. Geno Stone and Jordan Battle combined for 47 missed tackles in 2025, bringing the total for all four players to 82. For reference, the Bengals defense missed 171 tackles total last season.
Carter and Knight have still struggled to stop ball carriers on the ground this season, with 14 combined missed tackles; however, they have improved in other areas of their game.
Carter has improved in coverage, along with his tracking ability in the open field, while Knight has become more of a downhill thumper against the run game.
Cook has made a name for himself as a reliable tackler at safety in the league, and he has carried that presence into this season.
He only has three missed tackles all season after dealing with an early ankle injury. If he stays on his current pace, he should finish the season with 11 missed tackles, a drastic improvement from Stone's 26 last year.
His presence alone has eased the growing pains for Knight and Carter, though Battle has remained inconsistent as the Bengals' other safety. Over six games, Battle has missed eight tackles and made mistakes similar to those he committed last season.
The potential remains for the Bengals to add another playmaker to the defense via a fairytale style trade and replace Battle.
As of now however, even with the inconsistency from Battle, the defense has shown steady improvement in Al Golden's second season as defensive coordinator. At their current pace, the defense should surrender 135 missed tackles, approximately 36 less than last year.

title: 'I Think Every GM Is Exploring' - Joe Burrow Comments on Bengals Adding Talent With Trade
full_text:
Is Joe Burrow eager for the Bengals to make another trade move this year? Not necessarily. Burrow dove into that topic during Wednesday's press conference and hammered home his confidence in all the players Cincinnati has right now.
The Bengals have a few needs the front office could shore up with another win-now trade like the home-run decision to acquire Dexter Lawrence.
"Number one, I feel really good about our team and the guys we have in there," Burrow declared. "Number two, I think every GM in football is probably exploring all options at this point, and very few ever end up materializing, but that's something that I think all those guys think about critically, and whether it ends up happening or not, who knows. But I feel really good about the team we have in there."
Cincinnati has played defense at a solid level so far, and the front especially is much better compared to last season. The trade for Lawrence is a huge reason for that.
He's posted four sacks so far and is on pace for a career-high, while notching an 87.6 Pro Football Focus grade (second-best in career).
"I think it was a unique situation," Burrow noted about Lawrence. "I don't think there's very often that a player like Dex becomes available, and then for one first-round pick in a high-need position for us. I think all those things together kind of created the perfect storm of a situation for us to involve ourselves, and yeah, obviously it's worked out great for us, and we couldn't be happier with it."
Burrow is graded right around Lawrence (91.2 overall, first among all qualified passers, third in ESPN QBR) and has been near the top of his position as well in normal stats. If he keeps playing like this, plus, Cincinnati stays healthy and maybe adds a player via trade, then an MVP award is on the table.
"Number one, you have to be on a great team," Burrow said. "Rarely does a bad team have an MVP, and at the end of the day, it's usually the best player with the most stats on the best team. So, best team is number one on that criteria list."
Cincinnati continues on that climb toward the top Sunday against the 1-6 Titans at 1 p.m. ET.
