title: Bengals DC Al Golden Disappointed For, Not In, Shemar Stewart
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals defensive coordinator Al Golden voiced his disappointment in wake of 2025 first-round pick Shemar Stewart being a healthy scratch Sunday in Baltimore .
But Golden’s disappointment wasn’t with Stewart. It was for him.
“I'm not discouraged at all in Shemar. I'm really not,” Golden said. “I think that was unfortunate. I was really hoping to see him take a big jump last week, and I have the same hope as I sit here today.
“I'm disappointed for him,” he added. “This has been a hard start.”
Not just a difficult start to his season, but a rough start to Stewart’s career.
The damage during his rookie year was self – or agent – induced, as Stewart held out for the entire offseason in a squabble over language in his contract.
By the time he signed at the start of camp, he had a lot of catching up to do. He could have got there, but more injuries followed, resulting in him playing just eight games and 280 snaps.
Stewart’s timeline flipped this year, with him taking part in every offseason session only to suffer a hyperextended knee in the first practice of training camp.
He didn’t practice until Sept. 2, 11 days before the season opener.
Stewart was inactive for Week 1 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Week 3 against the Pittsburgh Steelers and Sunday’s contest in Baltimore.
In the three games he has appeared, he’s barely seen the field, playing five snaps at Houston – all in the fourth quarter – four against the Jacksonville Jaguars and eight against the Miami Dolphins.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor threw his support behind Stewart on Monday.
“He's doing all the right things,” he said. “I mean, he's getting better every week. This is his training camp for the most part. I think he's been doing a great job of practicing.
“We're just in a really tough spot with our inactives right now,” Taylor continued. “Sometimes we're really healthy, sometimes we're beat up at a position where we need another guy up. So unfortunately we just had to pull from the D-line, and it's a really deep D-line group and it's really difficult to choose who's going to be an active there.”
The mounting healthy scratches for Stewart have led some to speculate the Bengals could trade Stewart before the Nov. 10 deadline.
That is not something the team is considering, and Taylor said, without mentioning Stewart specifically, that the reports are fabricated and he doesn't like that his players have to see them on social and traditional media.
"I feel great (about the current roster)," Taylor said when asked about the trade deadline. "I hate that our players have to deal with things that get made up sometimes. That’s a part of it. It’s a fun conversation for people. We really like our guys."
Cedric Johnson, the team’s sixth-round pick in 2024, has moved ahead of Stewart on the depth chart, as has this year’s top pick, second-rounder Cashius Howell, who is taking reps away from Stewart on the edge as well as inside on third down.
But Taylor said he doesn’t want to sit Stewart every week, and Golden made it sound as though they’re planning on playing him Sunday against the Tennessee Titans.
“We just worked him in in the walk-through,” Golden said after the team’s morning  session. “We'll continue to do that this afternoon in practice, and I'm looking for that moment when we don't turn back.”
In addition to the progress the coaches have seen from Stewart, they’ve also been impressed with his attitude despite being in such a difficult position.
“He's been really positive,” Golden said. “He continues to get better, and when it's his turn, the important thing is that he doesn't leave the field again.”

title: Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Revealed to Open Titans Practices
full_text:
The first injury report of Titans week is out for Cincinnati and Tennessee. Joe Burrow's Bengals team is pretty healthy, as the star quarterback and most of the roster enter Week 8 ready to roll. Ja'Marr Chase (rest-ankle) did not practice but it was a precaution after he was spotted in the locker room and is still scheduled to speak on Thursday.
Kyle Dugger (quad) didn't practice and is projected to be out this week, but other than that, no major issues popped up following the Wednesday session. Jordan Battles (hamstring) went limited.
Cam Grandy is taking Erick All's roster spot after the latter suffered a third torn right ACL in his career this past weekend.
"He's just somebody we can rely on," Zac Taylor said about Grandy this week. "Somebody we've got a lot of trust in. He was really a make-it-on-the-roster guy for us, and we were so deep at a lot of spots, we can't keep nine tight ends, as much as we wanted to.
"So he's kind of always been a guy we viewed as a roster guy, and this year just didn't work out, and it was a really tough one for us. And so to get him back, I think, is really critical because he's somebody we've always felt like was a part of this thing, and so happy to get him back, and he's going to help."
Cincinnati could go on a big run over the next few weeks.
They have ESPN FPI's easiest remaining schedule among all 32 teams, and they are power-rating favorites in all 11 games left on the board (53% winning chance against the Chiefs' shortest projection).
Continuing to respond the right way after halftime is crucial to capitalizing on this gift of a closing slate.
"I think, as I said earlier, it just reaffirms we can be as good as we want to be," Taylor said about finishing the win against Baltimore. "That's everybody pulling in the same direction and doing their job. I think that's all I take from it, and the players will take from it."
They can keep showing who they are on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET inside Paycor Stadium.

title: Bengals Star Not Spotted at Practice to Open Titans Preparation
full_text:
Cincinnati is back on the practice field Wednesday, but Ja'Marr Chase didn't appear to join the rest of his teammates. CLNS Media's Mike Petraglia first noted the star wide receiver wasn't present for the team's stretch during the 30-minute period open to the media.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor didn't flag anything on Chase injury-wise Monday or Wednesday, and Chase spoke to the media at his locker on Sunday.
He did not appear to be favoring any type of injury after giving a half-time speech in Cincinnati's 35-13 win over Baltimore.
"We had 15 plays, maybe two or three possessions, and it didn't go our way at all," Chase said about the speech reasoning at his locker. "We had opportunities to get the ball out of our hands. Joe was putting up with too much pressure, and I came in here screaming, saying somebody got to make a play. Somebody got to make a play, and I told the offense we can't look at our defense the whole time. We got to step this s*** up and make something work."
The Bengals' best player has had a slower start to the season by his standards (career-low 11 yards per catch), but hauled in five catches for 62 yards and a score on Sunday.
He now figures to have an injury status on Wednesday's report as Cincinnati lost Erick All (knee) to injured reserve and is working Kyle Dugger (quad) back from injury on week-to-week status.
Chase played just 15 snaps against Jacksonville in Week 4 due to a concussion but had been healthy other than that.
"I thought I was really fine. But after seeing the video, I felt like it was more like a whiplash concussion from just my neck being hit side to side," Chase noted about the ailment last week. "I don't think it was anything too crazy from a player. No dirty play. I just think it was maybe a reaction of him trying to grab me or something like that. I can't say he was trying to play dirty at the end of the day."
He is scheduled to speak to the media on Thursday afternoon.

title: Zac Taylor Drops Positive Injury Update to Open Titans Practices
full_text:
Zac Taylor and his team are running back onto the practice field this afternoon after the Week 7 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Cincinnati unfortunately had to put Erick All (knee) on season-ending injured reserve with his third career torn right ACL, and Kyle Dugger (quad) isn't playing this week against Tennessee.
Other than that, Cincinnati doesn't have many injury issues to worry about. Names like WR Andrei Iosivas (finger) and CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) have both been out the minimum four weeks on short-term IR.
They should be back to normal practices soon. It's just been a horrible few days for All, while Dugger is "week to week" with his injury.
"It's awful for him," Taylor said about All. "He's been through this a couple of times before. We'll be there to support him in his recovery and rehab. But it just sucks for him. This means so much to him. He's worked so hard to get himself back."
The Bengals are currently the seventh seed in the AFC as they keep trying to push for an AFC North title.
They are 3-2 in the AFC and cannot afford a loss to the one-win Titans. Bottling the second-half output from Sunday and sprinkling it into every game moving forward won't hurt the Bengals' chances of contending this season.
"I just am really proud of our guys, to be flat out honest with you," Taylor said about beating Baltimore. "I am just proud of the way they responded. When you coach, and you're in that position, and you think you know how they're going to respond, but to just see everybody step up at every position, every coach, and respond that way on the road in the second half – it just makes you really proud, and that's what makes you fired up. It's nothing more than that. It's your team responding the right way and putting together a significant win, and it fires you up."
Cincinnati's defense has been so much better in 2026 compared to last season.
The Bengals rank 11th in the NFL in EPA/play allowed (26th last season).
"If we're going to continue to be great in the red zone and really good at short yardage, it's going to be really difficult for people to put points up on the board, and we got to take a lot of pride in that," Taylor said. "And sometimes it's after long drives where you've been on the field for eight minutes, and it's defeating because they've converted third downs and gotten big plays, and you got to overcome adversity, and then you got to just buckle up and hold them to a field goal."
Cincinnati takes on the Titans at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: Bengals Land Two Conference Player of the Week Awards in Rare Scenario Across Team History
full_text:
The Bengals boast a pair of AFC Players of the Week following the 35-13 Week 7 win over Baltimore. Joe Burrow is the AFC Offensive Player of the Week, and Ryan Rehkow is the AFC Special Teams Player of the Week.
UPDATE: Burrow also won FedEx Air Player of the Week.
According to our Jay Morrison, it marks the ninth time Joe Burrow has won the weekly award, and he is tied with former Bengals NFL MVP Boomer Esiason for the most in team history.
This is the second time in team history Cincinnati has had two players of the week from one game. They also pulled it off in 1994 (Jeff Blake and Doug Pelfrey were honored following a 20-17 OT win against Seattle).
The Bengals' most-important player went 22-for-30 through the air for 292 yards and four passing touchdowns in the Baltimore win. Burrow's 91.5 ESPN QBR ranked third among all passers in Week 7 behind Sam Darnold and Malik Willis.
"Yes, we know who we are, we know who we have to be, and we let our big-time players go and make big-time plays. That's what the NFL is all about. You can do all these different things, but at the end of the day, you just have to go make plays. You have to execute what's called, and that's what we did," Burrow said on Sunday after the win. "That's who we got to be; that's who we got to be. Let our guys go make some big-time plays [and] efficient in the run game. [The] offensive line played great. But yes, we just have to continue to do what we did in that second half. We got that feeling, [and] we have to keep building on it."
Rehkow is the first Bengals punter to earn the award since Kevin Huber did it in 2013.
The booming punter was lights out with his four punts for an average of 46 yards. All four pinned Baltimore inside their own 20-yard line, and he had a long of 56 yards in the game.
Evan McPherson also won a Special Teams Player of the Week award for Cincinnati this season.

title: Referee Report: Bengals Look To Snap Losing Streak with White Hat They Know Well
full_text:
Brad Allen and the Cincinnati Bengals are really starting to get to know each other.
Allen will be the head referee for Sunday’s Ring of Honor game against the Tennessee Titans, marking his fifth Bengals assignment since the Week 3 Monday night game against the Washington Commanders in 2024.
That’s five assignments in a span of 39 games. That’s the most of any referee in the league.
The Bengals have lost all four of the previous games and are 4-7 overall with Allen, who is one of the rare NFL officials who began his career as a head referee, joining the league in 2014 after working for the ACC.
The most recent Cincinnati game Allen worked was the 24-0 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 15 last year. The other losses on the current skid were last year at Green Bay, 2024 at the Los Angeles Chargers and the Washington game earlier that season.
Allen and his crew are averaging 15.17 accepted penalties per game, which ranks fifth most in the league.
Last year, Allen ranked last in the league with just 10.13 accepted penalties per game. And in 2024 he was 11th (12.18).
His 3.83 offensive holding penalties per game are fifth most in the league, and his 1.17 unnecessary roughness flags rank second.
Allen and his crew were banned from the playoffs in 2023 after the infamous “failed to report” incident with the offensive linemen in the Dallas-Detroit game.
In the crew’s return to the playoffs in 2024 in a game between the Packers and Eagles, Allen and his crew made another controversial call, ruling that a fumble that appeared to be recovered by Green Bay kick returner Keisean Nixon was recovered by the Eagles.
They stuck with the call even after the review showed the ball had definitively been recovered by Nixon.
There were some calls for another ban last season, but Allen and his crew worked the AFC Wild Card game between the Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars.
Allen has earned seven postseason assignments in his 12 seasons. All have been Wild-Card round games except for 2017 when he called a Divisional game between the Steelers and Jaguars.

title: Bengals' Week 7 Performance Increases the Odds of a Very Special Season
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals' 35-13 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday was the tale of two halves.
Zac Taylor's squad did not have the ideal start, as they were looking to avoid a 0-2 start against the AFC North. Heading into the locker room for halftime, the Bengals trailed 13-0.
However, in the second half, the Bengals looked like a completely different team, scoring 35 unanswered points against their bitter rival.
A performance like the one on Sunday doesn't happen when just one unit is having a good day. The Bengals dominated in every facet of the game. Now, the numbers are reflecting a team that's looking to make a special run.
Aaron Schatz of FTNFantasy has shared that after the Bengals' Week 7 performance, the team has jumped to second in DVOA (Defense-adjusted Value Over Average) rankings, only behind the San Francisco 49ers.
Schatz has graded the Bengals as a top-10 team in all three phases of the game. The defense really was the unsung hero in Sunday's win.
With the offense sputtering its wheels in the first half, the defense didn't allow the Ravens to jump too far ahead, allowing just 13 points. The rest is history, as the unit didn't allow another point for the rest of the game.
Schatz also shared a deep dive into the postseason chances of every team after Week 7. In those playoff scenarios , Schatz gives the Bengals an 8% chance to win the Super Bowl and a 16.6% chance to win the AFC Championship.
But the biggest headline in this thorough explanation of postseason chances is that fans may get to see some Super Bowl revenge.
One of the potential Super Bowl matchups listed by Schatz gives the Bengals a 6.7% chance to take on the 49ers.
The 49ers and the Bengals have met in the big game twice, with San Francisco bringing home the trophy both times in Super Bowls XXIII and XVI.
Super Bowl talk may be premature with so much time left in the season. However, the numbers are already showing a lot of love for the Bengals' postseason chances.
All summer long, it felt like the message from this team was that this season was an "all-in" type of season. November is going to be a big month for the Bengals, and by the end of it, these postseason chances could be a lot larger.

title: Bengals Should Maximize Offense With Star Eagles Running Back Trade
full_text:
The Bengals need to beef up the rushing attack ahead of the 2026 NFL Trade Deadline on Nov. 10. One way to do it is by plucking Saquon Barkley off the Eagles' flailing roster.
Spotrac's Michael Ginnitti thinks it's a not-so-crazy idea to pursue the former First-Team All-Pro rusher.
He's got a lot of wear on his tires since 2018, but Cincinnati just needs the 29-year-old to be great for this stretch run and into the playoffs to snag a Super Bowl this season.
"The Eagles are currently operating within 'year-from-hell' confines, despite remaining largely competitive on the field for the first half of the season," Ginnitti wrote. "This is not an organization known for 'selling' in any capacity, but GM Howie Roseman has his hands on almost every trade, even if just to be an innocent bystander at times.
"It seems plausible that RB-needy teams will reach out here in the coming days, and both Barkley & Colts’ RB Jonathan Taylor will be coveted options. It should also be noted that the Bengals aren’t exactly known across the league as 'buyers', but an offseason move for Dexter Lawrence, and a healthy, motivated Joe Burrow have us thinking crazy here."
Ginnniti broke down the trade financials below:
Cincinnati would acquire Saquon Barkley at 3 years, $36M, partially guaranteed through 2027.
2027: $16M ($2.5M guaranteed)
Philly would take on dead cap hits of $9M this season, and another $26.4M in 2027 ($13M lost).
Barkley has cap hits of $13.1 million in 2027 and $17.3 million in 2028. The latter number would be tough to fit in with Cincinnati's other stars, but some cap headaches following a Super Bowl run this year would be a great problem to have.
Cincinnati sports the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL and has to beef up this lone weakness on the offense. Barkley could bring an explosive rushing factor that no one else on the roster has. He's posted career-highs of 5.7 yards per carry and 3.81 average yards after contact this season.
Compare that latter number to Chase Brown's 2.54 mark so far, and you get a huge upgrade. Cincinnati should package together its projected third-round 2027 compensation pick with another asset and make the Eagles say no.

title: Will Browns Make QB Changes? Monken’s Recent Comments Leave Things Up in the Air
full_text:
Second-year quarterback Dillon Gabriel is officially off the injury report and back in the lineup for the Cleveland Browns.
Gabriel, who the Browns selected in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, began the year on IR dealing with a back injury.
But how will his return shape up the quarterback room? Even Todd Monken is unsure as the question arose.
Todd Monken on how Dillon Gabriel's activation might change the QB order on Sunday: 'I haven't gotten there yet.'
Despite the young pup being available, it is no question the Browns will stick with Deshaun Watson as their starting quarterback.
Watson currently leads the NFL in game-winning drives with five. Currently, he is on track to get himself a brand-new deal to remain the Browns' starter after this season.
However, that is a different story. The main question with Gabriel being back with the team is where he fits.
Without the former Heisman candidate, the Browns had a nicely set depth chart with Watson as the starter, Shedeur Sanders as the backup, and rookie Taylen Green as the third string.
The reason why it worked so well was that Sanders is getting to learn from Watson as the backup, with Green as a possible option to bring in on plays the Browns want to utilize his athleticism.
Now, where does Gabriel fit? Clearly, Monken favors Sanders to be the backup, and with talks of potentially bringing in Green for designed plays, does that mean Gabriel is the fourth string?
While he will most likely slot in above Green, it does bring up another question.
Will the Browns look to deal Gabriel before the NFL trade deadline?
Let's say the Browns want to move on from Gabriel. Where could they send him and what could they get in return?
The best scenario for both parties is a situation where a team just lost their starting quarterback to injury. In that case, Gabriel would get the chance to actually compete for a starting job, and the Browns could get a slightly better package from a QB-needy team.
At the moment, a team that comes to mind would be the Philadelphia Eagles.
A potential package that could benefit the Browns could be sending Gabriel and a pick for tight end Dallas Goedert. This would fill a need of backup tight end for the Brown and Orange, while capitalizing on trading a young player.
As for now, Gabriel remains with the Browns and will find a spot to sit until something changes internally.
Who knows, maybe a team has had their eye on Gabriel since his time at Orgeon and believe in the 25 year old.
Regardless, it's time for the Browns to cut ties with the Hawaii native, who has shown disinterest in playing for the Browns. It truly does not seem like Gabriel is needed or fits on the team any longer.

title: This Rookie Breakout Gives the NFL's Most Exciting Team a Major Boost Offensively
full_text:
With the 24th pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, the Cleveland Browns selected wide receiver KC Concepcion.
The former Texas A&M Aggie was a standout in college, recording a whopping 185 receptions, 2,218 receiving yards, 431 rushing yards and 28 total touchdowns across three seasons of ball.
But just a few picks after selecting Concepcion, the Browns decided to add another talented wide receiver to the draft class, selecting Washington Husky Denzel Boston. Boston, unlike Concepcion, was more of a deep threat, providing the Browns with a 6-foot-4, 215-pound frame.
KC Concepcion is currently on pace for 73 catches for 800 yards Denzel Boston is currently on pace for 50 catches and 900 yards Just fantastic production from your two rookie wide receivers #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/FvyDtjQAJh
He was never popping off the stat sheets, but was just a reliable go-to option, especially in the red zone.
To begin their careers in the orange and brown, though, Boston stole the spotlight.
He was just downright dominant in the Browns' first few games of the season, hauling in 16 receptions for 330 yards and three touchdowns over five games . Those numbers were good enough for a whopping 20.6 yards per reception.
Concepcion may have been taken off the board a few picks earlier, but Boston was standing out as the steal of the draft.
However, that was, until Week 7 of the NFL regular season.
Concepcion went off against the Tennessee Titans , slashing through the defense time and time again as he hauled in eight receptions for 129 yards. He averaged 16.1 yards per reception and recorded a long of 32 yards.
Every time it seemed like he would go down, though, he fought for more yards and routinely extended plays.
Highest catch rate vs man coverage among WR this season (min 10 man targets) Garrett Wilson         92.9% KC Concepcion       84.6% Chris Olave               82.4% CeeDee Lamb          75.0% Tee Higgins               72.7% pic.twitter.com/unfryUQ1OI
"I play this game with so much heart, so much effort. I'm finally glad that Browns fans and the Browns community was finally able to see what I can bring to this team," he said after Sunday's game concluded.
His efforts out on the gridiron helped guide the team to a fifth victory of the season, with the Browns now sitting 5-2 overall.
With Boston and Concepcion emerging as threats and complementing each other’s games, the rest of the squad only stands to benefit. More opportunities will come the way of Jerry Jeudy and Harold Fannin Jr. as defenses shift their attention toward the two playmakers, creating a snowball effect.
From there, teams will have to adjust to the passing attack, led by Deshaun Watson, which will in turn open up Cleveland's rushing game.
As Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson return from injury and slowly get back to form, they will have an opportunity to capitalize on those openings and round out the offense nicely.
"It's been a little bit of an up-and-down challenge," head coach Todd Monken said about the Browns' offense. "But that's the NFL, as you try to find your way to be consistent. We're always under construction."
With Concepcion finally finding his form, the Browns have a perfect storm following them as they look to maintain the top spot in the AFC North.
This coming weekend, the Browns will clash with the Pittsburgh Steelers as the two sides face at Acrisure Stadium. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. EST on Sunday, Nov. 1.

title: 3 All-Time Worst Cleveland Browns Moves at the NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
When discussing failed trades and the Cleveland Browns, a number of well known names immediately pop up, beginning with the team’s current starting quarterback .
However, when it comes to midseason trades Cleveland’s history is nowhere near as bad, as the team is usually much less active than during the offseason.
With that in mind, here are the Browns’ three worst moves before the NFL trade deadline:
Back in October of 2024, Cooper was the team’s best wideout. He was coming off a personal best 1,250-receiving yard 2023 campaign which led to his fourth Pro Bowl nod, and was the club’s leader six weeks into the season with 24 catches for 250 yards and two scores on 53 targets.
However, Cooper was also on the final year of his deal, and at 30 years old, the Browns were seemingly not interested in extending him beyond that season. Additionally, the team was eager to force more targets towards their shiny new offseason acquisition, wideout Jerry Jeudy, who had cost the team a fifth- and a sixth-rounder in the 2024 Draft. At that point, Jeudy had caught 20 balls for 248 yards and one score off 36 targets.
While Jeudy earned Pro Bowl honors that year in Cleveland thanks to a personal-best 1,229 receiving yards, Cooper struggled with the Bills -- who handed over a 2025 third-rounder and a 2026 seventh-rounder for him and a sixth- -- catching just 20 balls for 297 yards and two scores in eight games for Buffalo.
What wasn’t known at the time was that Jeudy’s production would fall off a cliff in 2025, leading to him becoming an afterthought in the Browns’ current offense, behind rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston.
Yes, Cooper’s compensation was generous given that he failed to leave a mark with the Bills, but there’s no way of knowing if Cooper’s production would have declined so sharply had he not been sent away. And the immediate result was a 2025 offensive unit with the worst wide receiver room in the whole NFL, led by Jeudy and his constant dropped passes, which in turn gave way to the team picking up two wideouts within their first three picks in this year's draft while putting Jeudy squarely in the middle of intense trade speculation in the process .
Meanwhile, Cooper’s compensation would eventually turn into third-round quarterback Dillon Gabriel, currently third on Cleveland’s depth chart after a failed stint as a rookie starter.
During the same 2024 campaign, Cleveland showed the door to another veteran they would end up missing -- enough to try to sign him again this past offseason.
Smith had arrived in Berea via trade in 2023 fresh off a Pro Bowl appearance for the Vikings, his third overall. The cost? Two fifth-rounders for Smith, a sixth- and a seventh-.
He immediately proceeded to start all 16 games that year, posting 5.5 sacks along with 20 quarterback hits and eight tackles for a loss. That led to the Browns signing Smith to an extension before the 2024 season worth $23.5 million over two years, with the team believing they had found the perfect complement for Myles Garrett.
Nonetheless, things started to unravel pretty quickly for the team that year thanks to a 2-7 start and Smith -- who had recorded five sacks up until that point -- was shipped away to Detroit along with a seventh-rounder for a fifth- and a sixth. Smith managed four more sacks for the Lions, finishing his season with nine.
Fast forward to 2026 with the Browns’ inviting Smith to come out of retirement for a tryout after the team dealt Garrett away in the offseason, only for Smith to ironically choose to sign with the Falcons instead , now headed by his former head coach with the Browns, Kevin Stefanski.
Perhaps Cleveland would have just been better off honoring the two-year deal they had with Smith in the first place.
Unlike the previous two instances, Cleveland messed up in this instance by buying, not selling.
At the time, Collins was an up-and-coming young defensive talent on one of the most dominant teams in the league, the Patriots. On the flipside, Cleveland was awful, coming out of a 3-13 campaign that led to the firing of then head coach Mike Pettine and replacing him with Hue Jackson.
The Browns started ‘16 at 0-8 and in shocking fashion went out and acquired Collins -- whom the Patriots did not want to pay top dollar for -- in return for a third-rounder. Cleveland would finish that year at 1-15.
Next, Collins would secure a four-year $50 million deal, only to miss 10 games of the 2017 winless campaign due to a concussion and knee injury.  Collins would start every game in 2018, logging 104 total tackles along with four sacks, but the Browns would end up cutting him during the next offseason after failing to find a willing trade partner for the linebacker.
To this day, it’s still a mystery why an 0-8 team wouldn’t have opted to add draft capital at the deadline instead of spending.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Colts Fire Sale: Where the Cleveland Browns Can Enter the Picture
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts are blowing things up.
On Tuesday, Oct. 27, the Colts' front office decided to trade away future Hall of Fame offensive lineman Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and standout defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers.
With both still in the heart of a great career, the Colts moved them to load up on draft capital as they enter a rebuilding period.
Unfortunately for them, but fortunately for other teams across the league, such big swings being made the organization is in fire sale mode. Now, the door is open for teams to start throwing offers in.
The Cleveland Browns, sitting 5-2 on the campaign and in the hunt for a playoff spot here in a few months, should enter the picture and give the Colts a call about two players.
The Browns' defensive line is already good enough as is , with tackles Mason Graham and Maliek Collins leading the way in the sack column to begin the year. The outside, featuring a combination of Jared Verse, Isaiah McGuire, Sam Williams and Derek Barnett, seems to be really solid as well.
However, adding a player like Stewart is something the team should consider.
Coming in at 33 years old, he is approaching the end of his career, but would bring that experience and some more pop to the Browns' line.
Heading into the final year of his contract, the Browns could land him as a playoff piece, giving them the opportunity to remain competitive in a loaded AFC North.
He will provide the team with more depth at a banged-up position, while also helping lead a young room behind closed doors. He would give the team flexibility to shift bodies around if another Graham-type injury occurs.
When the year concludes, the Browns can let him walk to free back up that roughly $14 million in cap space , or sign him to a cheaper deal to retain him moving forward.
With Buckner going relatively cheap, Stewart would likely command a third or fourth round pick, which is something Cleveland's front office should be comfortable giving up if it means they become that much better on the line.
Outside the hashes and down the field, things have been dicey for the Browns this season.
While future Hall of Fame cornerback Denzel Ward has maintained his consistency , the likes of Tyson Campbell, Mekhi Blackmon and Toriano Pride Jr. have had their ups and downs.
To fully round out the unit, the Browns should consider adding in another body to balance out the productivity, especially considering the front office let Martin Emerson Jr. walk this past offseason.
The Colts, being in the spot they are now, could be looking to move Charvarius Ward, who is sitting on a $24 million cap hit for the rest of the season. Being a free agent in 2027, he is likely to walk, as the Colts usher in a new era.
For the Browns, pairing Ward with Ward and Campbell would be a perfect way to round-out the defensive back room.
The Browns have plenty of draft capital available, and if they threw a fourth- and sixth-round pick to Indianapolis, it should get the deal done. Just a few weeks back, the Dallas Cowboys sent a second- and fourth-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for Joey Porter Jr.
Ward hasn't been able to replicate his successes from his days with the 49ers, but still possesses good intangibles.
At 6-foot-1, 196 pounds, he runs a 4.44 forty and owns an 11-foot broad jump.
The Browns may try to run with what they have on the roster right now, but if both Ward and Stewart are on the board still at the trade deadline, they should at least explore what the moves would require giving up.

title: How the Browns Run Game Can Find New Life Following Injury Bug
full_text:
Last Sunday, the Browns won their fifth game of the season over the Titans, something they did not accomplish until Week 18 of last season. Led by Deshaun Watson, who passed for over 300 yards for the first time in his Cleveland career, the Browns offense was firing on all cylinders.
In the pass game, it was rookie KC Concepcion who led the team with 129 receiving yards, Harold Fannin Jr. rumbled his way past 90 yards, and Dylan Sampson contributed nicely also. Those 300+ passing yards should not overshadow the best game that Cleveland has had rushing the ball all season, though.
With Quinshon Judkins and Sampson both back and healthy in the backfield, it completely changes the Cleveland offense.
Sampson missed the past five weeks with a knee injury he suffered in Week 1 vs. Jacksonville, but came back and contributed very nicely in his nine touches. He totaled 77 yards (45 rushing, 32 receiving) and was using his speed to get outside on runs and swing passes to glide upfield. To see Sampson on the field gives defenses a whole other piece of the offense to worry about with the young receivers and bowling ball of a tight end.
Judkins has been nagged with injuries throughout the season but came back healthier than ever on Sunday. He rushed for 96 yards on 17 carries and two touchdowns , but the best indicator he’s healthy was that he hit 21.01 miles per hour on a run, the fastest he's run all season. Those 96 yards were the second-highest mark Judkins has hit in a game in his young Cleveland career, and the retooled offensive line gave him a great chance on each play.
For reference, last season the Browns had the lowest rushing yards before contact per carry in the league at 0.59, as Cleveland backs were getting contacted almost immediately at the line. The team was also among the highest in the league in rushing yards after contact, which gives more credit to Judkins breaking tackles and fighting for extra yards.
In Week 7, though, those numbers were flipped, as Cleveland led the league in rushing yards per play with 6.3 and got 2.43 yards before being contacted by a Tennessee defender, the sixth-highest mark by a team in the week.
Cleveland got some big pops running behind the left side of that line, led by Spencer Fano , Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins, and Blake Whiteheart. With that o-line finding its footing and two healthy great options at back, the run game for the Browns could be turning a corner that will provide great balance to this offense.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Browns DT Room is Set, but the Edges Could Get a Boost With These 3 Trades
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have flipped the script on the season and could be looking to be buyers at the trade deadline to maintain their first-place standing in the AFC North. They could use offensive line help, but players like Quentin Nelson are not typically available at the deadline.
The Browns could use a bolster at defensive end, and there are several options that could be good fits.
The defensive line has been good as a whole, and they are second in the NFL with 20 sacks. However, an improvement at the defensive end position could make them even better. The current starters are Jared Verse and Isaiah McGuire.
Verse came in as a reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year, but he has had zero sacks this season. McGuire got his chance to start after an injury to Alex Wright, and he has performed solidly with three sacks.
The defensive end group is rounded out by Derek Barnett and Sam Williams, both acquired after roster cut downs due to the Wright injury. The Indianapolis Colts shipped off DeForest Buckner for a fourth-round pick, in which the Browns have three in 2027 . These defensive ends can help elevate the Browns’ strength to be even more dominant:
. @JFowlerESPN lists the Browns as a fit to trade for: - EDGE Khalil Mack - EDGE Jermaine Johnson - EDGE YaYa Diaby pic.twitter.com/Eau26cu7Ew
The former All-Pro has three sacks in six games this season . He is 35 years old and is in the last year of his contract. Mack is similar to Buckner, and at most, a fourth-round pick should be sufficient to land him.
The Browns’ defense has a lot of leaders on it, but they are inexperienced. Mack has seen everything an NFL offense can throw at him, and he can share his knowledge with the rest of the unit.
Johnson is on a lowly Titans team that should be selling off parts to get as much as draft capital as possible. He has three sacks and has played in every game this season. He is a free agent after the season and could be a nice depth piece to down the stretch.
He can be had for a late-round pick and maybe even a pick swap in the Browns' favor. He is only 27 years old, and if he puts together a solid last half of the season for the Browns, then they can re-sign him to a longer deal to stabilize the position.
The Buccaneers may be sellers, as their season has not played out the way they had hoped after extending Baker Mayfield. Diaby has three sacks for the Buccaneers this season and is 27 years old. Diaby was a third-round draft pick of the Buccaneers and has 22 career sacks.
Diaby is in the last year of his rookie contract, and like Johnson, if he is productive, then he can be eligible for an extension.
The Browns' defensive line has caused a lot of havoc in the backfield this season, but most of that pressure is coming from the interior. They could use some help on the outside to provide containment when a quarterback tries to escape.
The run defense has struggled this season when Grant Delpit or Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has not played close to the line of scrimmage. An addition of a run-stopping defensive end can free them up to play in coverage.
These players would not take much in return for a trade, and the Browns have plenty of ammunition to obtain their services. The young roster has arrived at least a year early, and they should consider a trade to help win the division this year .

title: Browns May Have Found Football’s Next Dynamic Duo in These Two Rookies
full_text:
Coming into the 2026 NFL Season, the Cleveland Browns were in desperate need of wide receiver help.
Luckily for the organization, they were able to draft KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston in this past year's NFL Draft.
Seven weeks into their young careers, Concepcion and Boston are already proving that they are poised to be the NFL's next dynamic duo.
KC Concepcion is currently on pace for 73 catches for 800 yards Denzel Boston is currently on pace for 50 catches and 900 yards Just fantastic production from your two rookie wide receivers #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/FvyDtjQAJh
In the first seven weeks, each receiver has put up some big-time performances for the Browns.
For Boston, he leads all rookie receivers in touchdowns with three. Meanwhile, Concepcion is coming off a dominant game where he had eight receptions for 129 yards.
The two receivers rank second and third in total receiving yards, only behind the first receiver drafted, which was Carnell Tate.
Looking at the pace, both guys are projected to get close to that 1,000-yard mark. If they keep up the production they have had, there is no doubt they could both reach quadruple digits in their first season.
As long as the injury bug doesn't come around too often or severely, Cleveland has their wide receiver room set for the foreseable future with the two rookies and second year man Isaiah Bond.
It's all just a matter of who the quarterback is.
If the Browns can find a top-tier guy, they will have the chance to put together a team that can win lots of games, go on playoff runs, and maybe just try and compete for that coveted championship.
Regardless, having multiple great receiving options means whoever does inevitably take over the offense will have help. It does not fully matter if the Browns have a top quarterback or not.
Outside of Boston and Concepcion, the Browns have had back to back phenominal draft classes.
Some other big names the Browns have drafted in the past two season are:
If the Browns can figure out a quarterback that can take them to the playoffs in the near future, they can capitalize on all these star players being on their rookie contracts.
It's also a good time to note that they just traded for Jared Verse, who was drafted in 2024 and won DROY after his rookie campaign.
While Deshaun Watson has been winning games, how sustainable is the injury-prone 31-year-old? Now more than ever, Cleveland truly is a quarterback away.
After the 2025 NFL Draft, I thought the Browns had to have just gotten lucky by getting so many great players. Then, they clearly did it again.
Something has changed in the front office, and Andrew Berry is seeing prospects clearer than ever.
Now is a great time to be reminded that Cleveland has 11 picks in the upcoming 2027 NFL Draft . Not only do they have two first-round picks, but over the past two seasons have been known to trade up and down and move all around the board while collecting more and more assets.
What if the Browns have another winning draft?
The future is clearly bright for a team with such a dark past. Cleveland, it's time to get excited.

title: Denzel Ward Reached a Major Career Milestone in Browns Win Over the Weekend
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns improved to 5-2 over the weekend , which is tied for their best start since 1999, and the game was an offensive explosion for the Browns. Cleveland totaled 491 yards on the day (308 passing, 183 rushing), easily their highest mark of the season so far.
Deshaun Watson was tossing the rock to almost everyone on offense, leading to breakout games from KC Concepcion and Harold Fannin Jr. primarily. While the attention should be on the offense for shattering through, on the other side of the ball, there was an achievement that should not go unnoticed.
Denzel Ward picked off Tennessee quarterback Cam Ward (no relation) in a pivotal spot of the game in the second quarter. The Titans had just gotten the ball off a Fannin fumble at the Browns' 44-yard line, and on the first play after the turnover, Ward stepped in front of Elic Ayomanor to snatch it right back. The Browns then drove down 78 yards and capped it with a Quinshon Judkins touchdown to level the score at 14.
This interception was Ward’s 20th career pick , passing Joe Haden on the Browns all-time list up to spot 15. Only 14 other Browns players have amassed that 20-pick mark, but as we know, when you are as good as Ward is on the outside, teams will avoid him.
That avoidance doesn’t stop Ward from racking up other key defensive statistics, as he is Cleveland’s all-time leader in passes defended with 110, a feat he achieved last season, and is also top 10 in solo tackles with 309.
Ward has kept up his Pro Bowl-level play throughout his career; in his ninth season in the league, he is the highest-graded cornerback in the NFL this season, per PFF.
While the Browns have shipped away notable players like Myles Garrett on defense and parted ways with others in free agency, Ward has been the mainstay who was worthy of the fourth overall pick. His five Pro Bowl selections are the most by a cornerback in Browns history, and his play this year is calling for a sixth.
Cleveland recognized that in the offseason, keeping him home with an extension until 2029 . One of the franchise’s best cornerbacks still plays like he is trying to earn a spot each and every week, though. He continues to be the leader of that secondary, which is putting up another great season defending the pass, as they rank in the top 10 of the NFL in fewest passing yards allowed per game (201.7) and per play (5.5).

title: Andre Szmyt is Forcing Browns Ownership To Put Their Money Where Their Mouth Is
full_text:
Andre Szmyt has done his job.
On Sunday, Oct. 25, the Cleveland Browns took down the Tennessee Titans on the road at Nissan Stadium 27-24 , with Szmyt kicking his third game-winning field goal this season. Now, on the campaign, he has been directly responsible for sending the Browns home with wins against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football, the Baltimore Ravens and the Titans.
Since Post-1999, Szmyt now ranks second in Browns game-tying or go-ahead field goals in the final two minutes of a contest, trailing just legendary kicker Phil Dawson with 10.
Szmyt, himself, has a total of five.
Across the last two seasons, Szmyt hasn't just been clutch, but also consistent. He has made 38 of his 43 attempts, good enough for an 88.4% completion rate , while also knocking through 36 of his 38 attempts on PATs.
Post-1999 #Browns game-tying/go-ahead FGs in final 2 minutes: 🔸Phil Dawson (10) 🔸Andre Szmyt (5) 🔸Dustin Hopkins (4) Owner Jimmy Haslam called Szmyt a "cornerstone player" this past offseason. Right he was 🥹 (h/t @DanielOyefusi ) #DawgPound https://t.co/TsFWl0tx7X
But with how good Szmyt has been, it is surprising to see how weak a contract he is currently playing on.
This past offseason, the 28-year-old signed a one-year, $1.1 million extension to stay with the organization. After an impressive rookie season, one in which he booted 24 field goals and 25 extra points, one would expect him to see a bigger deal come across the table.
And surprisingly, Browns owner Jim Haslam talked as if he would make the big bucks.
When reflecting on the roster the team built in 2026, a group that was built on youth and first-year players, Haslam spoke highly of Szmyt and many others.
"I think what is important to understand about our rookies, though, and you will see them, you all know them, [is that] they are not only really good players, but they are also really good people," he said. "They will be the cornerstone with which we will build and grow and develop this winning team."
If Szmyt is really a long-term cornerstone for the team, and the front office just wants to see him come out and continue the 2025 success into 2026, now is the time to put the money in front of him.
Consistent and clutch kickers are hard to come by, especially in today's game, so being able to secure one is incredibly important. The Browns, who have routinely gone through kickers since Dawson left the organization back in the early 2010s, should know this better than anyone else.
Szmyt has made as many game-winners as field goals he has missed. If the Browns don't see how valuable that is, other teams will. He has arguably one of the league's most valuable legs.
And if he enters the open market this offseason, some team is going to pay him a hefty sum.
The Browns better hope that they can get to him before then and lock him down as a cornerstone in The Land for the next few years.

title: Browns' 5-2 Start Raises a Major Question About Quarterback Position Future
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ season was supposed to be all about which quarterback to draft in 2027, but that was flipped upside down after a 5-2 start and sitting in first place in the division.
Deshaun Watson has led the offense to five game-winning drives, and the offense will continue to improve in the last 10 games. The Browns will have too many wins to be able to draft a top quarterback, and their other first-round pick from the Los Angeles Rams is expected to be outside of the top 10.
All the winning is fun now, but it leaves the future of the quarterback position in limbo.
They can move on from Deshaun Watson next season, but if he leads the team to the playoffs, then it will be difficult to justify replacing him. He threw for his first 300-yard passing game last Sunday, and the offense looked smooth. If he can continue to put up big numbers and elevate the young players, then the Browns should seriously consider extending him.
However, Watson has not been consistent. Extending him would take into consideration his entire body of work with the Browns, which is incomplete. During his first season in Cleveland, he came off a year-and-a-half gap without playing and could not practice with the team while his suspension was in effect. He then had an unprecedented shoulder injury, led the offense for the Ravens, and suffered two Achilles injuries.
If the Browns feel that he is a long-term solution, then he will cost a lot of money as the price for the position continues to grow. The roster is filled with rookie contracts, so the Browns can afford a new contract next season, but they will need the cap space starting in 2028 to extend their draft picks.
Shedeur Sanders is also the backup, and he was in a competition with Watson for the starting position in training camp. He has been able to observe how Watson prepares and learn Todd Monken’s offense without getting rushed into action. He is on a rookie contract, but the Browns need to figure out if he has enough talent to be able to replace Watson .
The roster is showing that they are ready to win now, and the team cannot take a step back next season because of poor quarterback play.
If they move on from Watson, Sanders may not be the automatic replacement . They activated Dillon Gabriel from the injured reserve list this week, meaning that he has to take a roster spot. The team is 5-2 and the defensive line depth has performed well in addition to special teams. A player will have to be cut to make room for Gabriel.
He has been praised for understanding the offense, but his physical limitations may be too much to overcome. Gabriel was not considered for the starting position at any point this season and does not seem like a viable option to elevate the offense next season.
The Browns drafted Taylen Green in the sixth round, and his physical tools are immeasurable. He is considered very raw for the position and will not be ready to take the keys to the offense next season. His future in the league may be at a different position where his speed can be utilized.
A mid-to-late first-round pick may be an option, but it has to be a quarterback that Todd Monken believes can win. There could also be reclamation projects that can step in for a year or two, but that will not solve the long-term future of the position.
Monken gets a lot of credit for reviving Watson’s career and putting him in good positions to exceed. He is winning with this roster, which nobody expected when he was named the starter. The answer for the position’s future is muddy, but Monken is proving that he should be trusted with the solution.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Clarifies Why His Cowboys-Eagles Press Conference Was Cut Short
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys got a much-needed win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night in a 38-21 finish over their injury-plagued rivals.
After an ugly two-game losing streak that brought with it tons of criticism, the Cowboys had no choice but to respond, or things could have gotten messy fast for head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who lives to see another day as Dallas' head coach.
Following the win in Philadelphia, Schottenheimer spoke with reports for an unusually-short amount of time. The answers were shorter than usual and his demeanor was controlled instead of giddy after a divisional win. The press conference lasted just 4:15 seconds.
When asked if he was good, Schottenheimer simply said, “I’m great. Excited for our guys.”
Once the team got back to Texas on Tuesday, Schottenheimer touched on why his was short with reporters after the game.
It wasn't personal with the media, at least according to him. It's clear his focus on what's ahead given the fact that Dallas still has a strong chance to win the NFC East and host a playoff game.
“No, I’ll be honest. I really do a good job of blocking you guys out," Schottenheimer said, per Jon Machota of The Athletic. "I think it was a big game for us. We’re motivated as a football team. I’m motivated as a head coach to get our guys playing to the standard that I know they’re capable of playing."
“So, no, it was more just my focus was getting the team to be focused and motivated. And I think you saw that (Monday) night, so I’m proud of our group.”
The two-game losing steak has created tons of negative headlines around Schottenheimer and the team, so it's understandable why he would be ready to move on with the press conference instead of laugh and joke with reporters like he often does.
But Schottenheimer admitted he expects the criticism and knows it comes with the job. Being around the NFL for his whole life certainly helps with this.
“Intense game against a real rival. But no, at the end of the day, in this business you get paid to deal with the criticism and things that come with the job and that never (plays a role). Remember, you’re talking to a guy that grew up for 25 years in a household with a head coach in the NFL."
Schottenheimer and the Cowboys will need to remain focused while blocking out the noise as they prepare to host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at 12 p.m. CT.

title: Cowboys & Steelers Linked as Possible Partners For Unlikely Trade By ESPN
full_text:
It's that time of the year where trade conversations are heating up and just about every scenario is being thrown out there. The latest example of that came in a trade idea involving the Dallas Cowboys and Pittsburgh Steelers that was floated by ESPN.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Matt Bowen listed off 25 trade candidates ahead of the deadline on Nov. 10.
Among them was Steelers linebacker Patrick Queen, and Dallas was named among the best fits for him, along with the Buffalo Bills.
The problem with that idea, as Fowler notes, is that the Steelers are unlikely to trade Queen amid a 5-2 start to the season. That made us wonder why he would even be listed in the first place.
"Rumors of a Queen trade persisted in the spring, with the Cowboys among teams that checked on his availability," Fowler said. "He's also a 2027 free agent. But the Steelers' status as a 5-2 team likely keeps him in Pittsburgh."
It is true that the Cowboys were rumored to have interest in a trade for Queen, but the possibility of acquiring him in a trade amounts to a ship that has long sailed.
It's true Queen will be a free agent in 2027, and he has been a big disappointment in Pittsburgh since signing in 2024. However, the Steelers don't have a natural replacement on the roster, so they really have no choice but to keep him.
A trade of Queen was a much more realistic scenario during the offseason, when Pittsburgh had time to find a replacement.
If anything, the Steelers will be buying at the trade deadline, not selling, so Queen isn't going anywhere.
The Cowboys are in good shape with the trio of Jaishawn Barham, DeMarvion Overshown and Dee Winters, and even Shemar James has begun to emerge, and so much so the Cowboys have him sporting the green dot after making a change in Week 7.
As long as that group stays healthy, the Cowboys should be in good enough shape to stand pat at the position.
However, as we've seen, health isn't guaranteed for the Cowboys' linebackers. Overshown has missed five games due to injury and has been injury-prone throughout his career, and Winters is now banged-up and missed last week's game .
If health continues to be an issue at the position, we could see the Cowboys springing for a linebacker trade. But, until Dallas finds itself in a precarious spot, Jerry Jones has bigger fish to fry.

title: Dallas Cowboys RB Javonte Williams Admits Contemplating Retirement Before 'Rebirth'
full_text:
Before he joined the Dallas Cowboys last season, running back Javonte Williams gave serious thought to retiring from the NFL.
Williams entered the league as a second-round pick of the Denver Broncos in 2022, but after having success in his rookie campaign, Williams struggled with injury and ineffectiveness over his final three seasons in Denver.
He would eventually sign a prove-it deal with the Cowboys, but before that, Williams said he thought about retiring.
"I was really about to just hang up the cleats," Williams said on the Downs 2 Business podcast.
Williams admits that he fell back in love with the game upon joining the Cowboys and strongly hinted the coaches stopped believing in him in Denver.
"No disrespect to nobody in Denver or nothing like that, I respect everybody over there, I respect what they got going on," Williams added. "Just coming to Dallas it felt like it's a new awakening. I felt like a rebirth."
"Just leaving there and coming here, the coaches believing in me, everybody just like lifting me up. It kind of felt like UNC all over again. Me just going out there just playing, having fun."
"I just fell in love with the game again. I really had lost love for the game... I had already bought a crib... I'm like I might just start my real estate or something," Williams concluded.
A rebirth is a perfect way to label what Williams has done in Dallas.
There were no shortage of skeptics when the Cowboys made Williams their starting running back after his failures in Denver. However, Williams ultimately proved to be a total steal.
Williams ripped off career-highs in rushing yards with 1,201, and scrimmage yards with 1,338 while also scoring 13 total touchdowns, including 11 on the ground.
For his efforts, the Cowboys re-signed Williams to a three-year, $24 million contract this past offseason.
Williams has had a tougher time over the first seven games this season, but he has remained productive with 472 rushing yards and 103 receiving yards and nine total touchdowns, including eight rushing scores that leads the NFL.
Williams is on pace to shatter both what he posted through the air and his touchdown total from last season.
The Cowboys running back is also coming off his best game of the 2026 campaign after he exploded for 155 rushing yards in Week 7, which was also a career-best mark for him.
Dallas is hoping that is a sign of things to come because the Cowboys desperately need their rushing attack to get going to take some pressure off Dak Prescott and the Dallas air attack.

title: Josh Sweat Trade Rumor Gives Cowboys Asking Price for Cardinals Edge Rusher
full_text:
The one player the Dallas Cowboys have been linked to the most ahead of the NFL trade deadline is Arizona Cardinals edge rusher Josh Sweat.
This past weekend, ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport suggested the Cowboys as a potential landing spot for Sweat. Then, on Wednesday, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that one NFC executive believes the Cowboys and Sweat are a match.
"Sweat to Dallas makes a lot of sense to me," the exec said told Fowler. "That's a profile fit."
There's no doubt the Cowboys should at least explore a trade for Sweat given the lackluster showing from their edge rushers this season, with the group posting just 3.5 sacks combined.
While that's all well and good, price will play a huge factor in just how interested the Cowboys are in making a trade for Sweat.
Speaking of Sweat's price, Johnny Venerable of PHNX Cardinals is reporting that the Cardinals are seeking a "high Day 2 pick."
Venerable also noted that Sweat had previously requested a trade after the team fired former head coach Jonathan Gannon, so it's certainly logical to assume he still wants out.
"The Cardinals are aware of Josh Sweat’s trade market and are believed to be seeking a high Day 2 pick for the veteran pass rusher, per source," Venerable wrote.
"Sweat previously requested a trade following the firing of Jonathan Gannon and is signed through 2028," he added.
Seeing as how there are only two rounds on Day 2 of the NFL Draft, a high Day 2 pick means a second-rounder.
We've previously estimated Sweat at a trade value of a third-round pick, at most, so we don't think Arizona will get a second-rounder.
What is working in the Cards' favor is the fact that the market for edge rushers will be hot, per usual, and the more teams that get involved, the more the price for Sweat could go up.
What also helps is Sweat's history of sack production. He has twice posted double-digit sacks in the past four seasons and hasn't tallied fewer than six since he had four in 2019.
But, in 2026, Sweat is having a down year with just two sacks in seven games, so that certainly won't help his stock.
Another positive is Sweat is under contract for two more years after this one, although he doesn't have any guaranteed money left on his current deal and will almost certainly want that addressed by whoever acquires him.
When you add everything up, a third-round pick is probably the best the Cardinals can hope for, and even then they might be forced to send a pick back in such a deal.
The Cowboys have traded away a lot of picks in recent years and don't have a great situation currently.
Dallas doesn't have a third-round pick in 2027, nor do they have a second-round selection in 2028. If Dallas was to give up its 2027 second-round pick in a trade for Sweat, it would be left with just three selections in next year's draft.
With plenty of competition expected for Sweat's services at the trade deadline, the Cowboys might have a tough time competing against teams with a better stable of picks.

title: Ranking 6 Edge Rushers Dallas Cowboys Should Target Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
We are a shade under two weeks away from the 2026 NFL trade deadline on Nov. 10 and the Dallas Cowboys should be shopping around for help along the edge.
Owner Jerry Jones continues to say he's willing to do something to help the Cowboys' struggling defense and adding an edge rusher should be a to priority.
That's because the Cowboys have goten a measly 3.5 sacks from their edge rushers this season, with Donovan Ezeiruaku tallying 1.5 and Rashan Gary and Malachi Lawrence having one apiece.
Knowing that, here's a look at six edge rushers who could be available, ranked from best to worst.
The Cowboys need to swing for the fences at edge rusher and the five-time Pro Bowler would be the best option to do so after notching double-digit sacks in three of the last four years.
We know the Cowboys tried to trade for Crosby before they lost out to the Baltimore Ravens back in March, and after seeing what has transpired with their lackluster edge rushers room in 2026, Dallas would almost certainly re-visit such a trade.
However, the Raiders haven't been as bad as expected, so Crosby might be content with staying in Las Vegas at this point. Even still, the Cowboys should keep checking in to see if he might be available before Nov. 10.
Projected trade value: First-round pick
There were rumblings during the offseason that Sweat wasn't happy in Arizona , and it's not hard to see why. Not only are the Cardinals rebuilding, Sweat also doesn't have any guaranteed money left on his current deal.
A former Pro Bowler and Super Bowl champ, Sweat has notched 7.5 sacks or more in four of the past five seasons, with two double-digit sack campaigns included in that stretch.
Speaking of that 2024 Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles, Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker was on Philly's staff that year, so there's a connection in Dallas.
The Cowboys continue to be heavily linked to potential interest in Sweat, with ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noting that rival teams "could see him getting moved" and one NFC executive believing that "Dallas makes a lot of sense" as a landing spot for Sweat.
Projected trade value: Third-round pick
The 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers should be open to selling off some pieces as they navigate a lost season. Trading Mack, who is on a one-year deal and could very well retire after this season, definitely makes sense.
Mack is long in the tooth at 35 years old, but he's still capable of making an impact, as evidenced by his three sacks in six games this season. He would also bring a much-needed boost to the culture in Dallas.
Projected trade value: Fourth-round pick
After the New York Jets made a few additions at edge rusher this past offseason, McDonald has seen his playing time dip, so he could be expendable.
McDonald only has two sacks in seven games, but he has shown he's capable of more after posting 18.5 combined over the previous two campaigns.
Along with his past production, the fact that McDonald is under contract through 2027 at a reasonable $14.4 million makes him more attractive.
Projected trade value: Fourth-round pick
With Johnson headed for free agency next offseason, and with the Tennessee Titans going nowhere, he could get moved.
Fowler reports that teams consider Johnson a "toss-up to be traded," while also noting that "teams in the market for an edge rusher believe Johnson could be available at the right price."
Johnson has posted three sacks in 2026, which is double what any of Dallas' edge rushers have. He had a career-high 7.5 in 2023 before suffering a major injury. He has posted six sacks in 21 games since then, including three in 14 games last season.
Projected trade value: Fourth-round pick
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could be sellers at the deadline with another loss or two in the next few weeks and Diaby stands out as a potential trade candidate because he's on the final year of his rookie deal.
Diaby has posted seven or more sacks in two of his first three years in the NFL, and he has three this season, although all of them came last week in a win over the Carolina Panthers.
Projected trade value: Fourth-round pick

title: Dallas Cowboys Insider Believes 'All-In' Jerry Jones Will Make NFL Trade Deadline Deal
full_text:
We are less than two weeks away from the 2026 NFL trade deadline, and one of the teams that everyone will have an eye on is the Dallas Cowboys . Anytime Jerry Jones is involved, you know that something unpredictable can happen, and that could once again be the case despite a slow start to the year.
Dallas snapped a two-game losing streak on Monday night by running through the wounded Philadelphia Eagles in primetime, and now has an opportunity to string together consecutive wins for the first time this season when they welcome the Arizona Cardinals to AT&T Stadium .
If the team can get a small winning streak rolling, the urgency for Jones to swing a deal before the deadline will continue to increase, and that's exactly what Cowboys insider Jane Slater of the NFL Network believes will be the case.
Slater stopped by the Not So Fast podcast with Paul Pabst and Andrew Perloff to share her thoughts on how the deadline could play out for Dallas, and a trade certainly seems to be in the cards .
“I think he’s all in.” - @SlaterNFL thinks Jerry Jones will make a move before the trade deadline. Possibly pass-rush. pic.twitter.com/L9WdQQdJod
"Yes, I think they will. And I think that's because here's the one thing I'll say about Jerry. You know, for the last couple of years, we said the definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over and expecting the same results. Well, this offseason, Jerry was very active, going out and getting you players," Slater said. "Went out, got you the George Pickens.He got you Quinnen Williams. He got you Jalen Thompson. He traded away guys that, at the time, they didn't think fit the scheme, like Osa Odighizuwa.
"I mean, I never thought I'd see Jerry bring in a young first-time [defensive coordinator] into Dallas. And then we're hearing him talk about bringing Troy Aikman in at some point, which I'm like, pigs are flying around here in Dallas. Right. If you guys know the lore between those two. Yeah. And so I think he just, at 84 years old, I think he truly is all in. And I think he still sees disparity despite the two-game lead by the Giants. And I think he thinks that if he can just get that pass rush going, they had two sacks last night. You know, it's like he had the interception from DeMarvion Overshown. The wheels are turning for Jerry. And I think it will be impossible for him not to make a move."
Pass rush remains one of the biggest weaknesses for the Cowboys despite some improvement this weekend, but there is no denying a star player on the edge could take Parker's defense to the next level.
Prior to the season, Maxx Crosby was the hot name, but recently, there have been strong talks about a potential trade with the Arizona Cardinals for star pass rusher Josh Sweat.
We'll have to see how everything plays out over the next two weeks, which includes two very winnable games against the Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts, but if the Cowboys go into the trade deadline on a three-game winning streak, there is no doubt Jones will try to make a splash.

title: Broncos' First Week 8 Injury Report: Updates on Surtain, Hufanga & Waddle
full_text:
The Denver Broncos released their initial Week 8 injury report ahead of Sunday's pivotal home showdown against the Kansas City Chiefs.
Denver listed wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), and defensive end Zach Allen (hip) — all starters — as "DNP" (Did Not Practice) following Wednesday's session.
An earlier report indicated that Waddle suffered a re-aggravation of a prior chest issue toward the end of last week's victory over the Arizona Cardinals, and his status for Sunday's game is to be determined.
The injury occurred on a trick play that head coach and offensive playcaller Sean Payton consequently apologized for.
"Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call? ... It was awful. I'm sorry," Payton said in his postgame press conference on Sunday. "If you look it up, in 2008, in a similar situation — even a more radical reverse — fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play."
Hufanga remains on the wrong side of questionable after missing the last two games due to an ankle injury. The former AFC Defensive Player of the Week will need to get in at least limited practices on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at suiting up versus Kansas City.
Allen's apparently hamstring ailment is a new development, though one that, as of this writing, seems unlikely to hold him out of Week 8 action.
Elsewhere on the injury report, left tackle Garett Bolles (hip) and wide receiver Marvin Mims (ankle) were considered limited, while cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) were full participants.
Surtain appears poised to return from a three-game absence as his ankle presumably is at or near full health.
Of note on the Chiefs' end, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (personal/knee) did not practice on Wednesday while receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) and tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) were full goes.
In the event that Waddle is inactive on Sunday, the Broncos would be down to Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin as its primary wideouts, with Pat Bryant (ankle) still on short-term injured reserve.
Although, in this case, some (more) of the receiving work could be spilled onto running back RJ Harvey's plate, the Broncos may take the opportunity to get the ball in the hands of Mims, which Payton has repeatedly insisted remains a priority on his offensive totem pole.
“I think to his credit, whenever we ask something of him—whether it’s intermediate, down the field—he’s been really effective," he said of Mims on Wednesday. "Obviously as a returner, that first return with the ball midfield, those are... I’ve said this before, the receiving now to start the game. [At] minimum there’s a threshold, but to start where we started, those are things that he’s shown us consistently. He continues to have those touches and then where you want to even get him more touches. It’s sometimes a challenge, but certainly he’s deserving.”

title: Broncos' Most Surprising Trade Candidate Is Hiding in Plain Sight
full_text:
J.K. Dobbins doesn't seem happy at the moment.
The Denver Broncos' veteran running back received a season-low 14 snaps in Week 7's 30-16 win over the Arizona Cardinals. With rookie Jonah Coleman returning from injured reserve, Dobbins took a back seat in the desert, both in snap and touch share.
The Broncos' offense looked different with Coleman on the field , and his versatility as a receiver and as a pass protector gives Sean Payton so much more to work with. When Coleman is on the field, opponents can't be sure whether it's a run or a pass coming, while with Dobbins and RJ Harvey, defenses can play the probabilities more accurately.
In the NFL, it's good not to be predictable. The Broncos have to make the tough decision to continue ceding snaps and touches in Coleman's favor if they have any hope of digging out of being a bottom-10 rushing offense.
Dobbins doesn't appear to be taking this development well, and if he's unable to get his mind right, the Broncos could suddenly become amenable to trading him away . Several teams have serious running back issues right now — including the New York Giants, who've already orchestrated a big trade (quarterback J.J. McCarthy).
The Giants would also make a lot of sense because of head coach John Harbaugh's ties to Dobbins from their time together in Baltimore. Harbaugh drafted Dobbins in the second round back in 2020.
There are other teams in need of some running back help, including the Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers, and maybe even the Carolina Panthers. Dobbins has a long injury history, and while he was dinged up early this season, he's yet to miss a game.
The one fly in the ointment of a potential Dobbins trade is his contract. The Broncos just re-signed him to a two-year, $16 million deal, but only the first year was guaranteed.
That's good and bad. It's good in that a team acquiring him via trade wouldn't necessarily be locked to Dobbins beyond 2026, unless he were to arrive and hit it out of the park.
The bad? A lot of the money gets funneled into Dobbins's 2027 contract. He goes from a $6 million cap number this year to $10 million next year, with a $7 million base salary. That's a solid deal for a mid-level No. 1 running back, but for a second guy in a rotation, it would be a drastic overpay.
Now, it's helpful that nearly half of the 2026 season is over, so the Broncos have already absorbed a good chunk of his contract, and they've already paid out his $4 million signing bonus. That simplifies things somewhat for an interested suitor that's mostly concerned with running back help this season, and less worried about 2027.
With Tyler Badie on injured reserve for three more games, the Broncos would have to really be blown away by an offer to trade Dobbins. They do have Cody Schrader on the practice squad, so if a team made the Broncos an offer they couldn't refuse, there's an immediate running back available to use on game day.
The Broncos love Dobbins. Payton values Dobbins and has given the veteran back a lot of credit for the Broncos' sudden rise in confidence and swagger last year.
Payton's appreciation of Dobbins was reflected last week against the Cardinals. On a drive in which Coleman did the heavy lifting as a runner, moving the chains on two of his three carries, Payton gave the Broncos' only goal-line carry to Dobbins, which he punched in.
However, instead of jumping up and celebrating with his teammates, Dobbins ran straight back to the Broncos' sideline and sat down on the bench. Following the game, he purportedly didn't make himself available to reporters in the locker room, further showing his frustration.
Payton is big on body language. As a leader that guys in that locker room look to, if Dobbins isn't able to get his mind right and frustration continues to show through his body language, the situation could devolve ahead of the November 10 deadline.
But I give Dobbins more credit than that. His disappointment in being rendered second fiddle last week is understandable, but I'd be surprised if we don't see a more chipper energy on Sunday against the Kansas City Chiefs. Character has never been a concern with Dobbins.
Iron sharpens iron, after all, so if Dobbins doesn't want to be the No. 2 running back, it's up to him to prove it on the field. And the Broncos will give him that opportunity, provided he gets his vibe back on point.
I doubt the Broncos trade Dobbins. However, he has become as surprise player to watch, given Coleman's rise, Dobbins's antics last week, and the growing need at running back several teams have ahead of the deadline.
Dobbins is an experienced back, and he's healthy. I could see a needy team calling the Broncos, but again, it would take a serious offer to get Payton and company to give up on the veteran back.
