title: Feel the Pain!: Here’s Where Packers Are in NFL Injury Rankings
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The injury rate in the NFL is 100 percent, as players like to say. Some injuries are more painful than others, though, and the Green Bay Packers have felt the sting of torn ligaments and sprained muscles more than anyone this season.
According to Rotowire , the Packers are the second-most injured team headed into their Week 8 home game against the Carolina Panthers. That’s just the number of injuries, though. The Packers have a lot of star power on their injury lists, and that’s reflected in Rotowire’s Impact Index.
From that perspective, no team is more impacted by injuries this week than Green Bay. That list is headed by All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons and budding star Edgerrin Cooper. Parsons hasn’t played this season due to last year’s torn ACL. The team’s biggest X-factor in replacing Parsons was Cooper, who suffered a torn Achilles in Week 4.
Along with the possibility of standout receiver Matthew Golden missing the game with a shoulder injury, the Packers have three of the 13 most-impactful injuries this week.
Here is the list of key injuries on offense.
Receiver Jayden Reed, the premier slot player who received a contract extension this offseason, suffered a season-ending back injury in Week 2. The Packers have missed his playmaking ability in the intermediate zones and his run-after-catch skill.
Complicating matters, Skyy Moore, who had been Reed’s replacement, is on injured reserve, as well. Savion Wiliams missed the first five games due to an ankle injury but has made a few impact plays upon his return.
What would really complicate matters is if Matthew Golden is out. “I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Tuesday about Golden’s status. He would not have practice on Monday or Tuesday; the team will get on the field for some individual drills on Wednesday, which will be important in determining Golden’s status for the game.
Running back Chris Brooks started the Week 4 game at Tampa Bay but went down with an ankle injury and was placed on injured reserve. Thursday’s game will mark his third game on the sideline.
Tight end Luke Musgrave suffered a neck injury during the offseason practices and there is no estimated time for a potential return.
Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele suffered a season-ending knee injury one play after Reed was injured against the Jets. The Packers signed him to a huge contract extension before last season. By the end of this season, he will have played about 32 percent of the snaps over two years.
Center Sean Rhyan, who was re-signed to a lucrative three-year contract just before the start of free agency, suffered a high-ankle sprain on the fourth snap at Detroit. He might be headed to injured reserve, where he’d join his backup, Jacob Monk.
“We got some time yet before we determine that, I would say,” LaFleur said.
Left guard Aaron Banks never landed on injured reserve but the team’s highly paid left guard has played in 22 snaps this season due to knee and toe injuries.
Here is the list of key injuries on defense.
Edge Micah Parsons remains on the physically unable to perform list due to last year’s torn ACL. He might make his practice debut next week . Without him, the team’s four edge rushers have 5.5 sacks and 64 pressures in seven games. Detroit’s Aidan Hutchinson has five sacks and a league-high 42 pressures in six games.
Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave suffered a torn Achilles at the end of the Chicago game and will miss the rest of the season. He wasn’t great and perhaps not worth the contract, but he had six pressures in four games, which is one more than Devonte Wyatt in seven games.
Defensive tackle Warren Brinson, who looked primed for a Year 2 jump, missed the start of the regular season with a calf injury and then suffered a groin injury during his first week of practice. He’s on injured reserve and might not be back until late in the season.
Defensive tackle Jonathan Ford won a spot on the roster because of his stoutness against the run. He’s on injured reserve with a calf injury. Fortunately for the Packers, Jordon Riley made his season debut at Detroit after missing the first six games following last year’s torn Achilles.
Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper was having a dominant, breakout season before suffering a torn Achilles in Week 4 at Tampa Bay. The Packers are fortunate to have quality backups but Cooper really is that cliché one-of-one player. Even while missing the last three-plus games, he leads the team with six tackles for losses.
Linebacker Zaire Franklin will miss a second consecutive game with an injured shin. He’s the team’s defensive captain.
From that perspective, Green Bay will be facing its kindred spirit on Thursday. According to Rotowire, the Panthers have a league-high $90.0 million of salary cap tied up in injured players. The Packers are on their heels, ranking second with $86.8 million. They are head and shoulders ahead of the rest of the league from the financial component.
The Packers, who are coming off a bitter loss to Detroit last week, were crushed by the Falcons on Thursday night in Week 3. They must shake off the pain and inflict some pain on the Panthers.
“We’ve got to be better than we were last time we played a Thursday night game here at home, and I know we will be,” quarterback Jordan Love said. “So I think, in terms of preparation, it’s always tough on a short week. Everything kind of just gets jam packed.
“And then especially in terms of trying to get your body back, we’ve got a lot of guys that are injured right now. So, it’s always tough. You’re never going to make excuses, but we’ve definitely got to be a lot better than we were last time we played the Thursday game.”

title: With NFL Trade Deadline Approaching, Where Do Packers Need Help?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The NFL trade deadline is Nov. 10, but that didn’t stop two of the Green Bay Packers’ playoff rivals from striking early by plundering the Indianapolis Colts on Tuesday.
The Seattle Seahawks acquired elite left guard Quenton Nelson. The ninth-year pro was a Pro Bowler each of his first eight seasons and a first- or second-team All-Pro in six. The San Francisco 49ers immediately retaliated by landing defensive tackle DeForest Buckner.
What about the Packers? They’ve never been buyers under general manager Brian Gutekunst, but the veteran-centric approach this year suggests this deadline could be different.
Here’s a position-by-position look at the Packers to see where they could be active in the trade market, with where we’d place the need on a 1-to-10 scale.
Absolutely not. The presence of Jordan Love is why the Packers could be buyers.
While the Packers have been linked to Colts standout and former Wisconsin star Jonathan Taylor, they didn’t stick with Josh Jacobs through his legal problems – to the dismay of some of their fans – just to turn around and trade for a running back.
Could the Packers find a better tag-team partner than MarShawn Lloyd and Pierre Strong? Obviously, so maybe that’s where there’s a deal to be made, though that would admit that Lloyd was a bust, which seems unlikely.
Receiver has been a focus of multiple trade deadlines over the years, only for the quarterbacks to be told to make it work with who they’ve got.
Could it be different this year? The Packers gambled at receiver by parting ways with veterans Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks, with the belief that Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Jayden Reed could carry the passing game.
Well, Reed is on injured reserve, and while Watson and Golden have made a bunch of big plays, the passing attack really could use one more consistent, reliable weapon, because no defensive coordinator or cornerback on earth is going to lose a minute of sleep over Savion Williams, Bo Melton or J. Michael Sturdivant. What a difference a sure-handed, intermediate-level route-runner could do for this offense.
Tucker Kraft hasn’t been vintage Tucker Kraft during his comeback season from a torn ACL, and there’s no reason to believe Luke Musgrave is going to return this season, let alone help the team in its playoff push.
Mark Redman (especially), Jonnu Smith and Josh Whyle have provided some value but some more impact in the passing game wouldn’t be a bad thing. If the Eagles are going to surrender, how about Dallas Goedert, who has 22 catches in five games?
The Packers’ projected offensive line was supposed to be Jordan Morgan at left tackle, Aaron Banks at left guard, Sean Rhyan at center, Jacob Monk at right guard and Zach Bako-Bewele at right tackle.
Instead, the Packers played most of Sunday’s game against Detroit with Morgan at left tackle, Laken Tomlinson at left guard, John Williams at center, Travis Glover at right guard and Anthony Belton at right tackle. There could be another change at right guard for Thursday night with Glover banged up.
The Packers have a bunch of decent linemen. Adding another would be of no help whatsoever. A big swing on an above-average starter, however, would make sense. The best of the bunch, obviously, was Nelson, a living legend and Hall of Famer-in-waiting. The Eagles aren’t going anywhere and might be looking to move left guard Landon Dickerson. Tomlinson has been fine and Banks was a zillion-dollar backup last week, but Dickerson would provide some thunder as an interior blocker to help get the run game out of its coma.
For what it’s worth, Dickerson played center during his final two seasons at Alabama.
The Packers emerged from training camp with a seven-strong group at defensive tackle. Three of those players, Javon Hargrave, Warren Brinson and Jonathan Ford, are on injured reserve, though the return of Jordon Riley helped offset the carnage.
That group played well against Detroit, but games are won up front. Whether it’s another run-stopper or someone who can add some juice as a pass rusher, another impact player would help. The Colts traded Buckner to the Niners and could be persuaded to trade Grover Stewart, a 33-year-old who remains productive and incredibly durable.
Washington’s Daron Payne, who is only 29, might be the best player available and maybe Dolphins GM Jon-Eric Sullivan would be interested in giving the Packers a thank-you gift named Zach Sieler.
The Packers have gotten absolutely nothing resembling consistent impact from the quartet of Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Dani Dennis-Sutton or Brenton Cox. They’ve combined for 5.5 sacks; four individuals have more and another four have exactly 5.5.
Fortunately, help could be on the way soon . The return of Micah Parsons will be more impactful than any potential trade, though there could be a difference between Parsons playing in games and Parsons making an impact in games.
Really, the time to make a trade was a month or two ago. Now, it is time to be patient.
The Packers were fortunate to have depth at linebacker, so they’ve been able to survive without Edgerrin Cooper, who is out with a torn Achilles. Even with Zaire Franklin out with an injured shin, the Packers were OK with Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper. Hopper was a third-round pick in 2024 who hasn’t been given many opportunities on defense. This is his time to show he’s a real player.
The trade market is weak and the Packers are better off with who they’ve got, unless the deal of a lifetime falls in their laps.
Cornerback was a big question mark entering the season with Keisean Nixon coming off a lackluster season and Brandon Cisse being thrown into a starting role as a rookie. They’ve been the last of Green Bay’s problems, though. They haven’t been great but they haven’t been overmatched, either.
“I think the coaches do a really good job with my development, especially coach (Daniel) Bullocks, making sure I’m ready to go each and every week,” Cisse said on Tuesday. “Obviously, JG (defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon) being a DB guy helps me, as well.
“I would say it’s a mix of that putting me in position to make plays, but as much time as I’ve put on task studying and really making sure on my own just to go out there and be dominant. Every day I’m studying a lot. When I go home, I have an office space I study a lot. I’m just trying to make sure I continue to grow.”
You could do worse than Carrington Valentine and Benjamin St-Juste for depth.
The team’s best position coming out of training camp has been the team’s best position through seven games. Xavier McKinney and Evan Williams are an elite tandem at safety and Javon Bullard is a big-time player in the slot.
The Packers used a sixth-round pick on kicker Trey Smack, who has missed a league-high seven kicks. Coach Matt LaFleur gave the embattled kicker a vote of confidence after two horrendous misses against Detroit.
“I think we got enough of a sample size, seeing him just kind of progress throughout the course of the offseason to where we’re at now,” LaFleur said on Tuesday. “And, you know, it was unfortunate, but it is what it is, and it’s the next-game mentality.”
If the Colts are open for business, Spencer Shrader is 19-of-21 on field goals. As if it matters. Brian Gutekunst drafted Smack for what he could become. It’s almost impossible to believe he’s going to give up on him after a couple bad games.
Need: 4 at kicker (but nothing will happen).

title: Aerospace Engineer John Williams’ Career Rockets Up With Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Until Sunday, Green Bay Packers offensive lineman John Williams was better known for being an aerospace engineering major in college than for anything he’d done in the NFL.
Williams was a seventh-round pick in 2025 after being a two-year starting left tackle at Cincinnati. He spent his entire rookie season on injured reserve with a back injury that required surgery.
When Sunday’s game at the Lions kicked off, he had played in five games this season with all 23 snaps coming on special teams. And then, disaster struck. On the fourth snap, Josh Jacobs was tackled into the back of starting center Sean Rhyan’s leg. Jacob Monk finished the series but dropped out after five snaps with a quad injury.
The next man up to the next man up was Williams.
“Obviously, a nightmare scenario and, really, not the first time that’s happened to us,” Williams said on Tuesday, two days before potentially making his first NFL start against the Carolina Panthers. “Always got to be ready. Stay ready so you don’t have to get ready.”
Coach Matt LaFleur, who after the game called the scenario “a little bit terrifying,” wouldn’t commit to Williams being in the lineup this week.
“Pretty impressive to be able to go in there a first time and play the way he did, I was really impressed by it,” LaFleur said on Tuesday evening.
There are a lot of things that made it impressive.
First, Williams was drafted last year but really is a rookie because of the injury. Second, he had no game experience at center at any level of football or in this year’s preseason. Back on the field after last year’s injury, he spent the offseason practices and start of training camp at center but bounced back out to left tackle for all three preseason games. Third, few venues could be tougher for a player who ostensibly was making his NFL debut than Ford Field.
“Well, obviously, I’ve done it before,” he said of playing center. “I hadn’t practiced center in a while but I’ve done it before, so you’ve just got to get back to it. Took a few practice snaps on the sideline and got to get going.”
Asked to define “a while,” he said it’d been a couple weeks since he’d practiced at center.
“I mix it in here and there,” he said.
What was going through his head as he got thrown into the fire?
“Take a few practice snaps on the sideline and then got to get to it,” he said. “Sh**, ain’t got much time to really dilly-dally, panic, think about what’s going on. Just got to go in there and get the job done.”
Williams wasn’t in-his-prime Corey Linsley, but he mostly got the job done amid all the challenges in his first career snaps on offense. In 58 snaps, Sports Info Solutions charged him with two blown blocks – one pressure in the passing game and one in the running game.
His performance impressed left guard Laken Tomlinson, who is closing in on 11,000 career snaps.
“I thought he did great,” he said. “For a guy to have to come in – and, like I told him – not blink at all, it was amazing. Especially in a hostile environment like that, man, kudos to him, for real.”
The center is the quarterback of the offensive line. His intelligence was a major factor in getting things organized at the line of scrimmage.
“That’s the thing. The way he handled it, the way he communicated with confidence, the way he was tripping with the guys, it’s great,” Tomlinson said. “Especially when you have a guy like that, who’s obviously not taking the reps in practice and then coming out and executing in the game, it was phenomenal.”
On the practice field, quarterback Jordan Love works almost exclusively with Rhyan and perhaps a little with the backup, Monk. So, Sunday’s game was probably the first time they’d worked together.
“I think John did a great job,” Love said. “Like you mentioned, coming in, not expecting that situation to happen with two guys going down, but for a guy that hasn’t gotten a lot of reps, obviously, hasn’t taken a lot of center reps with us going into that week,” Love said.
“I think it’s just a great job by him, obviously, being prepared, knowing the plan. Obviously, he’s making a lot of calls at center, and I thought he handled it really well with the noise, the environment and everything. I thought he did a great job.”
Williams wouldn’t go that far. He limited it to “pretty well” considering the circumstances.
“I think I did all right,” he said. “Want to win. Got to win. That’s what we need to do. Win.”
Williams was the 250th out of 257 selections in the 2025 draft. The Packers were intrigued by his versatile skill-set; after he was drafted, he said he could play all five positions.
However, because of the injury, a roster spot had to be won during training camp. By playing left tackle and center, he earned his place.
“It felt good being back out there, especially after everything that happened last year,” Williams said. “Just feels good to be a part of the team, feels good to contribute.”
Williams isn’t a lock to start – the Packers could go with rookie Jager Burton or even Donovan Jennings – but how he performed on Sunday under the most dire of circumstances should get him in the lineup in a big game against the Panthers.
It’s not just this game. Monk was placed on injured reserve on Monday and Rhyan could join him before the week is over. That means Williams could be the team’s starting center for at least the next four games.
“I just like to contribute, be part of the team,” he said. “Whatever they need me to do, that’s what I’m going to do.”

title: Packers-Panthers Tuesday Injury Report: Time Near for Micah Parsons, Kevin Zeitler?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – As is typically the case for a Thursday night game, the Green Bay Packers will be a banged-up bunch for their game against the Carolina Panthers.
The Packers held a walk-through practice on Tuesday. If they would have practiced, they would have been down four starters. One of them was Travis Glover, who has started the past four games at right guard.
More on that and the injury report in a moment. But first, there was a potential big update on the status of Micah Parsons.
The Packers didn’t designate Micah Parsons for return this week because the team doesn’t actually practice this week, which would mean one-third of his 21-day return-to-play window would have been wasted.
“I sure hope so,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Wednesday evening.
There was a touch of optimism there, though LaFleur was quick to remind that it will be a medical decision before the superstar pass rusher returns to practice.
“I’m itching for it, though, for sure,” LaFleur said.
Glover is dealing with a knee injury and didn’t play particularly well against the Lions. If he’s not ready, will Kevin Zeitler make his long-awaited debut?
“You shall see,” LaFleur said.
Zeitler was inactive against Detroit and has played only on special teams in his two appearances.
“If we need him, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Zeitler is ready to contribute on offense. “I think he's done a nice job. Here's a guy that came in and didn't have an offseason, didn't have training camp, and he's kind of gradually working his way back into it.”
Linebacker Zaire Franklin would not have practiced due to the shin injury sustained at practice last week and will not be ready for Thursday, LaFleur said. That means a secon consecutie week for Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper.
Receiver Matthew Golden (shoulder and foot) did not practice. Along with Christian Watson, Golden is the driving force in the passing game. Without him, the Packers would be incredibly shorthanded in terms of passing-game playmakers.
“I sure hope so,” LaFleur said when asked about Golden’s availability, “but we're still kind of working through it. You're not getting any real reps. Everything's pretty much walk-through. We will have a short indy [individual drills period] tomorrow, but to move guys around and see how they look, but certainly hopeful for him.”
The fourth and final player to not practice was center Sean Rhyan, who suffered a high-ankle sprain early in the loss at Detroit and will miss “at least” four games , according to Matt Zenitz of CBS.
LaFleur wouldn’t say if John Williams would get the start after playing well in his first career snaps from scrimmage. The other options are Jager Burton and Donovan Jennings.
“We'll see. We're kind of working through everything right now,” LaFleur said.
There was some good news, though. Defensive tackles Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and Anthony Campbell (ankle) would not have practiced on Monday but would have been limited on Tuesday. Campbell was one of the standouts against Detroit.
Same as with Green Bay, four Panthers starters would not have practiced on Monday: defensive tackle Bobby Brown III (hand), cornerback Akayleb Evans (triceps/knee), left guard Damien Lewis (knee) and outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips (hamstring). Brown and Coker, though, moved to full participation on Tuesday.
Still a DNP was Phillips, who signed a four-year, $120 million contract in free agency this past offseason. He has 2.5 sacks in five games but was inactive last week against Tampa Bay.
“We’re [going to] try to get him back for this game but, again, the recurring same hamstring,” Panthers coach Dave Canales told reporters on Monday. “It’s still that kind of a tight window, so it'll be close on that one.”
Evans started three of six games and has two pass breakups. Brown is the 332-pounder in the middle of Carolina’s defense.
Not on the injury lists are the starting offensive tackles, left tackle Ikem Ekwonu and right tackle Taylor Moton. They are on injured reserve. Former Packers starter Rasheed Walker has struggled in place of Ekwonu. According to Pro Football Focus, he’s tied for the NFL lead with 26 pressures allowed.
Quarterback Bryce Young was full participation for a second consecutive day as he handles an ankle injury.
This will be Green Bay’s third game against him, late in his rookie season in 2023 and again last year.
“It's been pretty remarkable to watch him,” LaFleur said. “The one thing that jumps off tape is just how he anticipates, and he is not scared. I mean, he'll stand in there, he'll get blasted, he'll get rid of the ball, but he throws into tight windows with a lot of anticipation, and he's got people to throw to.”
Did not participate: LB Zaire Franklin (shin), RG Travis Glover (knee), WR Matthew Golden (shoulder/foot), C Sean Rhyan (ankle).
Limited participation: G Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), edge Brenton Cox (quad), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle).
Full participation: CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring).
Did not participate: CB Akayleb Evans (triceps/knee), LG Damien Lewis (knee), OLB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), G Torricelli Simpkins (ankle).
Limited participation: None.

title: Packers-Panthers Matchups: Can Green Bay Take Advantage of Huge Weakness?
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers dropped to last place in the NFC North with a mistake-laden 20-17 loss to the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
They have very little time to lick their wounds thanks to another home date on Thursday night, this one against the Carolina Panthers, who beat the Packers at Lambeau last season.
The Packers had their three-game winning streak snapped by Detroit and are 4-3. The Panthers are 3-3 and lead the NFC South. They are coming off a 43-13 loss to Tampa Bay.
Both teams need a win. How do they get it? Here’s our look at the weekly matchups.
Carolina’s passing offense is a bit of a one-man band. Tetairoa McMillan leads the team in targets, receptions and yards. He’s 11th in the league with 511 yards even while playing one fewer game than most teams. He’s second on the team in touchdowns behind field-stretching tight end Darren Waller.
McMillan caught just four passes for 46 yards last year against Green Bay, but was one of the top rookie receivers in football as he won the Offensive Rookie of the Year Award. The one blemish on his season is that while he’s only dropped one pass, he’s fumbled twice.
Carolina’s passing game starts with Bryce Young, who has been solid if unspectacular this season. He’s thrown 12 touchdowns to just four picks but has been sacked 17 times. He ranks 14th in the league in passer rating.
According to Next Gen Stats, old friend Rasheed Walker leads the Panthers in giving up 34 pressures and four sacks. He allowed three sacks against Tampa Bay on Sunday.
The Packers could have potential for a bounce-back game. Their pass rush was largely nonexistent against the Lions’ Jared Goff, and their coverage suffered as a result.
The combo of Young and McMillan, however, is not exactly the Lions’ offense on turf against Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Jahmyr Gibbs and Sam LaPorta. The Packers should have a good chance to control the passing game.
Jonathan Gannon probably would have signed up for giving up just 119 yards on 29 carries to Jahmyr Gibbs in Sunday’s game against the Lions.
The Packers have done a good job at controlling opposing ground games save for one disastrous performance against Bijan Robinson on a Thursday night against Atlanta. They’re ranked 17th in the NFL with 115 rushing yards allowed per game.
The Panthers are 21st in yards gained per game on the ground. The question in this matchup will be the health and availability of Green Bay’s defensive line. Anthony Campbell and Devonte Wyatt were estimated non-participants in practice. The Packers got a boost to their depth last week with Jordan Riley returning from last year’s Achilles injury, but are starting to run thin on healthy bodies up front.
As poor as Carolina has been in some games against opposing offenses, its pass defense is pretty good. It ranks sixth in the NFL with just 195.7 passing yards allowed per game and eighth with an opponent passer rating of 83.9.
The defensive backs have yet to get their hands on an interception, as its leading man in that department is linebacker Devin Lloyd with two.
One potential game-changing dynamic this week in this matchup will be the availability, or lack thereof, for the Panthers’ star rusher, Jaelen Phillips. Phillips wrecked the game against Green Bay last year when he was playing for the Eagles. According to PFF, Phillips had eight pressures and two quarterback hits as the Eagles held Jordan Love and Co. to just 10 points. He has 2.5 sacks in five games this season.
Last week, the Packers piled up yards but could not find their way into the red zone. Their offense inside the red area was putrid, going 1-of-4, which included a failed fourth down and a missed chip-shot field goal by Trey Smack.
The drops are becoming obscene. Matt LaFleur can continue to say that it’s just football and those things happen. He’s right to some degree, but they need to find a solution. Matthew Golden, Bo Melton and Josh Jacobs were culprits last week. All three cost them big plays, including a potential game-winning score from Jacobs.
There will be some shuffling on the offensive line. The question is how much? John Williams played most of last week’s game at Detroit after starter Sean Rhyan suffered a high-ankle sprain and backup Jacob Monk sustained an injured quad. Rhyan will miss at least a few weeks and Monk is on injured reserve. Presumably, Williams will start, but don’t discount the possibility of Jager Burton getting the call.
Right guard Travis Glover is on the injury report with a knee injury. Left guard Aaron Banks, the former starter, was active last week but sat on the bench in favor of Laken Tomlinson.
Regardless, they need to protect Jordan Love better than they have the last two weeks against Ejiro Evero’s defense.
The potential for big plays always makes the Packers a threat, but the lack of consistency pushes this matchup to a draw.
As it turns out, Josh Jacobs was not enough to save the Packers’ run game from the depths of hell it continues to descend into.
The Packers remain 32nd in the league in rushing, with their 59.9-yard average right in line with the 60 yards gained against the Lions.
Perhaps some good news is on the way? The Panthers have the worst rush defense in the league, giving up a league-worst 153.2 rushing yards per game and a league-high 5.16 yards per carry. They also lead the league in rushing touchdowns surrendered with 11.
“Just be quicker,” Jacobs said on Tuesday. “Just stuff that come with playing ball. I would also say just keep try to encourage the guys and make the O-line right when it’s opportunities. That’s the only thing I would’ve been preaching really this whole week, just telling guys to finish straight up on guys and allow me to be me and allow me to make them right, so just trying to have that trust.
“Obviously, this week we have a different group of guys up there, so it’s going to be a feel-out process. But we’ll see how it goes.”
The Panthers were clobbered by Chicago in Week 1, when D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai ran for more than 100 yards. Quarterback Caleb Williams added another 65. Overall, Chicago carried 39 times for 291 yards and averaged 7.5 yards per carry.
Sunday’s blowout loss against Tampa Bay was pretty similar. The Bucs averaged 5.3 yards per carry, piling up 258 yards on 49 attempts.
The Packers’ run game should have some opportunities this week, but you don’t have to look that far into the past to see another game where they should have had chances to get moving. Dallas was the worst run defense in the NFL when it came to Lambeau a couple weeks ago, and the Packers’ leading rusher had 28 yards.
Maybe Jacobs changes things this week as he’s more acclimated, but until there’s any improvement that is seen on the field, it’s impossible to give the Packers the benefit of the doubt.
One of the biggest reasons the Panthers were able to knock off the Packers at Lambeau Field last year was Brandon McManus missing a field goal.
McManus’ struggles last season culminated with a disastrous performance in the postseason. As a result, the Packers traded two draft choices to grab Trey Smack in the sixth round.
Smack has shown off a big leg. He’s 2-for-2 on kicks more than 50 yards this season. The problems have been for the more makeable field goals. Smack is 5-of-9 on kicks between 30 and 49 yards. He’s also missed two extra-point attempts. In the three-point loss to Detroit, he missed a 26-yard field goal and had a 35-yarder tipped at the line for another miss.
This is the rollercoaster ride the Packers chose to get on when they gave a rookie kicker unlimited runway, like they did with Anders Carlson during the 2023 season. That year, predictably, ended in disaster with Carlson missing a key field goal in the team’s postseason loss to the 49ers.
We’re a long way away from Smack deciding a playoff game, should the Packers even qualify.
For now, however, he’s the single biggest reason that special teams goes in the direction of whoever Green Bay is playing.

title: Week 8 Consensus NFL Power Rankings: After Big Rise, How Far Did Packers Fall?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers lost 20-17 in Motown on Sunday, but they weren’t driven off a cliff in our Consensus NFL Power Rankings.
First, what are the Consensus Power Rankings? We take eight sets of national power rankings and turn them into one turbocharged power ranking.
With a three-game winning streak, the Packers rose from 24th to 12th in our rankings . After the three-point loss to Detroit, they fell back three spots to 15th.
Here is a closer look, with more information and full rankings available by clicking on the links.
The Packers slipped six spots in Conor Orr’s rankings .
“I’m not sure why – maybe it’s because Jordan Love had a two-week stretch where he played like the Madden quarterback of our dreams – but I am more interested in Green Bay at the trade deadline than any other team in football. I’m still not letting go of Super Bowl aspirations for this team.”
Pete Prisco dropped the Packers only one spot in his rankings.
“Their winning streak came to an end against the Lions in what was a sloppy game. The injuries on the offensive line are a big concern.”
Mike Florio dropped the Packers five spots and offered a word of warning. “They can’t let one loss become two on Thursday night.”
The Packers are down four spots in ESPN’s rankings , which are voted on by their team beat writers.
This week’s theme is best offseason addition. Rob Demovsky selected defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon, who has kept the defense going without Micah Parsons on the strength of takeaways.
“They lead the NFL in forced turnovers (13) and interceptions (nine). They've already topped their interception total from all of last season (seven) and nearly matched their takeaway total (14). Two years ago, the Packers had the fourth-most takeaways with 31, including 17 interceptions. … Gannon has also used disguises and blitzes to manufacture pressure without injured edge rusher Micah Parsons.”
Nick Shook kept the Packers at No. 15 after they lost due in part to Trey Smack’s two missed kicks.
“I can’t dock the Packers for losing a close divisional game on the road, but I can suggest they start exploring other kicking options. … Looking ahead, I am curious to see how much of a difference Josh Jacobs can make for Green Bay’s largely inept running game.”
The Packers were dinged only one spot in Frank Schwab’s rankings. He focused on the officiating – including Xavier McKinney’s reaction. But:
“Officiating or not, the Packers made key errors. Josh Jacobs was good in his return, but he dropped a pass in the end zone in the fourth quarter. Trey Smack missed two short field goals, one that was partially blocked right after Jacobs' drop. Matt LaFleur passed on a field goal to go for it on fourth-and-4 in the first half. Green Bay put up only 17 points on a bad Lions defense. And the officiating didn't help, either.”
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff dropped the Packers three spots in their rankings.
This week’s theme is something spooky, and they chose Green Bay’s NFL-worst rushing attack.
“Josh Jacobs returned to the lineup in a move that should have helped lift the league’s worst rushing attack (based on EPA per attempt). Instead, he managed just 36 yards on 11 carries. Jacobs was better in the passing game (five receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown), but it’s tough to run an offense without a respectable rushing attack.”
Instead of inching up close to the top 10 , Ralph Vacchiano backed the Packers up four spots in his rankings.
“The Packers were a couple of missed kicks away from beating the Lions … but they just couldn’t make the big stop or the big offensive play when it mattered most. QB Jordan Love is still playing well, and he’s got RB Josh Jacobs back now to boost their rushing attack. And their defense is playing sneaky good too. So, the Pack has it all … except that they’re 4-3 and that puts them in last place in their tough division. So, they remain in the middle of the pack for now.”
The Panthers are 19th in the Consensus, with individual rankings ranging from 16th to 22nd. They plunged from 18th to 13th in Frank Schwab’s rankings at Yahoo.
“Every team is allowed a mulligan or two over a long season, but what happened Sunday was atrocious from the Panthers,” he wrote. “They trailed 43-6 at home to a Buccaneers team that had just one win beforehand. Carolina turned it over four times. It even had an extra point blocked and returned for 2 points. Bryce Young had by far his worst game of the season.”
Schwab pointed to Carolina’s horrendous run defense. Well, can the Packers take advantage?
Sportsbook odds aren’t part of our rankings, but they do provide one more perspective on the state of the league. In Packers-related odds at FanDuel Sportsbook :
The Packers, who were +2000 to win the Super Bowl before Week 1, plunged to as low as +6000. They rebounded to +3000 with their three consecutive wins, but fell back to +3500 after losing to Detroit. While the odds changed since last week, they remain 15th on the board.
Among NFC North teams, the Bears are +1400, the Lions are +1700 and the Vikings +1800.
Green Bay opened the season ranked seventh in the NFC playoff odds at -112, fell to as low as 12th at +250 after the win at Tampa Bay, rebounded back to -118 with their winning streak but fell to +126 after losing to Detroit. That is eighth on the board and last among the NFC North teams (Minnesota is -520, Detroit is -270 and Chicago is -255).
Quarterback Jordan Love is rising fast in the MVP race. He opened at +2200 but bottomed out at +10000. He rose to +3300 after their three-game winning streak and moved to +2500 after the Detroit game. That’s tied with Jared Goff for eighth on the board. Buffalo’s Josh Allen (+150) is the heavy favorite.
The Packers are last in the NFC North standings and far back in the back in the division odds at DraftKings. Minnesota is -105, followed by Detroit at +300, Chicago at +315 and Green Bay at +1125.

title: Sean Rhyan Injury Update, John Williams’ Opportunity and Packers Roster Move
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – John Williams went from the end of the bench to front and center for the Green Bay Packers in the blink of an eye.
Williams, a seventh-round pick in 2025, hadn’t played a single snap on offense in his career. Until Sunday. With starting center Sean Rhyan and backup Jacob Monk injured within the first 10 plays, Williams wound up playing 58 snaps against the Detroit Lions on Sunday.
The job, presumably, is his now.
Rhyan suffered a high-ankle sprain during the opening series against Detroit when running back Josh Jacobs was tackled and fell into the back of Rhyan’s leg. He will miss “at least” the next four games, according to CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz.
Testing has confirmed that #Packers center Sean Rhyan has a high ankle sprain that will likely sideline him at least a month, sources tell @CBSSports . Not currently expected to undergo tightrope surgery but currently viewed as likely that he’ll miss at least four weeks. pic.twitter.com/P8mqaYnajh
With Monk suffering an injured quad during that same series and landing on injured reserve on Monday, Williams could be the team’s starting center for the next month. The other option is rookie Jager Burton, who was inactive for the third consecutive game.
With Monk on IR, the Packers promoted Mekhi Becton from the practice squad. The 11th pick of the 2020 draft, he had started 59 games during his first six seasons. The Packers signed him after the Week 3 disaster against Atlanta . He spent the past few weeks working at right guard and right tackle while getting acclimated after offseason surgery.
“Got a lot of confidence with what he’s been able to display on the practice field. So, 100 percent,” coach Matt LaFleur said recently.
Becton is an enormous individual at 6-foot-7 and 357 pounds. He was a first-round bust with the Jets, where he played left tackle, but his career changed when the Eagles placed him at right guard in 2024. That’s where he played for the Chargers last season.
“Mekhi is a big guy; big physical guy,” said Packers left guard Laken Tomlinson, who played with the Jets in 2022 and 2023. “He’s a people-mover. I played with him with the Jets. He’s a physical freak. Definitely excited to have him on the squad.”
Including Rhyan, the Packers have 11 offensive linemen on their roster.
The projected starting five after training camp consisted of left tackle Jordan Morgan, left guard Aaron Banks, Rhyan, right guard Jacob Monk and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele. For most of the game against Detroit, only Morgan was on the field.
Williams was an excellent left tackle at Cincinnati. The Packers drafted him in the seventh round last year, but he missed his entire rookie season following back surgery aside from three weeks of practice late in the season.
This year, he spent the offseason practices and the start of training camp at center before bouncing out to left tackle. In fact, all 93 preseason snaps came at left tackle.
However, with Rhyan and Monk injured and Burton inactive, Williams was thrown into the fire at Detroit, where he was challenged by a strong defensive line and incredible noise. PFF charged him with one pressure allowed on 43 pass-protecting snaps.
“I can’t say enough about the job John Williams did, coming in in a hostile environment and just handling the operation, the communication,” coach Matt LaFleur said after the game. “To lose two guys at center that quickly in the game, it was a little bit terrifying, but I thought he did a really good job.”
Williams majored an aerospace engineering , so his ability to handle the mental aspects of the game are not in question.
“He’s so intelligent. He’s got great command, understands all the calls, why we’re doing what we’re doing,” LaFleur said. “Again, I commend him for the job he did stepping in a tough situation.”
After the game, quarterback Jordan Love laughed when asked if he’s ever taken snaps with Williams. After all, Love is the starting quarterback and Williams was an end-of-the-depth-chart player.
“Not much,” he said. “I think it’s one of those things where we always talk about that next-man-up mentality. Early on, losing Sean and losing Monk, I think John did a great job being able to step up. He hasn’t taken many reps at center, let alone with the ones.
“I think for him, that’s just a great job of being ready, being able to come in, be able to make these calls in a position where he hasn’t played too much. We talk about it all the time – that next-man-up mentality – but I think he did a great job tonight, and it’s going to be another short week for him to get ready. We’ll see what those guys’ status is. It’s a tough situation losing two guys early, but I think John did a great job.”

title: Latest NFC Playoff Standings, Projections Are Double-Whammy for Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers are in last place in the NFC North but are clinging to a spot in the NFC playoff field following their loss to the Detroit Lions.
With a 4-3 record, the Packers are in seventh place in the NFC. If the season were to end today, they would be – you guessed it – the No. 7 seeds. That was their spot in the playoff field each of the last three seasons.
Making matters worse, their first-round opponent would be the 49ers, who knocked the Packers out of the playoffs in 2019, 2021 and 2023.
Here’s where things stand, along with the latest playoff projections.
The Packers are in seventh place in the NFC. They have the same record as the Seahawks but have a better conference record.
Talking about the state of the team, quarterback Jordan Love said after Sunday’s game:
“Man, I just think looking at tonight, just taking today into consideration, not good enough. I still think there’s so much more out there for us as a football team in every area.
“I think just looking at the offense, we’ve made some strides. There’s still a lot of plays out there where we can really be dominant, but we’ve got to be able to come out here and finish these drives, put up points and just execute at a higher level. I still think there’s a lot out there for us.”
The Packers are one game ahead of the Falcons, Rams and Cowboys. The Packers lost to Atlanta, beat Dallas and will play Los Angeles.
2. San Francisco 49ers, 6-1
12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 2-5
13. New Orleans Saints, 2-5
14. Arizona Cardinals, 2-5
15. Philadelphia Eagles, 2-5
16. Washington Commanders, 1-4-1
Here are the Packers’ playoff chances, according to various playoff simulators. Their playoff hopes took a significant hit following Sunday’s loss to the Lions.
Using The Athletic’s playoff simulator , the Packers have a 40 percent chance of qualifying for the playoffs. It was 53 percent before the game. Their NFC North odds are only 5 percent with a less than 1 percent chance of winning the Super Bowl.
Their playoff chances would bounce back to 48 percent with a victory over NFC South-leading Carolina on Thursday night.
At NFL.com , the Packers have a 42 percent chance of reaching the postseason, down from 54 percent last week. That ranks ninth in the NFC, with Seattle and Dallas ahead of the Packers even while behind them in the standings.
At Playoff Status , the Packers have a 50 percent chance of reaching the playoffs, with about a 4 percent chance of doing it as the NFC North champions. They had a 61 percent chance at this time last week.
With a win over Carolina, their playoff chances would improve to 56 percent. With a loss, they’d fall to 40 percent.
At ESPN , the Packers have a 41 percent chance of earning a playoff berth, down sharply from 56 percent last week. They have a 5 percent chance of winning the NFC North.
The Packers have a 65 percent chance of beating the Panthers, according to ESPN. It’s a big game; their playoff chances would improve to 49 percent with a win but plunge to 27 percent with a loss.
At Stick to the Model , Green Bay’s playoff chances are merely 37 percent. They were at 49 percent before the Detroit game.
With a win, they’d bounce back to 45 percent; with a loss, they’d plummet to 23 percent.
In the latest playoff odds at FanDuel Sportsbook , the Packers are eighth at +126. They are behind the 49ers, Vikings, Lions, Bears, Seahawks, Rams and Cowboys.
“It is what it is. You got to learn from it and move on,” coach Matt LaFleur said after the game. “You know, we’re going to have a team that I’m sure is gonna be pretty ticked off in their own right coming into Lambeau, and it’s going to be the team that can bounce back the best.”
The Packers are 3.5-point favorites against Carolina, for what it’s worth.
The Packers’ remaining opponents have a .538 winning percentage this season, according to Tankathon . That’s the eighth-toughest remaining strength of schedule, which is the bad news. The good news is the Vikings rank first, the Bears third and the Lions fourth due to the bruising NFC North gauntlet.
Green Bay’s remaining 10 games come against four teams with losing records: the Dolphins, Saints, Texans and Rams.
“Just get back to the drawing board, obviously, refocus, regroup and put all of our focus in getting our bodies back in preparing for Carolina,” quarterback Jordan Love said.

title: Texans Sign Former Cowboys RB Amid Backfield Depth Concerns
full_text:
The Houston Texans have made a new addition to their backfield on Wednesday despite being in the middle of their Week 8 bye .
And that signing just so happens to have come via waivers from their in-state neighbors in the Dallas Cowboys.
According to the Texans' transaction log, the team has claimed running back Emari Demercado off waivers after he was let go by the Dallas Cowboys earlier in the week.
We have claimed Emari Demercado off waivers and made other roster moves. pic.twitter.com/2V0C9WcsDm
Demercado, a 5-foot-9, 215-pound running back who's been in the league for the past four seasons. He spent his first three years pro with the Arizona Cardinals, where he played a total of 40 games and recorded over 1,100 yards from scrimmage throughout that span.
More recently, Demercado had been with the Kansas City Chiefs earlier this year as a part of their 90-man roster leading into the regular season.
He was ultimately sent to waivers by the Chiefs at the end of August, and would quickly be scooped up by the Cowboys, where he would play two games over the course of this season.
In those two games he played in between Weeks 1 and 2, Demercado put together five carries for 15 yards on the ground, but would not be activated past those pair of appearances.
Now, Demercado is able to land on his feel with the Texans heading into the second half of the season, as he'll be able to provide some sense of backfield depth that Houston was left without during their most recent game against the New York Giants.
Since the Texans' Week 5 win vs. the Tennessee Titans, the offense has been without their lead veteran in the backfield in David Montgomery, as he's been dealing with a groin injury to keep him sidelined for Weeks 6 and 7.
Montgomery has still yet to log a limited, let alone full practice, for the team since going down with his injury. And while the Texans do have a bye week ahead of them that provides extra time for him to get right, there are no guarantees he'll be ready to go before their next game in Week 9 against the LA Chargers.
Without Montgomery, the Texans were currently left with just two active running backs on their roster in Week 7. RB3 British Brooks has been on injured reserve since Week 4 with a hamstring injury, and Jawhar Jordan was just placed on Houston's practice squad injured reserve after suffering an injury in Week 6 vs. Jacksonville.
That meant Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale were the only names the Texans could lean on in their backfield for Week 7. And while that setup worked relatively well for most of the contest against New York, an injury scare for Marks in the second half put that need for a third rostered running back on full display.
Therefore, the Texans now have another running back on their 53-man roster to lean on in Demercado, who brings depth, experience, and another ball carrier to utilize in the event that Montgomery–– or any other running back in the mix–– is due to miss any more time moving forward.

title: Texans WR Jaylin Noel's Foot Injury Update Is Worst-Case Scenario
full_text:
In the midst of the Houston Texans' Week 7 loss to the New York Giants, the wide receiver room would see one of their key contributors leave the game early with a toe injury: second-year wideout Jaylin Noel.
Noel would inevitably not return to the game, was said to have been suffering from turf toe from head coach DeMeco Ryans after the game, and was waiting further testing to see just how long he would be sidelined.
And it turns out, Noel will be out for a significant amount of time. The Texans have announced that Noel will be placed on injured reserve due to the toe injury he sustained this weekend against the Giants.
But that's not all. According to the Houston Chronicle 's Jonathan M. Alexander , Noel's toe injury is expected to be serious enough to sideline him for the rest of the season.
It's yet another tough injury blow for the Texans to sustain to be without Noel for what appears to be the rest of the season.
Houston has seen multiple starters on both sides of the ball deal with extended absences over the past few weeks. That includes injuries to Jalen Pitre, Reed Blankenship, and David Montgomery, and now, the newest issue is within their wide receiver room.
But those injuries are expected to subside within the next few weeks. Noel, however, now seems to have reached the end of what's been a really inspiring second season when he's gotten a chance to be on the field.
Noel has gotten off to at hot start for his second season in Houston, finding his way to become a gradually more involved piece within the Texans' passing attack–– especially for the past three weeks.
On the season, Noel has put together 19 receptions on 23 targets, 331 yards and two touchdowns, while currently leading the NFL in yards per target (14.4).
But now, the Texans will be forced to move forward for the next 10 games on the schedule without him. Noel now joins his draft classmate, Jayden Higgins, on injured reserve while being expected to miss the season; both of whom entered this season expected to make a big leap in terms of their development.
And while Houston does have a deep wide receiver room to bank on in his absence, not having Noel does take away a big-time explosive piece offensively who was just beginning to catch his stride within the passing attack.
The silver lining for the Texans in a rough turn of events for Noel is the fact that their wide receiver room is extremely deep compared to where things stood at the start of this season.
They've got Nico Collins leading the way, Xavier Hutchinson and Kayshon Boutte due to remain key parts of the Texans' passing attack, and Marvin Harrison Jr. and Tank Dell are just beginning to catch their stride within the offense within their respective situations.
The two names that remain the most compelling to keep an eye on now that Noel is due to miss the rest of the season will be both of Harrison Jr. and Dell.
While both pass-catchers were extremely limited in Week 7's game plan against the Giants, their usage and involvement should only be expected to increase in the weeks ahead. Harrison Jr. is still learning his way around the Texans' playbook and overall offensive scheme, while Dell just came back for his first NFL game in over 670 days .
So the Texans might be able to navigate the storm offensively, even without one of their biggest bright spots on the offensive side of the ball so far this season. But there's no doubt that losing Noel's explosiveness and downfield ability is going to sting for C.J. Stroud and the rest of the surrounding offense.

title: Texans' DeMeco Ryans Has a Simple Plan to Reset During Bye Week
full_text:
The Houston Texans have officially arrived at their bye in Week 8 –– a mid-season break that many would consider much-needed for this team after a rough 2-5 start to their 2026 campaign.
DeMeco Ryans and the Texans' staff will have an extra week at their disposal to take a step back, evaluate what's working and what's not through this team's up-and-down start to the season, and hope that this ship can be turned around in time for their Week 9 meeting facing the LA Chargers .
But when it comes to the Texans' plan for their players and any practice over the next week, it seems that Houston is putting a major emphasis on rest, recovery, and resetting rather than doubling down on any work on the field.
Ryans recently appeared on Texans Radio earlier this week to break down what the Texans' plans will be over the course of the bye as they try to rebound from their slow first half of the season.
And overall, Ryans' message was simple: take a deep breath, reset, then come back recharged for next week.
“Yeah, for the bye week, I think it comes at the right time, getting it right in the middle. I think guys just need to take a deep breath; just reset,” Ryans said.
“I think it's not going out and practicing four times this week, that's going to help us get better. I think everybody just needs to hit a reset mentally, see where they are mentally, physically, get their bodies recovered, heal up, and then we'll come back next week.”
Some who have seen the Texans' performance over the past several weeks may argue that more time on the practice field and in the weight room will be able to help Houston turn around in their desired direction.
After all, the Texans have lost five of their first seven games, so maybe more on-field work at the bye could be an approach to consider.
But for Ryans, he sees the situation as quite the opposite.
Instead of putting further strain on the players through what's already been a challenging start to the new year, Ryans wants his guys to really take this time off as a true bye week, then hope that extra rest can spark some new energy once the Texans are back at practice next Wednesday.
“Our plan this week isn't to go out on the field and do more practices. It's truly to give the guys a break,” Ryans continued.
“Let them get out of here. Make sure they're taking care of their bodies the right way. Get a couple days to themselves to just, ‘Hey, reanalyze yourself as a player, as a man. Like, where are you? What do you need to do?’"
The bye week also gives the Texans' staff some extra time to work through some of their own successes and failures that they may have encountered through the first seven games––and they certainly aren't without their own mistakes, just like the players.
Whether it revolves around their defensive scheme and their woes in pass coverage, some of their offensive plays or personnel that might not be working, this week has the chance to be even more constructive for the Texans' coaches than it is for the players.
So Ryans and the rest of the staff on the Texans' sidelines will also make sure to take some time to decompress throughout the bye. But the time will also give Houston a perfect opportunity to work through what aspects of their game plan are or aren't working as expected.
“Yeah, for the bye week, I think it comes at the right time, getting it right in the middle. I think guys just need to take a deep breath; just reset,” Ryans said.
“It's extremely important that we go all in on the self-scout,” Ryans continued. “We can look at certain things from a coverage standpoint. Hey, we're giving up explosive passes. I know what we probably want to do. What was the intentionality behind this scheme going into this game, and did we do it well? Is that working for us right now?”
“So, it's a really good week to just hit reset, refocus. You don't have to game plan, but you look internally and truly look at it. I tell coaches, look at it without feelings. Take your feelings out of it. Like, what does the film actually say? Does it say jumbo is working? Does it say man coverage is working? If that's not it, then we got to adjust.”
There's still so much more time to go this season, which means there's certainly an opportunity for the Texans to turn things around in time for a late run like they did around this time last year .
But this bye week is a pivotal point in the season where the Texans can get some coveted time off to really be ready for the second half of the year that could arguably be more challenging than the first few games Houston's had to endure.
So for Ryans, this week will mark a perfect time to step away, and thus offers the best chance for the Texans to try and rally for the second half of the schedule, starting with Week 9 against the Chargers.

title: Predicting Texans' Next 4 Games After Disappointing 2-5 Start
full_text:
The Houston Texans are heading into the bye week with an ugly-looking 2-5 record over their first seven games.
That's not where anyone expected the Texans to be at this point in the year. Many viewed this Houston roster to have one of the league's best defenses and a much-improved offense to rank towards the top of the AFC, but Houston now is just hoping that they can hang onto a spot in the Wild Card.
So now, the pressure is on for the Texans to kick it into high gear after the bye, and put some wins together and climb out of the deep hole they've since dug themselves into. Only four more losses would guarantee Houston finishes the year under .500, and pretty much ends any hopes of being one of the final playoff teams in the conference.
But just how well might the Texans fare through their next four games on the schedule? Is there any hope that Houston can run the table for a perfect 4-0 stretch? Or is that post-bye-week success just wishful thinking?
Let's pass some of the time through the Texans' Week 8 bye by predicting how each of Houston's next four games on the schedule could go, and what their record could end up looking like coming out of that Week 12 matchup:
The Texans have no choice but to take care of business in this game against the currently winless Chargers. And even while taking the long road trip to the West Coast, it feels like Houston should still be able to do so.
They'll be well-rested after the bye, with guys such as Jalen Pitre, Reed Blankenship, and David Montgomery possibly returning , and have an ideal matchup against a struggling Chargers offense for their defense to have a bounceback from the woes they encountered against the New York Giants.
The Chargers currently average the lowest points per game in the NFL (15.0), are bottom five in total yards per game (287.2), and are one of two teams to have not recorded 10 touchdowns or more through the first seven weeks of the season.
If the Texans can't get their defense right against this team, it'll be hard to find a better matchup for them to do so.
The Deshaun Watson revenge game... maybe?
The Texans have only faced off against their former quarterback once since they shipped him to the Cleveland Browns in 2022, and it was in that one matchup that Watson actually got the last laugh in a 27-14 victory over Houston back in December of 2022.
Fast forward to 2026, and Watson gets another chance to face his former team. And there's no question that both sides will be looking significantly different than they did from that last meeting four years ago.
Each team has cycled through some head coaches. C.J. Stroud will get his first opportunity to face the Texans' former signal-caller, and the Browns are surprisingly coming together for one of their more solid seasons in recent memory with a 5-2 record through seven weeks.
Heading into the season, many probably would've picked the Texans to take home a victory here pretty convincingly. However, considering how each of these teams has kicked off the first half of their schedule, and how inconsistent Houston has been on both sides of the ball, it's a whole lot harder to have that same confidence here.
Based on what we've seen through seven games, the Browns might just have the upper hand with a respectable defense, strong coaching, and momentum on their side to give Watson a 2-0 record against Houston.
Prediction: Texans Lose, 20-21
We'll keep this one quick. The Texans, at this point in the season, would be desperate to cling onto a victory against the Colts to try and go on a late-season run, especially after having dropped their last meeting against Indianapolis to find themselves 0-3.
The Colts have been the trade deadline's biggest sellers thus far with moves to already send out Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner. And with two more weeks to go, this roster could be down even more key contributors like Josh Downs, or even Jonathan Taylor.
The Texans have little excuse not to split the season series against Indianapolis. It was a shock that Houston couldn't claw out a victory in Week 3 after Daniel Jones had committed a total of three turnovers through the day, and it'd be even more surprising to see the Colts get another win here with a worse roster for meeting number two.
Houston should win this one rather convincingly on their home field, and perhaps even in a bit of a blowout fashion. It'd certainly be a plus for team morale.
Prediction: Texans Win, 33-10
There's no doubt that this game is the toughest Houston has on the schedule through the next four weeks: Houston gets to host Lamar Jackson and the Baltimore Ravens on their home field at Reliant Stadium with their backs against the wall to try and avoid another loss on the books.
Perhaps the Texans have a fighting chance in this one. If their offense can pick up a bit more steam compared to what they showcased against the Giants, and the defense looks healthy and at least a little bit closer to their 2025 status, Houston can pull out a much-needed win against a tough Ravens opponent.
But the Texans' defense hasn't exactly shown to be a reliable force when it comes to stopping some of the best quarterbacks on their schedule right now. They've fallen flat against Josh Allen, Joe Burrow, and Dak Prescott, and Jackson finds himself right on the same caliber as those guys.
Last year, the Texans dominated the Ravens in their Week 5 matchup, 44-10 . But that was without Lamar Jackson on the field, paired with what was then a dominant defense that was just starting to catch its stride. For this season's matchup against Baltimore, the situation could look a whole lot different.
When combining Houston's recent troubles against opposing quarterbacks, along with their struggles against the run (plus tackling) against an evasive offense led by Lamar and Derrick Henry, I have my reservations about the Texans being able to get a home victory here.
Prediction: Texans Lose, 18-24
This would not be the most ideal outcome for the Texans, all things considered. At 3-1, or even running the table at 4-0, there starts to be a whole lot more optimism in play that Houston can turn their season around for a late bid into the postseason.
But with seven losses in 12 weeks, the Texans would have to essentially win out through the rest of their schedule to have a chance at a Wild Card appearance.
However, that's simply the price to be paid for the Texans' slow start to the season. Margin for error becomes a whole lot thinner, and only a couple of losses across their next four games could be just enough to bury their hopes of clawing into the postseason for a fourth-straight season, let alone win the AFC South.
Of course, there are a lot more games to go, and anything can happen throughout the next 10 weeks. If this is the end result for Houston following Week 12, though, it's going to be hard to feel a whole lot better about the Texans' odds to make a late-season run from what things look like right now.

title: 3 Texans Players Who Need Bigger Roles After the Bye Week
full_text:
The Houston Texans are heading into their Week 8 bye at a gloomy 2-5 record.
For the Texans to get back on track for the second half of the season, some changes around the roster will have to be made–– even if that doesn't include making a big swing on the trade market ahead of the deadline.
Some of those changes could be as simple as handing a few players around the roster more playing time than they've been accustomed to through the past several weeks.
This Texans roster already has several talented players on both sides of the ball to bank on even if they're three games under .500, so maybe flipping the switch for a few wins could be as simple as distributing more opportunities to a select few players in need of increased snaps.
With that in mind, let's take a look at three players around the Texans' roster who feel due to be more involved coming out of this week's bye:
The Texans have taken a slower approach to get their new wide receiver, Marvin Harrison Jr. involved as a key piece of their offense through the first two weeks he's been in the building.
He's seen less than 30 combined offensive snaps against the Jacksonville Jaguars and New York Giants, and has turned those appearances in for four receptions, 40 yards, and one touchdown.
On one hand, it's probably justified for the Texans to keep Harrison Jr. limited within his first couple of games as a part of this offense. Making sure he's fully adjusted within this passing attack to become the true downfield weapon Houston brought him in to be will be the best course of action for the long term .
But the Texans did give up a second-round pick for this coming draft to bring in Harrison Jr. That's a significant investment in a wide receiver that should encourage Houston's staff to get him more snaps as a complementary piece opposite of Nico Collins sooner rather than later, which might be a bit easier now that the bye week is upon us.
The Texans need to get Harrison Jr. on the field for much more than the sub-30% he's seen over the last two weeks. And if the flashes he's shown through the start of his tenure in Houston are a sign of anything, getting him more touches should be a decision that pays off pretty nicely.
It's become pretty easy to forget about Marlin Klein as a piece within the Texans' offense, considering he's been a healthy scratch ever since his Week 3 appearance against the Indianapolis Colts. But it wasn't too long ago that he was Houston's 58th pick of the 2026 NFL Draft as their third selection off the board.
Klein projected as an intriguing, but raw, talent at the tight end position who has stout 6-foot-6, 250-pound size with upside both as a blocker and a vertical threat for the offense.
His production at Michigan was far from eye- catching, but he did make a few plays in both training camp and preseason (and from a 16-yard reception in Week 1 vs. the Buffalo Bills) that made it feel like he could be an impactful player for this offense to use in heavier 12 and 13 personnel situations.
However, the Texans have essentially shut him out from the game plan entirely throughout the past month. Why? Houston's coaching staff has wanted him to be a more quality contributor on special teams, and to this point, that aspect of his game hasn't clicked––or else he'd be on the field more than he has been.
Regardless of that impact on special teams, though, the Texans have to give Klein a chance to get on the field on gamedays. He was one of Houston's top selections in their most recent draft for a reason, but has yet to really get a chance to spread his wings as the talent this front office brought him in to be.
Another rookie the Texans added in the second round of their most recent draft, yet has been on the field more than Klein throughout the regular season, is defensive tackle Kayden McDonald.
McDonald started the first four weeks of the year stuck on injured reserve with an ankle injury , but has gradually found his way into Houston's defensive line rotation alongside Sheldon Rankins and Tommy Togiai.
And so far, McDonald's integration into that defensive line rotation has put him into a role as Houston's DT3, which is somewhat expected as a first-year talent still fresh off of a weeks-long injury. But the Texans have every reason to get him more involved after the events of their last loss vs. the New York Giants in which they struggled to stop the run, as well as their lackluster ability to tackle.
McDonald, however, was viewed by many coming into the draft as a high-level run defender, and a super productive tackler from his one year starting at Ohio State.
While he might be a bit more raw than the more experienced Rankins and Togiai, handing him some of their snaps in an effort to improve both of those areas defensively could be a huge lift for this struggling unit for the second half of the season.

title: Texans Missed a Golden Opportunity to Trade for Quenton Nelson
full_text:
The Houston Texans just missed their chance to bring a major upgrade on their offensive line.
That's because the Indianapolis Colts just shipped out one of the best interior offensive linemen in the NFL, Quenton Nelson, who was traded to the Seattle Seahawks on Tuesday afternoon as the first domino to fall in the Colts' potential deadline fire sale.
According to ESPN 's Adam Schefter, the Seahawks gave up a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange to bring in Nelson; a major upgrade to Seattle's offensive line that takes their interior to the next level en route to their hopes of another Super Bowl push.
Trade: Colts have agreed to send eight-time Pro-Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks, per me and @rapsheet . Nelson is on an expiring contract and the Colts are opting to get back draft capital now before they could lose him in free agency. But an all-time Colt now… pic.twitter.com/uKlAEYkPnZ
However, when looking at this deal through a Texans-centric lens, it leaves you wondering: what was stopping Houston from going out to make a move like this?
Now, to address the obvious, it's not often you see two division rivals make a move with one another, especially for a star-level addition like Nelson is. Perhaps Indianapolis would've been totally unwilling to ship off Nelson to Houston in an effort to boost their hopes of winning the AFC South.
However, in the event that the Colts were open to such an outcome, the Texans certainly would've had a comparable package to Seattle's that could entice Indianapolis to consider them as a trade partner as well. And Houston certainly has a dire need on their offensive line that would warrant a big swing like this one.
Yes, the Texans did just trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. a couple of weeks ago for the steep price of a second-round pick from the Arizona Cardinals. Trading away even more draft capital for an expiring contract like Nelson in an effort to boost a 2-5 team could be seen as a bit too short-sighted.
But the Texans' decision to go out and secure Harrison Jr. earlier this month was seemingly done with the mindset that this team was still to be considered mid-season buyers. One loss against the Giants, while a bad loss, shouldn't totally derail that thought process from Caserio and Co., and should at least leave them open to adding even more talent, if the price is right.
Houston's lead decision-makers have remained outspokenly confident with the core group this team has in place. But with consistent offensive line issues— that were on full display this past weekend in the form of their penalty woes — have always been a recurring issue for the Texans' offense to reach its full potential.
Nelson, through the first seven games of the season with Indianapolis, he's found his way to landing the third-best PFF grade for offensive guards (85.7) . He's excelled as a pass-blocker, has allowed just six pressures, one QB hit, and zero sacks through that span. Most importantly, he's been called for just one penalty.
In retrospect, this was the big swing the Texans should've taken to upgrade their roster; not trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. Nelson fills a major need on the offensive line, could've seamlessly fit in at left guard next to Keylan Rutledge and Ed Ingram on the interior, and would've brought a ton of optimism upfront compared to what Houston has been accustomed to in recent memory.
Even if Houston had their eyes set on spending a second round pick to acquire Stroud's former Ohio State teammate in Harrison, this team still had enough future draft picks in their war chest to make a push for Nelson on top of their prior move.
They've got a first, a third, and a fourth round pick for this coming draft, have all of their picks outside of a sixth in 2028, and all of their resources in 2029.
A 2027 third-rounder, paired with a 2028 fourth, could've been just enough to beat Seattle's offer, and should've been at least on the table for the Colts to consider.
Instead, the Texans decided to hold off on Nelson. It remains to be seen whether or not a big deadline swing could still be in the cards, but finding an immediate plug-and-play lineman like Nelson is going to be pretty tough to find elsewhere.
