title: Chargers' Ladd McConkey Could Emerge as Trade Target for AFC Contender
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have exercised a plan to stand pat and hold off trade calls despite being 0-6. They will play two more games before the November tenth trade deadline and the calls will not stop anytime soon and if they fall to 0-8, the front office will have serious decisions to make.
It is no surprise that the Chargers would be receiving trade calls on their best players who may be on expiring deals and not part of the immediate or future plans. Trade rumors have been ongoing since the Chargers started 0-3 and will continue as they look like the walking dead on offense.
Veteran edge rusher Khalil Mack is the most mentioned named amongst NFL insiders and trade rumors circulating the NFL landscape. NFL insider Tomy Pelissero floated ten potential Chargers who could be moved at the deadline, but it appears Mack and running back Kimani Vidal are the only names that have been recurring in discussions.
It is no surprise that other players, including the Chargers' best, are now being floated in trade discussions on sports shows and media segments around NFL-focused media platforms. Given the Chargers' direction and current position to land the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL draft it would not be a shock if teams tried to inquire about seemingly off-limits players.
One Chargers player sure to be floated as a potential trade target is Ladd McConkey. This is especially clear with teams like the Pittsburgh Steelers out there as possible buyers and McConkey would be a good fit and target for Aaron Rodgers' style.
To be clear, it's all speculation on whether the Steelers would reach out to the Chargers to engage in any form regarding McConkey’s availability. If the Steelers front office does try to reach out to Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz regarding the availability of Ladd McConkey, Hortiz should laugh and hang up the phone.
It is clear, the Chargers offense has been a train wreck through the first six weeks of the season. However, Ladd McConkey, who is not healthy right now, has been the only functional target for Justin Herbert when he has been on the field. McConkey is in year three of his rookie contract and has been a reliable target for Justin Herbert since he entered the NFL, he is not a player that should be traded.
There may come a day where the Chargers entertain trade offers from McConkey but it will not be in the middle of this season. If the Steelers are looking for wide receiver help, they will likely look elsewhere.

title: Chargers Miss Out on Quenton Nelson, But Draft Favorite Waiver Target Emerges
full_text:
It has been buzzing for a few weeks that the Los Angeles Chargers could be in contention for the All-Pro guard, Quenton Nelson . Even with the team at 0-6, they have reported to the media the belief in their squad giving reason for the belief they could actually make an offer for the Colts legend.
As of today, Oct. 27, that was not true. The Chargers were reportedly not one of the teams interested in Nelson, with the Seattle Seahawks being the winners of the sweepstakes, giving up a fair price of a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick.
This does not mean that the saga is over. The Chargers could very well look into the Seahawks player who was released in the corresponding move.
Christian Haynes is a 26-year-old offensive guard who was drafted in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft with the 83rd overall pick. Since being drafted, Haynes has started five games for the Hawks, all of those games coming this season.
His 210 offensive snaps of playing time thus far have earned him a 59.7 overall PFF grade, 43rd among 74 qualified offensive guards. His PFF pass-blocking grade of 46.0 ranked 62nd among 74 qualified offensive guards. His run-blocking grade is 62.5, ranking 33rd among the same 74 qualified candidates.
Christian Haynes (RG #64) I did not know he had this in his bag #seahawks pic.twitter.com/FLQfOd4hYW
For reference, Chargers starting right guard Cole Strange , on 387 snaps, which is nearly double Haynes, ranks 67th in overall PFF grade, 69th in pass blocking and 50th in run blocking. Haynes is better in every PFF category.
Furthermore, Haynes has allowed 11 total pressures in pass protection. That total included one sack and three hits allowed to opposing pass rushers. He was flagged for zero penalties over the course of the season.
Strange has allowed one more pressure, two fewer hits and the same number of sacks. He has also been penalized five times with the Bolts. Even if Haynes is only marginally better than Strange, an improvement is still an improvement.
Overall, it is very fitting for the 0-6 team led by Joe Hortiz to go bargain-bin shopping on the second-hand market. Haynes has been released by the Seahawks, making him available on the waiver wire. The Chargers are the worst team in the NFL, with the only week they have not lost being their bye week.
After acquiring All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson, the Seahawks waived guard Christian Haynes to make room on their 53-man roster.
This means the Bolts get the first selection on the waiver wire. If you are going to be the worst team in the NFL, you might as well take advantage of the perks that come with it.

title: Desperate Patriots Could Help Chargers Offload Quentin Johnston, More at NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
When thinking about NFL trade partners for the Los Angeles Chargers , the usual suspects come up.
For example, good luck ducking chatter about the Chargers sending Khalil Mack to the Chicago Bears .
And the Chargers could always go after Brian Thomas of the Jacksonville Jaguars , if they end up wanting to be buyers at the deadline while aiming at finding pieces that help create a long-term fix.
Most likely, though, the 0-6 Chargers limping out of the bye have eyes on acting as big sellers at the NFL trade deadline. That’s especially the case for Mack, who they should do right by as his career winds down.
And it should be the case for guys with any sort of value who might not be around after this season. Quentin Johnston is one name who comes to mind in this category.
Elsewhere in the AFC, the New England Patriots might be able to help the Chargers out.
Those mentioned Patriots are 4-3 in the AFC East, just behind the 5-1 Buffalo Bills. They’re 2-0 in division play, so they’re right there in the hunt.
Mike Vrabel and Co., too, are desperate to prove this year isn’t a bust. The Chargers happen to roster some very Patriots-like players, too.
That’s something recently brought up by Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer, who mentions Mack and Johnston as obvious Patriots fits.
“I think stylistically he would really fit Mike Vrabel as a bigger, more rugged edge,” Breer said, according to Michael Hurley of NBC Sports Boston. “Quentin Johnston's another player that you could look at, somebody that may not have a future in Los Angeles."
Mack signed another one-year deal with the Chargers this past offseason after weighing retirement. Shipping him to a possible contender would make plenty of sense, even if the return wouldn’t be that big now.
When it comes to Johnston, the former first-round pick had the team pick up his fifth-year option. The Chargers saw a deal, but Johnston’s limitations as a route-runner and drop issues have popped up again. Through five appearances, he’s third on the Chargers in receiving with just eight catches on 21 targets.
Even if the Chargers don’t keep rolling with Mike McDaniel’s system for the rest of the year or even into 2027, it wouldn’t make sense to keep Johnston. At this point, the non-Ladd McConkey aspects of the depth chart probably need thrown out, especially if they remain on track for Jeremiah Smith at No. 1 overall in next year’s draft.
For the Chargers, a team like the Patriots is a really good example of a franchise worth calling often over the next few weeks, even if it’s just used as a leverage play against other buys while trying to find the best value possible at the deadline while selling.

title: Ranking Chargers' Top NFL Trade Deadline Targets From Realistic to Delusional
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6 and the front office's plan to stand pat will be put to the test before the November 10th trade deadline. The Chargers have no business being buyers at the trade deadline with the season essentially lost and the injury list substantial . However, could they convince themselves to make moves for the future? Potentially, but at what cost?
NFL insiders such as Jordan Schultz have been adamant that he believes the trade market will be very active this year. Historically, the NFL trade deadline has been an overhyped affair with few trades actually taking place. That historic trend has started to shift to move activity on the trade market in recent years. If the Chargers for some reason want in on the action, here are some trade targets they could pursue if they want to get wild.
Former first-round pick Brian Thomas Jr is in his third year in the NFL and has not found a home with Liam Coen's offense since Coen's arrival in Jacksonville. After posting a 1,200-yard season as a rookie in 2024, Thomas has seen his target share decline almost weekly.
Thomas is off to a very slow start in 2026 despite the Jaguars winning and throwing the ball all over the field with Trevor Lawrence. Thomas has only nine receptions on the year for 105 yards and could clearly benefit from a change of scenery. However, the Jaguars are winning and have eyes on contending.
Jacksonville will not part with one of their starters while he is on a rookie contract simply because he hasn't fit into the offense as well as they hoped. Wide receiver depth is needed in the NFL. If they were losing, this would be a different story.
Is it possible the Jaguars would entertain the right offer? Sure, but because of his production or lack thereof, his value is at an all-time low. Chargers wide receiver Quentin Johnston has been more productive than Thomas this season.
For the Jaguars to move off of him midseason as they are trying to reach the playoffs and contend they would have to get undeniable draft compensation. Considering the going rate for a struggling former 2024 first-round wide receiver is a second-round pick, Thomas would like cost the Chargers their third-round pick. I doubt the Jaguars will move Thomas midseason but NFL insider Adam Schefter did mention Thomas as a name to watch before the deadline but this feels more like an offseason move.
Some names to watch ahead of the NFL’s Nov. 10 trade deadline: pic.twitter.com/6THEK7IFqT
Cowboys owner Jerry Jones loves to wheel and deal. The Cowboys are in a relatively weak division this season with the Giants surprisingly in first place so moving off of their swing guard is not in their best interest for this season with a winnable division in front of them.
However, the Cowboys have been experiencing some injuries to the depth in their defensive back and linebacker rooms and the Chargers have been starting rookies all over their offensive line but have depth at both safety and linebacker. Jones has already shown a willingness to trade to address the defense, could there be a deal to reunite former Oregon teammates TJ Bass and Justin Herbert?
More than likely any potential trade would be a player for player swap plus draft pick. Bass is scheduled to be a unrestricted free agent in the coming offseason and the Chargers could take the rest of the year to gauge whether Bass would be a good fit moving forward while trying to keep quarterback Justin Herbert standing long enough to see 2027 in one piece.
The Colts have signaled they are open for business by trading away All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson. Keenan Allen was a late signing for the Colts and he has slowly become a reliable receiving target with Alec Pierce done for the season. The Colts have other wide receivers that could fill in if Allen was no longer there.
It is no secret that Justin Herbert trusts Keenan Allen. Ladd McConkey has been injured all season and with Herbert completely out of rhythm in Mike McDaniel's offense, it may be worth bringing Allen back to help give Herbert any semblance of confidence. Acquiring Allen would not cost much given his circumstances, potentially a late-round swap. It may be worth it to help Herbert get back on track and head to 2027 with some positive momentum.

title: Chargers Should Aggressively Take Advantage of the Endless Bears Trade Rumors
full_text:
Every public suggestion around the Los Angeles Chargers says Jim Harbaugh, Joe Hortiz and the organization out West won’t host a fire sale at the NFL trade deadline .
It’s not a shocking public stance right now. It also won’t be shocking when actions speak louder than words and they end up selling big. Harbaugh’s Chargers are the worst team in football at 0-6 and top the NFL draft order for good reason .
In related news, every public suggestion hints that the Chicago Bears are about to be big buyers at the upcoming NFL trade deadline.
This is related for one simple link between the teams: A guy named Khalil Mack.
For those out of the loop, the Bears are 5-2 and just behind the 6-0 Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North. The need for more pass-rushers and other all-in moves is obvious.
Among the many bits of reporting, Jordan Schultz appeared on The Pivot and linked the Bears and 49ers to Mack.
“Two teams I’m watching very closely, the 49ers and Bears,” Schultz said. “I’ve heard both teams connected to several defensive players, including rushers Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack and also DeForest Buckner…I’d be shocked if they don’t make a move before the deadline.”
Chargers fans don’t need to be told that Mack going to the Bears would be a reunion. In the process, the Chargers would do right by him by letting him go contend for a title.
Mack, after all, pondered retirement before coming back to the Chargers for at least one more year on an $18 million contract. He’s still playing at a high level for a defense that is slowly morphing into form after an adjustment period since the arrival of new coordinator Chris O’Leary.
In theory, the Chargers could sweeten the pot on a trade and up the return a bit by offering to absorb some of Mack’s remaining money on the one-year deal. But the overall return will be minimal. Even multiple teams interested in Mack won’t drive up the value that much.
The silver lining on a Mack trade, beyond just doing right by him, means even more developmental reps for the likes of Tuli Tuipulotu and first-round pick Akheem Mesidor.
And at this point, 0-6 is 0-6. A few wins won’t change this soon-to-be-selling outlook for the Chargers. But it’s especially true with Mack, as there’s no real reason to keep him around on a sinking ship after what he’s done for the franchise. Shipping him out to a franchise he’s familiar with and giving him a shot at a title is a no-brainer, especially with the rumors stressing just how active the Bears want to be at the deadline.

title: The Perfect Trade Target for the Chargers May Have Just Become Available
full_text:
Brian Thomas Jr. is a name worth keeping an eye on as the NFL trade deadline approaches, and the Chargers could have a legitimate opportunity to add a receiver who still has plenty of potential.
Between his place in the offense, the receivers competing for targets and the struggles that have followed an incredible rookie campaign, Thomas has become a fascinating trade candidate.
According to NFL insider Adam Schefter , Thomas Jr. is a name to watch out for. Also stating that the Jags “might be willing to listen” to offers.
It is easy to forget just how impressive Thomas looked as a rookie. He finished the 2024 season with 1,282 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. Establishing himself as one of the most exciting young receivers in the league. He had the speed to get behind defensive backs, the length to make difficult catches and the ability to turn a routine pass into a game-changing play.
The problem is that the production has not continued at that level. His numbers fell considerably in 2025, and his involvement has become even more limited this season. The recent decision to keep him on the sideline for an entire second half only added to the uncertainty surrounding his future.
But the bigger question is whether Thomas is in the right situation to get the most out of his abilities.
Liam Coen’s offense has evolved around the players who are producing consistently, and Thomas has struggled to take advantage of his opportunities. His issues with drops and consistency cannot simply be blamed on the scheme. At the same time, an offense that has found other reliable options has less reason to keep forcing targets toward a receiver who is not making the most of them.
Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington have earned important roles, while rookie Josh Cameron has also started to receive more opportunities. Travis Hunter adds another layer to the receiving picture as well. With more competition for snaps and targets, Thomas no longer has the same clear path to opportunities that he once did.
That is what makes a potential trade interesting. A change of scenery would not automatically fix his problems, but it could give him a chance to rebuild his confidence and find a role better suited to his strengths. Herbert would be an intriguing quarterback for that process. His arm strength and willingness to attack downfield could allow Thomas to get back to doing what made him such a dangerous receiver in the first place. The Chargers would not need to reinvent the player. They would need to help him become a more consistent version of himself.
The biggest question is what the Chargers would have to give up to make this happen.
Thomas was a first-round pick for a reason, and his rookie season is still a reminder of the ceiling he possesses. However, teams cannot ignore what has happened since then. His declining production and recent reduction in playing time should affect his trade value, particularly when there is no guarantee that his early-career success will return.
I would be interested in exploring a deal built around a Day 2 or conditional draft pick, depending on what the front office learns about his development and the asking price. Giving up a premium selection without understanding the reasons behind his struggles would be a gamble.
Landing him for a more manageable price, on the other hand, could make the risk worthwhile.
There is also the financial side of the decision. The Chargers would need to evaluate his contract, future commitments and how a potential acquisition fits into their longer-term plans. Adding another receiver is only worthwhile if it does not prevent the team from addressing other needs. Still, the potential reward is hard to overlook. Thomas has already demonstrated that he can produce at an elite level, and he is young enough that a turnaround could benefit a team for years rather than just a few weeks.
The Bolts need to be confident that the problems are correctable and that the price makes sense. But if those conditions are met, this is a conversation worth having. Thomas might not be the guaranteed solution some fans are looking for, but he could represent an opportunity to add legitimate upside to Herbert’s supporting cast without paying the price normally associated with a receiver coming off a breakout season.

title: When is Myles Garrett Actually Playing for the Rams Again? Things Are Murky
full_text:
With every passing week, the uncertainty around the Los Angeles Rams and edge rusher Myles Garrett continues to grow. Despite NFL Media’s I an Rapoport reporting last week that the expectation was for Garrett to return to practice this week, the Rams will not be activating his 21-day practice window.
Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson will not practice this week, Sean McVay said.
Ever since the Rams traded for Garrett, something hasn’t been right. Garrett first missed practice at the beginning of training camp with what was described as lower-body soreness. He missed three straight practices in early August. While he was in and out of practice for a few weeks, Garrett missed the last few weeks of training camp entirely and didn’t return until Week 1.
Garrett played in Week 1, but said after the game that he didn’t feel like himself. He was then placed on injured reserve after undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery. Following the surgery, many reported a six-week timeline, calling that a worst-case scenario, and that Garrett was determined to beat that timeline.
With Garrett not returning to practice this week, his timeline continues to get extended. We are now 6.5 weeks post-surgery and Sunday will be the seventh consecutive game that Garrett has missed. Without Garrett, the Rams rank 18th in pressure rate on defense and 28th in sack rate. That’s down from being second in pressure rate and ninth in sack rate last season.
Since the beginning, the Rams have lacked transparency when it came to Garrett. They've never explained what caused Garrett’s knee injury or even what the specific injury was. Garrett has only been described as having lower-body soreness and knee swelling.
The entire situation has been murky from the jump and the Rams haven’t helped at all by providing any sort of clarity. For much of the offseason, McVay said that the team was simply erring on the side of caution. With Garrett set to miss Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers, Garrett will not have played a healthy snap for the Rams as we get into November.
At this point, it’s worth wondering when the Rams will see Garrett back on the field. The Rams are taking it week-by-week, but will it be next week on the road against the Washington Commanders? Does he come back after the bye week? Will Garrett play again in 2026?
Right now, there is no clear answer. The earliest Garrett could return is Week 9 against the Commanders, but with the Rams not even ready to open his practice window, a return following the Week 11 bye may be more realistic.
For the most part, this has been mismanagement from the Rams’ training staff and has only been emphasized by the lack of transparency. While the team and Garrett likely wanted to avoid surgery, it can be argued that Garrett should have gotten the surgery back in August. It’s also worth wondering whether the Rams did their due diligence, considering that Garrett’s knee injury popped up all the way back in training camp.
Those are all fair questions with Garrett set to be out another week and the continued lack of transparency. He’s spent almost half the season on injured reserve with no signs of coming off of it anytime soon.
The Rams traded a promising young edge rusher and two first-round picks for Garrett, and he hasn’t played a healthy snap for the team. While Jared Verse doesn’t have a sack yet this season, he does have a 10.1 percent pressure rate, which is higher than both Josaiah Stewart and Wesley Bailey. It’s also worth noting that Verse hasn’t been a good fit and has had to adjust to the Browns’ 4-3 defense.
When the Rams traded for Garrett, the expectation was that he would be the missing piece on a Super Bowl-caliber roster. Instead, the Rams are heading into Week 8 with more questions than answers. The elite edge rusher that they traded for hasn’t played since Week 1, and even then he wasn’t healthy.
Until Garrett returns to practice, there’s no reason to believe his return is imminent or that he returns before the bye week. The question isn’t just when Garrett will play for the Rams, but whether they will ever get the player they traded for and the impact they expected from their biggest offseason acquisition. That's a concerning position for the Rams to be in, especially considering what they gave up to acquire him.

title: Rams Sign Josh Karty, Jake McQuaide in Surprising Special Teams Moves
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams continue their attempt to improve their special teams uni t. On Wednesday, the Rams signed long snapper Jake McQuaide and kicker Josh Karty to the practice squad.
Through the first seven weeks of the season, the Rams have struggled on special teams and it’s become a point of emphasis for head coach Sean McVay. The Rams currently rank 32nd in special teams DVOA and gave up two long returns as well as a fake punt against the Las Vegas Raiders.
“I have to figure that out. It's one of those deals that’s driving me crazy. We have to figure it out and we haven't yet,” said McVay when he spoke to the media on Monday.
McQuaide visited the Rams on Wednesday. He spent the first 10 years of his career with the Rams and signed with them last year after they moved on from Alex Ward. The McQuaide signing does come as a surprise, as Joe Cardona was signed in the offseason and seen as a player favored by Bubba Ventrone. While the Rams haven’t been good on special teams, Cardona has been one of the few bright spots.
Whether McQuaide replaces Cardona or is simply there to provide a veteran presence as someone McVay trusts remains to be seen. However, it would be odd for the Rams to keep two long snappers available.
The addition of Josh Karty is just as surprising. Last season, the Rams cut Karty after he had issues with timing and kicks getting blocked. Karty was 10-for-15 last year and had two field goals blocked that would have given the Rams the win against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Additionally, last week, the Rams signed kicker Brandon McManus to add some stability to the field goal unit after they moved on from Harrison Mevis. McManus went 5-for-5 on extra points last week.
It seems unlikely that the Rams would move on from McManus, but Karty gives the Rams a younger option to develop on the practice squad. Karty was seen as a talented kicker at one point. From the end of his rookie season until his two kicks being blocked against the Eagles, Karty had made 21 straight field goals and was 5-for-5 from 50+ yards during that stretch.
Another aspect of signing Karty is what he can do on kickoffs. Some have speculated that the knuckleball kickoff messed up his kicking form, but the Rams implemented it last season with Karty and had success with it.
Given some of the Rams’ issues on their kickoff coverage unit, it wouldn’t be surprising if they brought up Karty on game days or found a roster spot for him just to take kickoff responsibilities. The Rams can also hope to develop Karty with the idea that he can possibly overtake McManus at some point.
The Rams have created the best field position on kickoffs this season. Blocked FGs overshadowed what was a GREAT performance from Karty. This knuckleball on the kickoff has been a weapon for the Rams STs unit. pic.twitter.com/FbbxJN3fdw
In a corresponding move, the Rams released offensive lineman Austin Blaske. Blaske was signed as an undrafted free agent and seemed to play well during the preseason. However, with the Rams prioritizing special teams , they have opted to part ways with Blaske. The signings of Karty and McQuaide also come after the Rams bringing in Jon Rhattigan on Tuesday.
McVay has made it clear that the Rams' special teams performance isn't acceptable, and the moves to bring back McQuaide and Karty are another indication that the team is searching for answers. It's uncertain whether either player will make an immediate impact, but the Rams are certainly making an effort to improve.

title: How Rams' Week 7 Win Changes Their NFL Trade Deadline Plans
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams entered Week 7 of the NFL season at a crossroads. With a win against the Las Vegas Raiders, they would be back in playoff contention . However, dropping to 2-5 with a loss would have forced them to have some uncomfortable conversations.
At 2-5, the Rams’ season likely would have been over. At that point, the Rams may have needed to consider trading assets for draft capital and start focusing on 2027 with the hope that they would have their stars healthy to start the year. Had the Rams dropped to 2-5, it’s possible that they would have started shopping Byron Young, Braden Fiske, and others in hopes of stocking up for 2027.
However, the Rams are in a much different spot at 3-4. With three winnable games on the schedule, they could realistically enter their bye in Week 11 at 6-4 and in a prime position to push for a playoff spot. Over the next three weeks, the Rams will play the Los Angeles Chargers, Washington Commanders, and Arizona Cardinals. The Rams need to take care of business , but they have a realistic path back into the NFC playoff picture.
That may not be where the Rams saw themselves at the beginning of the season, but it puts them in a position where they can be more aggressive at the trade deadline than they would at 2-5. At the very least, it allows the Rams to evaluate the roster, see where their needs are, and explore opportunities. If the opportunity fits, they have the ability to capitalize on it.
With that said, that doesn’t mean that the Rams need to make another all-in blockbuster-type trade. In a sense, that might be possible, but it’s certainly not necessary. The Rams can live with the idea that the return of Myles Garrett and Terrance Ferguson are similar to making two in-season acquisitions. The addition of Garrett once he comes back from injury should provide a major boost to the defense.
At the same time, the Rams still have needs on the roster. Since the offseason, the Rams have needed a more reliable third wide receiver . With the season-ending injury to Poona Ford, an argument can be made that the Rams need a run-stuffing nose tackle. The Rams have had issues on special teams and could look to make additions there as well.
It’s important that the Rams don’t confuse beating a struggling Raiders team with proving that their problems have been fixed. The performance against the Raiders was encouraging, but the Rams still need to show that consistently, which is something that they haven’t done this season.
Sitting at 3-4 with a 38 percent chance of making the playoffs, as opposed to sitting at 2-5, gives the Rams the ability to trade away minor future assets and continue strengthening the roster for a potential Super Bowl run.
With the win against the Raiders, the Rams can be calculated buyers at the trade deadline . They don’t need to overpay for a player to provide a short-term boost like Von Miller in 2021. However, if Snead can acquire a player who addresses a clear need without sacrificing significant future resources, it’s a move worth considering. Some of Snead’s best trades have been low-value targets such as Austin Corbett and Kevin Dotson.
That has been the goal since they made the move for Trent McDuffie back in April. Again, they don’t necessarily need to make a blockbuster move, but another piece that might better position them in a competitive NFC makes sense.
The Rams aren’t in a position to stand pat and do nothing as they remain in the middle of the playoff hunt. The Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers have both shown a willingness to be aggressive at the trade deadline. Additionally, the Rams have already committed to winning this season. After saving their season with a win, the Rams can continue on that path.
By beating the Raiders, the Rams gave themselves new life. With the trade deadline quickly approaching, the Rams have the flexibility now to address some of their weaknesses and properly compete for a playoff spot. If the Rams believe they can still compete for a Super Bowl, they need to approach the trade deadline with that same mindset.

title: Rams Must Act Quickly to Land Josh Downs Before NFL Trade Deadline
full_text:
With the NFL trade deadline approaching, the Los Angeles Rams have reportedly been active on the phones, especially for a wide receiver. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported last week that the Rams were exploring wide receiver options and added on Wednesday that they are a team that could acquire help at the trade deadline.
The Rams will certainly have their options. However, on Tuesday, the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers took advantage of the Indianapolis Colts’ fire sale . It wouldn’t be surprising if the Rams did the same, especially when it comes to wide receiver Josh Downs.
Given the injury to Davante Adams, the Rams could use wide receiver help. Even when Adams returns, the Rams need to upgrade their third wide receiver spot, which is where Downs fits best in their offensive infrastructure.
While the Colts had already been taking calls on Downs, on Wednesday morning, the wide receiver officially requested a trade, likely with the hope to fast-track something. As it stands, a trade for Downs isn’t considered likely this week, but the expectation is that a trade will eventually happen, according to Jordan Schultz.
Sources: Colts WR Josh Downs is requesting a trade from Indianapolis. pic.twitter.com/rwGaVGMTFf
If the Rams have interest in Downs, they may need to act quickly with how the Colts are moving on from players they don’t see as part of their future. While Downs is having a down year, no pun intended, he still has 122 more yards than Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, and Jordan Whittington combined. Downs’ yards per route run and targets per route run are also both higher than all three, despite having a larger sample.
The market for Downs appears to be competitive at this point, adding more urgency for the Rams to get something done quickly. While there is some concern about Downs’ size and how he could be used in the McVay offense, he does give the Rams flexibility once Adams returns.
Downs may be a slot-only player, making him a more difficult projection in the Rams’ offense. Still, the Rams have operated out of 11 personnel at a 55.9 percent rate this season. When they have had to go to three wide receivers, it’s been difficult for them to trust Mumpfield, Whittington, and Atwell.
4 clips of the Colts in 12 personnel in 2025 with Josh Downs and Alec Pierce as the 2 WRs on the field. Can see the "slot" formations (two WRs on the same side of the field) that they created on most of these plays. It's a classic play action shot play formation that also gets… pic.twitter.com/UAAUfumgSl
When the Rams have been in 11 personnel this season, Mumpfield has a -0.07 EPA per target, while Whittington has a -0.24 EPA per target. While Atwell has been better, he’s only been targeted twice. It’s clear that the Rams only see him as a clear-out player.
That WR3 spot is an area where the Rams need an upgrade once Adams returns, and Downs would provide exactly that. While Downs may be the same size as Atwell, they are not similar players. Downs is a much better separator, wins in the intermediate and short areas of the field rather than just vertically, and provides value as a punt returner.
He’s much more akin to Zay Flowers than Atwell.Downs and Flowers are both compact, twitchy wide receivers with quickness, change-of-direction ability, and route-running skills. Downs has speed, but winning vertically isn’t his specialty.
Josh Downs is a completely effortless mover, sheesh. Incredibly electric. Don't love him in traffic/contested catch situations/outside, but he creates a ton of separation and has rocket launchers attached to his cleats https://t.co/VHC5g6a2uL pic.twitter.com/jZOPpUBlFL
While Downs is smaller, he is still a willing blocker, and that’s an area where he’s improved over his four-year career. Downs was expected to be able to block in a Colts offense that featured Jonathan Taylor. According to PFF, Downs had 108 run-blocking snaps during the first six weeks of the season and had a 64.2 run-blocking grade. Mumpfield has a smaller frame as well and had a 59.7 run-blocking grade on 54 snaps. At some point, the Rams have to prioritize athleticism and speed in the offense.
If the Rams are going to make a move, the time for them to make it is now. The Colts aren’t waiting to move on from players, and Downs has a market. If the Rams believe Downs can help provide a reliable option and be an upgrade over their current options, they can’t afford to sit back and wait. The opportunity is there, and it’s up to Les Snead to make it happen.

title: What the Rams can Realistically Afford at the Trade Deadline
full_text:
As the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers take an aggressive approach ahead of the NFL trade deadline, the Los Angeles Rams are stuck contemplating what type of move they can make to keep pace. The Rams are in a different spot than both of those teams as they made moves for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie in the offseason. At the same time, they still have a roster with very clear flaws.
The Rams are set to get reinforcements over the next few weeks as Garrett hopefully returns and they should also get Terrance Ferguson back. Kobie Turner will return at some point and Davante Adams should be back in time for a playoff run as well.
Still, with the Seahawks trading for Quenton Nelson and the 49ers acquiring DeForest Buckner and still looking to improve, the Rams may need to find ways to respond . Simply having the mindset that getting Garrett, Turner, and Adams back counts as your midseason acquisitions isn't the correct approach.
However, the dilemma is finding a trade that the Rams can afford. They traded their first and third-round picks next year and don’t have their second-round pick in 2028. They also only have around $206,000 in cap space, according to OverTheCap.
The biggest constraint right now for a trade is the team’s cap space. They won’t be able to make a move if they don’t open up some money. However, that’s something they will likely need to do anyway as it isn’t feasible to make it through the rest of the season on $206,000.
While the Rams don’t like to restructure existing contracts, it is something they’ll need to do at some point. Earlier this year, the Rams had to restructure Quentin Lake’s contract, which opened up $3.4 million. The most realistic option would be to restructure Kyren Williams’ contract and open up around that same amount. They could also look to do the same to Alaric Jackson’s deal, but Williams may be the safer option.
If the Rams can open up around $3.5 million, that opens up the possibility for several trades. Brian Thomas Jr. would only cost the Rams around $600,000 for the remainder of the season. A move for Josh Downs would be a little more complicated as he would cost $2.4 million for the year. However, the Rams may be able to give up more for the Colts to agree to pay more of his salary. The Colts currently have $37 million in cap space. If the Rams were to trade for Quentin Johnston, he would cost $1.4 million.
The Rams may only have $206,000 in cap space right now, but they have the flexibility to make almost any move work. The Rams have made it a point to keep their cap situation clean post-2022. If they want to take an all-in approach, they have some flexibility to move money around and make it work.
Aside from their cap situation, the Rams also have to consider their future draft picks. They currently only have second, fourth, fifth, and sixth-round picks in the 2027 NFL Draft. However, things open up again in 2028 when the only selection they are missing is a second-round pick.
Moving off of their second-round pick in 2027 feels unlikely and irresponsible. If the Rams trade away their 2027 second-round pick, they wouldn’t select until the fourth round and would only be left with three picks.
However, the 2028 draft is mostly available. Ideally, the Rams would want to keep their 2028 first-round pick. However, the Rams could pair a fourth-round pick in 2027 and a conditional late-round pick in 2028 to still get a player.
It simply depends on how much the Rams want to give up in a trade. If they make a move for Downs, they may only have to give up a fifth- or sixth-round pick in 2027 to get that done. Downs is in the final year of his rookie contract with just nine games to play.
A move for Thomas could be more expensive . Realistically, Thomas would cost a second-round pick. If the Jaguars are hellbent on a second-round pick, it’s hard for the Rams to justify giving that up. If the Jaguars are desperate to move off of Thomas and his value is a third or fourth-round pick, a move is much more possible.
If the Rams were to give up a Day 3 pick for Downs, it wouldn’t be mortgaging the future even if they were unable to re-sign him. Additionally, it’s possible the Rams could get a compensatory pick in return for Downs in 2028.
The only thing possibly keeping the Rams from making a move at the trade deadline is their cap space. There are still moves that can be made that don’t also mortgage their future. Even then, the Rams have the cap flexibility to make something work.
It’s true that the Rams are going to get important players back from injury at some point. Because of that, they don’t necessarily need to make another blockbuster move. A trade for a role player like Downs, who would improve their wide receiver depth, is enough. With the Seahawks and 49ers continuing to be aggressive, the Rams can’t afford to sit back and hope that just getting healthy will solve everything. If the Rams still believe this team can compete for a Super Bowl, they need to make a move to show that.

title: Rams Shake Up Practice Squad, Sign Linebacker Jon Rhattigan to Address Special Teams Struggles
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams made a handful of roster moves on Tuesday, with the hope that their newest addition will help them on special teams . The Rams signed linebacker Jon Rhattigan to their practice squad and terminated the contracts of cornerback Nyzier Fourqurean and linebacker Eli Neal.
Over the first seven weeks of the season, the Rams have been trying to figure out how to improve on special teams. Against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Rams gave up a 36-yard kickoff return and then a 42-yard kickoff return before opting to just kick the ball out of the back of the end zone.
“It was not good enough. We've talked about this a lot and it has to get fixed. It's not good enough and we cannot allow ourselves to do that,” said head coach Sean McVay. “I have to figure that out. It's one of those deals that’s driving me crazy. We have to figure it out and we haven't yet.”
It’s somewhat surprising that the Rams cut Neal after he’s been with the team for the last three years on and off the practice squad. Neal had been active in two games this year, but not since Week 3. The Rams will hope that Rhattigan can help their issues on the coverage unit.
Rhattigan was an undrafted free agent out of Army in 2021 and spent three seasons with the Seattle Seahawks. He was with the Bears this summer but was released during roster cuts. Rhattigan has played 1,270 special teams snaps in his career. In 2022 with the Seahawks, he had a 90.1 special teams grade via PFF. Last season, Rhattigan had 2 tackles on special teams, but was credited with six missed tackles.
The Rams signing Rhattigan is another sign that they are continuing to bring in players to try and fix their issues on special teams. This is likely something that the Rams will have to address in the offseason, but McVay understands it’s a problem and they are doing what they can at this point.
Also among the roster cuts was Fourqurean. This offseason, the Rams signed a pair of undrafted cornerbacks in Fourqurean and Al’Zillion Hamilton. Hamilton was part of the first roster cutdowns and was not brought back on the practice squad. Fourqurean has now been cut as well after performing well in the preseason. It is worth noting that the Rams signed cornerback Damarion Williams two weeks ago, and Williams may have surpassed Fourqurean on the depth chart.
As another note on the transaction wire, the Rams also had long snapper Jake McQuaide in for a visit. Earlier this offseason, the Rams signed Joe Cardona to be their long snapper, so McQuaide coming in for a visit is certainly interesting. McQuaide spent his first 10 years with the Rams and was brought back last year after the team cut Alex Ward.
It's clear that the Rams aren't satisfied with how things have gone on special teams, and Tuesday's roster moves are another example of their efforts to address those issues. Rhattigan may provide some help on the coverage unit, but it remains to be seen how much of an impact he’ll have.

title: Blake Corum Is the Key to the Rams Turning Their Season Around and Making a Playoff Run
full_text:
When the Los Angeles Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6, it was rock bottom . The offense scored 16 points against a struggling Cardinals defense, and the Rams fell at home to the bottom-dweller of the NFC West
On Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, the Rams leaned on Blake Corum to spark the offense along with Kyren Williams and a steady run game. Corum and Williams combined for 192 yards rushing as the offense found its identity . They became the first running back duo since Marshall Faulk and Trung Candidate to each rush for over 90 yards in the same regular season game.
Throughout the McVay era, there have been times when the offense has gone through ruts. In 2018, the Rams lost two out of three games and didn’t look like themselves during that stretch. During the 2021 season, the Rams went through “No win November” and Stafford was plagued with turnovers. The offense turned the ball over seven times across three games.
In every case, the Rams simply got back to what they did best. The foundation of the McVay offense is built around the run game.
“Any good offense that we've had here that I've been a part of, you have to be able to do both,” said head coach Sean McVay after the game. “You have to be able to have balance, or you at least have to have the threat of if they overcommit to something, then you have to be able to make them pay.”
During Weeks 16 and 17 in 2018, C.J. Anderson had 43 carries for 299 yards. In the playoffs, the Rams beat the Cowboys on the back of Anderson and Todd Gurley rushing 39 times for 238 yards and three touchdowns.
When the Rams went through 'No Win November,' they leaned on Sony Michel after struggling to find consistency in the run game all year. Michel had 20 carries in Week 3 of the 2021 season. He didn’t have another game with 20 or more carries until Week 13.
Between Week 13 and 18, Michel had a league-high 129 carries and rushed for 540 yards, which ranked third. During that span, the Rams had just a +3.2 pass rate over expected compared to +5.5 during the losing streak.
With Williams on injured reserve in 2023, the Rams went 1-3 and fell to 4-6. Once Williams came back, he had 20 carries in five of the next six games, including 25 or more in Weeks 14 and 15 as the Rams went 5-1.
From Weeks 12-17, Williams ranked second in EPA per rush and led the NFL in rushing success rate. Williams had the most rushing attempts and yards during that span as well. The Rams had a +1.3 pass rate over expected over those six games.
That’s what the Rams needed to get back to last week. They needed to simplify things on offense. During the first six weeks of the season, Stafford led the NFL in passing attempts. The Rams ranked fifth in pass-rate over expected at +4.9 and it was at +7.7 between Weeks 3-6. In Week 7, the Rams had a +0.8 pass rate over expected. They were much more balanced .
“When you're able to do that, you're not in a bunch of bad spots on second down and on third down and a lot of things can come off of that,” McVay said. “I thought that was the first game that was reflected. We were able to really do some of the things that I've been in alignment with when we've been able to operate at a pretty decent clip offensively.”
While the Rams have a steady rushing attack with Kyren Williams, it lacks a creative dimension when he’s the only player involved. After Corum and Williams split carries in Week 2 against the New York Giants, the running game lacked that 1-2 punch.
Kyren Williams and Blake Corum's rushing charts shows exactly why they work well together. A lot more green/consistency from Williams, but Corum brings big-play ability. The answer to a dominant Rams' run game is using both in a 50-50 split. pic.twitter.com/TFVhtWlDac
From Weeks 2-6, Williams had 57 carries to Corum’s 25. Week 2 was also the last time that Corum had more than 10 carries in a game. On Sunday against the Raiders , Corum led the Rams with 17 carries to Williams’ 16. Again, they combined for 192 yards. Corum finished with 93 yards but had potential for more, as he had two touchdowns, including one from 43 yards, called back because of penalties.
“I thought he saw the holes well. I thought he pressed the line of scrimmage. It's a bummer the one long one came back. You see the explosiveness, though,” McVay said after the game. “It's something that we have to build on because this is a long journey. I thought this was a good step in the right direction, and you could feel that throughout the course of the week by the way the guys approached it.”
Over the last two seasons, when Williams and Corum each have 10 or more carries, the Rams average 0.03 EPA per rush with a 50.6 percent rushing success rate. When Williams has 10 or more carries and Corum does not, they average -0.07 EPA per rush with a 46.1 percent rushing success rate.
The best version of the Rams’ rushing attack is one that includes a heavy dose of Corum alongside Williams. Both players complement each other well, as Williams helps keep the offense on track while Corum has more burst and big-play ability.
Blake Corum: really good at football pic.twitter.com/NH2qHvjL4D
Getting Corum more involved and McVay committing to the run game are what will get the Rams back on track and back to the team that many expected coming into the season. In past years, the Rams have leaned on Stafford. However, they don’t need Stafford throwing 40 times per game when they have Corum and Williams.
The Rams have two running backs capable of making an impact, but that advantage means very little if only one is consistently involved. If the Rams are going to build on their win against the Raiders and turn their season around, Corum needs to remain a focal point of the offense.

title: Rams Face Mounting Trade Deadline Pressure as NFC West Rivals Make Major Moves
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams may have changed the course of their season with a win over the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, but they still have work to do to remain competitive. The NFC West remains one of the more competitive divisions in the NFL. With the Seattle Seahawks trading for All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson , and the San Francisco 49ers acquiring DeForest Buckner, the pressure is on for the Rams to make a corresponding move if they want to remain competitive with the Seahawks and 49ers.
While the 49ers may be the favorites to win the division, the battle for second place and a wild card spot in the playoffs is up for grabs. After the Seahawks beat the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, it’s clear they believe they are in position to push for that spot and do what they can to try and repeat.
The Seahawks making this type of move at 4-3 is a testament to how competitive the NFC West is as a division. Since the beginning of 2025, the Seahawks are 22-3 when Anthony Bradford starts at guard. Bradford has helped activate some of the things they do in the run game and allowed them to be more balanced on offense. Adding Nelson allows the Seahawks to be dominant in the run game and keep the interior clean for quarterback Sam Darnold.
Despite the 49ers leading the division, they responded with a move of their own with Buckner. Buckner gives the 49ers a dominant run-stopping defensive lineman that they've been lacking. It keeps them firmly ahead in the NFC West.
While the 49ers lead the group, the Rams and Seahawks will be competing very closely for a final wild card spot, especially with how strong the NFC North is currently. Between the Rams, Seahawks, and 49ers, all three are consistently looking to improve and seek out ways they can one-up the other. There are only three playoff spots available and five teams competing for those spots.
While the Rams made moves for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie earlier in the summer, Garrett has yet to play and McDuffie has missed each of the last two games. Simply sticking with the status quo may not be enough to make a legitimate push for one of those playoff spots, especially with the Seahawks pushing more of their chips into the middle of the table.
At the end of the day, this is still a Rams roster with its flaws. With the injury to Davante Adams, the Rams have a need for a wide receiver. Even if Adams comes back, the Rams need an upgrade at their third wide receiver spot over Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield. If the Rams don’t make a move there, it could come back to haunt them in the same way that ignoring the cornerback position did last season.
Additionally, the Rams could use a defensive tackle as well. Poona Ford is out for the season and Kobie Turner is on injured reserve. The Rams have depth on the defensive line, but it’s hard to promote some of that depth into a full-time role and expect to get the same production for half a season.
The Rams have options here to explore with Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Downs, and others. It simply comes down to how big of a move the Rams want to make and what they feel like they can afford. Les Snead doesn’t necessarily need to make a blockbuster move, but the Rams do need to be aggressive and show they aren’t waving the white flag on this season despite some of the injuries.
This isn’t necessarily about the Rams making a trade simply because the Seahawks did. However, the Seahawks’ willingness to give up draft capital to improve their roster should still increase the urgency for the Rams to do the same. The Rams have already invested heavily in competing for a Super Bowl this season, and can’t afford to fall further behind while a division rival looks to do the same.
Last season, the Rams lost an opportunity to compete for a Super Bowl because they lost to the Seahawks when it mattered. At that time, it was the Seahawks making a move for Rashid Shaheed that helped push them over the edge. It was Shaheed that sparked the comeback in Week 16 with his punt return for a touchdown. The Rams can’t afford to stand pat and watch a division rival surpass them again in a season when they were supposed to compete for a Super Bowl.
It’s true that the Rams will get healthier. Garrett is nearing a return, McDuffie could be back this week, and Terrance Ferguson should be back soon as well. However, the Rams can’t treat those players coming back as midseason additions. The Seahawks have made their move. With the Rams' Super Bowl hopes still hanging in the balance, it's time for Snead to make his.

title: Rams Trade Deadline Big Board: Realistic Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams needed to beat the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday to warrant making any move before the trade deadline. Had the Rams dropped to 2-5, an argument can be made that the Rams should have considered moving on from players they didn’t plan on re-signing. However, with the win, the Rams are right back in the hunt.
If the Rams were to make a trade, making a move for a wide receiver appears to be the most realistic. However, given some injuries at other positions, the Rams will likely keep their options open. They could trade for a defensive lineman if the right opportunity came up. As Max Klare redshirts during his rookie season, a tight end may not be out of the question either.
The 2026 NFL Trade Deadline getting closer. Here are a few names to track on our Rams trade deadline big board.
The Fit: Brian Thomas Jr. has been a popular name floating around Rams trade circles . Thomas put up 1,282 yards as a rookie and 10 touchdowns, but only has 812 yards in the 20 games since. There’s no question that Thomas would fit a need at wide receiver as the Rams are without Davante Adams for the next 6-8 weeks. While Thomas would slide right into the Rams’ “X” wide receiver role, it’s fair to wonder where he would fit once Adams does return. Both players fill a similar role on offense. As much as Thomas would be a trade for the future, they also need a player who can provide consistent production as they chase a Super Bowl title.
The Cost: The most realistic price for Thomas is a second-round pick. That’s what the Houston Texans gave up for Marvin Harrison Jr. a few weeks ago, and Thomas has been more productive. The Rams also gave up a second-round pick for Sammy Watkins when they traded for him in 2017.It’s possible the Jaguars get desperate to move off of Thomas and view trading him to an NFC team as a more attractive option. If that’s the case, the Rams may be able to acquire Thomas for the equivalent of a third-round pick. Thomas would cost the Rams around $656,000 for the remainder of the season.
The Fit: If there is a wide receiver available who would be a perfect fit in the Rams’ offense, it’s Josh Downs . Outside of Puka Nacua, the Rams don’t have a wide receiver who can consistently create explosive plays. They are also lacking a reliable option on third down. Downs is a player who could contribute immediately, but also fit into the offense once Davante Adams comes back. He’s a good separator with the ability to beat man coverage. Downs is a smaller wide receiver and built more like Zay Flowers than Tutu Atwell. While he can win vertically, it’s also not his specialty. He’s much more productive in the intermediate area of the field.
Watch Josh Downs slot left here. 3rd down in the red zone, Chiefs rush 7 and man up behind. Solution: run quick hitters and get open fast. Downs COOKS Sneed off the line, and a better ball from Jones makes this a TD. #49ers pic.twitter.com/31xTOk9vJn
The Cost: Downs is on the last year of his rookie deal and could be available given that the Colts are at 2-5 and just fired their general manager. He fits much more in the Austin Corbett and Kevin Dotson tier of trade than a splashy move for a star player. With that said, Downs could be available for a fourth-round pick. If he doesn’t re-sign in the offseason, the Rams could potentially get a compensatory pick in return. He also only costs $2.4 million for the remainder of the year.
The Fit: The Rams should get Kobie Turner back within the next four to six weeks. Still, Poona Ford played an important role for the Rams’ defense and is out for the season. Ojomo is a run-stuffing defensive lineman with pass rush upside. He would fit right in next to Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, and Kobie Turner and fit an immediate need.
Eagles DT Moro Ojomo with one of the best plays of the week to seal the game for the Eagles on the two-point conversion attempt. Jalen Carter gets popped, but Ojomo reads it perfectly and saves the game for Philly pic.twitter.com/d6cGHhKjBR
The Cost: Howie Roseman hasn’t been afraid to move on from players in lost seasons. Ojomo is likely going to earn a $100 million contract in free agency and that’s not a player the Eagles will be able to afford . It’s very possible that a fifth-round pick and a conditional fourth could get the deal done.
The Fit: Since the offseason, Vita Vea is a player who has been on the trade block. Vea asked for a trade back in July when negotiations on a long-term extension stalled. With Ford out for the season, the Rams could use a run-stopping defensive lineman and Vea fits that role perfectly. It may not be a flashy move, but as stopping the run gets more important in December, Vea could be the difference-maker the Rams need later in the season.
The Cost: Vea is not going to come cheap, but with the Buccaneers at 2-5, they could look to move on from an aging player in the last year of his contract. It’s likely they’ll ask for a third-round pick. While the Rams don’t have that in 2027, they could offer a Day 3 pick this year and a third-round pick in 2028. Vea would cost the Rams $1.4 million for the remainder of 2026.
The Fit: If the Rams make a trade, wide receiver seems like the most realistic position they would target. They need a reliable third wide receiver and an upgrade over Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell. It’s hard to see the Vikings trading away a player as they sit at 6-0, but Jennings has just four receptions on the year. He’s not a standard “X”, but fits into the offense when Adams returns. The Cost: Jennings is 29 and only has four receptions for 43 yards this season. If the Rams are looking for a low-value trade, Jennings makes a lot of sense. He could be had for a Day 3 pick swap and only has a cap hit of $2.2 million.
The Fit: Is it crazy to think that the Rams would consider trading for a kicker? Blake Grupe spent time with the Colts last season before the Rams signed him off the Jets’ practice squad. If the Colts can get value for their kicker, it might be something they consider. Trading for a kicker is rare, but the Rams’ special teams unit is just that bad.
The Cost: The Colts aren’t simply going to give their kicker away. Shrader is 19-for-21 on field goals this season and 6-for-7 on kicks of 50 or more yards. Would the Colts do it for a fifth-round pick? That’s a trade that ESPN’s Bill Barnwell suggested last week .
The Fit: It seems almost insane that the Rams would consider trading for a tight end. With that said, Terrance Ferguson has been hurt and Colby Parkinson has managed injuries all season as well. Given Max Klare was inactive and a healthy scratch last week, it’s clear he isn’t ready to contribute yet. Sanders also gives the Rams a potential long-term option at the position, with several of their tight ends set to hit free agency this offseason.
The Cost: Sanders wouldn’t cost the Rams more than a Day 3 pick and would count for just $656,000 against the cap this year. He’s a player the Rams could afford. It may not be a splashy move, but it also allows the Rams to continue leaning into 13 personnel.
The Fit: Again, wide receiver is going to be a position the Rams target heavily on the trade market. They are going to weigh their options. Jerry Jeudy and Calvin Ridley are both veteran options at the wide receiver position who could fit into that “X” role. Jeudy is slightly more versatile, which matters when Adams returns. However, with KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston emerging in Cleveland and the Titans at 1-6, both teams could look to move off of those two aging players.
The Cost: Jeudy has a very difficult contract to acquire. He would only cost $916,000 this season, but he has a $23 million cap in 2027, and because of his void years, it doesn’t make him easy to cut. Ridley is similar as well. title: Week 8 Consensus NFL Power Rankings: Rams Are Back on the Rise, but Doubts Remain
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7, 35-21 . After dropping in the consensus power rankings last week, the Rams are climbing back up. They may not be back inside the top 10 yet, but if they can start to stack wins together, it won’t be long before they are back there.
Until the Rams can prove they can win consecutive games and play consistently week to week, it’s going to be hard to trust what they can do. However, after rushing for 192 yards against the Raiders, it’s hard not to like what we saw. They seem to be a team with an identity again.
Oh my goodness the Bengals' remaining schedule pic.twitter.com/f7Mp0meoWr
Last week, the Rams looked like they had hit rock bottom. With the win against the Raiders, it looked like they may have turned their season around. Let’s jump into this week’s consensus power rankings.
The Rams move up two places in ESPN’s power rankings this week . They haven’t quite earned enough confidence from analysts to get back into the top 10, but it’s hard not to like what we saw against the Raiders. If the Rams can continue to play like they did on Sunday, they’ll start to earn some trust back and move back up the rankings.
Arguably the most impressive part about the Rams’ win against the Raiders was how they ran the ball. While the Raiders don’t have a stout run defense, the Rams still operated the offense through their dynamic rushing duo of Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. If the Rams are going to start to turn it around, that’s a gameplan they’ll need to stick to.
“There’s absolutely another gear from Blake Corum that we haven’t seen,” said Sports Illustrated’s Connor Orr . “And while it’s not the Sean McVay hidden weapon we’re waiting to see, it’s absolutely going to matter in January.”
After last week’s loss to the Arizona Cardinals, the Rams were close to dropping outside of the top 20 in The Athletic’s power rankings. Now, they’re back inside the top 15. Nothing is guaranteed with this Rams team, but they still have an opportunity to turn their season around. With games against the Chargers, Commanders, and Cardinals on deck, the Rams have a chance to go into their bye week at 6-4. If that’s where the Rams stand as they start to get healthy, they won’t be a team others want to play come December and January.
“Don’t look now, but the Rams could easily put together a four-game winning streak without batting an eyelash,” wrote The Athletic . “After dispatching the Raiders on Sunday, their next three games are against the Chargers, Commanders and Cardinals, who have a combined record of 3-15-1. There is plenty of time for the Rams to turn their season around.”
Nick Shook remains the lowest analyst on the Rams , but that’s not to say it isn’t fair. The Rams haven’t shown the ability to be consistent week to week. If the Rams can play like they did on Sunday over the next month, it will be easier to feel good about them going into December as they get healthy and fight for a playoff spot.
“Some might say this is too low for the Rams, but I’d like to remind everyone of where they stood after the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals. Their coach openly admitted they lacked an identity and were coming off an indefensible defeat that included a barrage of new injuries,” wrote Shook. “It was a much-needed bounce-back performance, but it’s not enough to convince me all of their issues are magically fixed.”
The key to the Rams finding their identity on Sunday against the Raiders was leaning into the run game . Corum and Williams combined for 192 yards. They were the first Rams running back duo since 2001 to have more than 90 yards rushing in the same game.
“If they can keep running the ball the way they did on Sunday, they can start stacking wins,” wrote Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio .
When the Rams lost their offensive identity in 2021, they leaned on Sony Michel to get out of their rut. If the Rams are going to be the team that many expected, it starts with remaining committed to the run game.
Following last week’s loss, it seemed as if everyone had lost faith in the Rams, and it was hard to blame them. However, getting back in the win column with their most complete win to date, they are the drug that you just can’t quit. The Rams moved up to No. 12 from No. 16 in Fox Sports’ rankings and could keep moving up.
“Just when I thought I was out, they pull me back in,” wrote Ralph Vacchiano . “It wasn’t just because of their win over the Raiders on Sunday. It was the way they raced out to a 28-3 lead, with some outstanding passing by QB Matthew Stafford and a strong, two-pronged rushing attack from Kyren Williams and Blake Corum.”
For the first time this season, the Rams looked like the team that many expected coming into the year. That’s not to say that they played a perfect game, but they were a team with an actual identity. After Matthew Stafford led the NFL in passing attempts going into Week 7, the Rams had more rushing attempts than passing attempts. That may not happen every week, but it’s a game plan they need to stick with.
“The team we saw beat up the Raiders is the Dream Team we expected to see before the season. The run game is back,” wrote Pete Prisco .
The Chargers are the only winless team remaining in the NFL and are dead last in the consensus power rankings. That’s a good thing for the Rams, who are looking to get a second consecutive win for the first time this season. However, the Chargers are also coming off a bye week.
Heading into the bye week, the Chargers had enough problems that they likely would have needed an entire month off to figure it all out, and even then it might not have been enough. With that said, the Rams can’t afford to overlook them like they did the Cardinals last week.
There is only one undefeated team remaining in the NFL through seven weeks. It may be harsh to only have them at six, but the Vikings have their flaws. If they can get out of this tough stretch of their schedule and look good, I can feel confident putting them in the top five.
With Caleb Williams, the Bears look like one of the best teams in the NFL, but still have a lot to prove. All eyes will be on their game on Monday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks.
