title: 5 Reasons Darren Mougey is Safe as Jets General Manager
full_text:
It seems like a foregone conclusion that the New York Jets will be looking for a new head coach after the conclusion of the 2026 campaign. At 2-5, it's hard to envision the team turning around their recent stretch of poor play.
One question that comes with a potential coaching change, though, is what happens to the front office.
Jets general manager Darren Mougey has done an admirable job acquiring talent across the board over his first two seasons. He hasn't been perfect, but many have wondered whether a decision on Aaron Glenn would also lead to one being made about Mougey.
New York would be wise not to bunch the two together, though. If anything, Mougey has earned the right to hire a head coach that best fits his model for a successful team. And there are five reasons the Jets should allow that to happen.
When Joe Douglas was first running drafts for the Jets, he was tasked with fixing the team's offensive line and finding a quarterback. Along the way, he needed to find competent players who could help the team in different rounds.
Instead, the team whiffed on the 2020 draft (Douglas' first), and swung and missed at Zach Wilson and the rest of the 2021 draft class (sans Jamien Sherwood).
Already, Mougey has proven to be far more successful at drafting than his predecessor. His first three picks in the 2025 draft class are all starters on the team and have each produced well to start their careers. The 2026 draft has five starters including three who have broken out in several games—David Bailey, Omar Cooper Jr., and Kenyon Sadiq.
Mougey will, of course, be judged on if he gets the quarterback decision right, but he hasn't made that call yet. And that leaves us with one clear takeaway: He knows how to draft well.
Should the Jets eventually fire Glenn, it will be up to Mougey to be at the center of a coaching search. Luckily for New York, Mougey has gone through this before.
As an assistant general manager with the Denver Broncos, Mougey was part of the regime that removed Nathaniel Hackett and brought in Sean Payton after a coaching search. If he was able to help the front office through that, and come away with a solid staff, it shows he can do it as the head of another.
Mougey is highly respected both in NFL circles and amongst the Jets' higher-ups. He should be given the chance to hire a coach who best fits his vision for the organization's future.
New York needs a general manager that understands modern NFL trends. Someone who will extend players early in negotiations to jump ahead of the market, as well as being willing to trade players for draft capital.
So far, Mougey has done that terrifically.
The trades of Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams were as forward-thinking as it gets. Instead of waiting around to see if they could be important cogs in the long-term future of the team, Mougey received three first-round picks and a second-rounder to aid his future capital. Along the way, he jumped ahead of the market on Garrett Wilson, Breece Hall and others who have received new deals. There are few Jets who could be described as "overpaid" under Mougey's guidance. That's another reason why the team is set to have over $80 million in cap space this offseason.
By keeping on pace with modern trends around the league, Mougey is showing his ability at being more than just someone who is overlooked as the face of an organization.
Mougey is not above mistakes. The team has made several since he took over the top job. Let's go through some of the big ones:
- Bringing in Justin Fields to start at QB in 2025 - Joseph Ossai signing - Not addressing wide receiver in 2025 - Signing Nahshon Wright - Uneven draft grades on Day 3 - Jamien Sherwood extension
But what's the common denominator on all of these mistakes? None of them is big enough to sink the organization. There will always be missed free agents. There will be missed picks late in the draft. But a good GM is able to move past those mistakes and find a way to keep the team afloat.
None of the whiffs from Mougey have ultimately sunk the Jets' future by any stretch. And for that, it shows he's deserving of a chance to correct some of those mistakes.
How many general managers for the Jets have been able to keep the team in good cap standing, have a treasure trove of draft picks in the next few drafts and seem to have already developed a young nucleus of talent?
The closest that comes to mind is the Mike Tannenbaum regime with Eric Mangini.
Mougey, at his worst, is a competent general manager. Someone who has a vision for the team, will make some mistakes, but also make very strong moves to improve the roster. At this point with where the Jets are, they can't really be in the business of moving on from competent people who do a solid job.

title: Darrell Jackson Jr. Facing Biggest Test Yet After Latest Jets Injury Concerns
full_text:
Not much has gone right for the New York Jets this season. Of course, not much has gone right for the organization over the last 16 years.
That said, there are positives to look at across the board for New York. Their young core, led by the last two draft classes, has borne quality starters across the board. The 2026 class, in particular, has seen several starters sprout in their first season.
An underrated name along that list is fourth-round pick Darrell Jackson Jr. The Florida State product was brought in as a project along the defensive line. Injuries, though, have brought his play into the limelight.
And that's only going to continue over the next several weeks.
New York hoped to use Jackson this season in a limited role as he learned how to play in the NFL. That changed when veteran defensive tackle David Onyemata was lost, potentially for the year. It's about to change even more after T'Vondre Sweat left Sunday's loss to Miami with a knee injury.
Sweat's injury is a massive blow to New York's already struggling run defense. He has been the Jets' best run defender by far. Without him, the team will be relying on Harrison Phillips and Jowon Briggs to carry the load.
Jackson will need an uptick in snaps as well.
So far, though, the rookie has proven up to the task. Jackson has proven to be above average in run defense by Pro Football Focus —ranking him as the 42nd-best player among interior defensive linemen. More importantly, he possesses an 11.4% run stop rate, which is third amongst players in his role. In his last three games, Jackson has recorded four pressures, a sack, a QB hit, and two batted passes.
To summarize? The Jets have something competent in Jackson. With more playing time, and a little more seasoning, they could end up coming away with an every down starter in the fourth round of this year's draft.
For a team that has struggled so much on Day Three of the NFL Draft, Jackson's play has been a welcome sign.
But it's only getting started. Due to the team's immense struggles at stopping the run, Jackson will be under even more pressure and play more snaps. While that can be seen as a good thing, it also lends itself to offensive linemen learning the tips and tricks Jackson uses. What makes him effective now could be obsolete by Week 10.
It's why this test without Sweat on the field will be a good barometer of how far Jackson still needs to go, and if the team has more than just a spot performer on the field.
At the very least, there's more to Jackson that fans will get to discover.

title: 4 Jets Most Likely to Be Traded as Deadline Sell-Off Becomes Inevitable
full_text:
Another year, another trade deadline sell-off for the New York Jets.
At 2-5, it doesn't make sense for Gang Green to be buyers at this point. New York has several veterans on expiring deals they could look to move to acquire more draft capital. The question becomes whether the team gets the right deal or not for any of them.
In many ways, the next few weeks before the NFL trade deadline will be massive for the future of the organization. If general manager Darren Mougey chooses to sell, it could add even more draft capital to its already rich collection.
It's time to break down which veterans may be on the move, and what New York could get for each player.
Hopeful compensation: 5th or 6th round pick
New York won't say what caused Brownlee to be a healthy scratch, only that they were dealing with things internally. With second-round rookie D'Angelo Ponds coming off a solid first start in the slot, it's obvious the Jets don't see Brownlee as part of their future plans.
It's hard to determine what a slot cornerback could go for on the open market, but it is something the team would expect to explore over the next several weeks. Whatever is the cause for the benching, it's obvious the team doesn't see a future with the former Titan.
Hopeful compensation: late-round pick swap
Much like Brownlee, Wright has watched himself be a healthy scratch several times this season. After reaching the Pro Bowl last season and leading all cornerbacks in interceptions, Wright lost a position battle to begin the year and just hasn't seen the field since.
It would probably be best for both the player and the team to part ways eventually. New York could look to get a late-round pick for Wright, but much of that will come down to cornerback-needy contenders on the market.
The longer Wright sits, the more likely it is that the team moves on from him eventually.
Hopeful compensation: 6th round pick
It's hard to envision the Jets moving on from a defensive captain and someone who has committed to helping head coach Aaron Glenn install a culture for the future. That said, Phillips has been very bad this season, and with the 30-year-old defensive tackle putting up career-worst numbers, it might be time for the Jets to see if they can get anything for him.
At this rate, the culture New York wants to bring in won't be brought in until a new coach is here.
Hopeful compensation: 3rd or 4th round pick
McDonald is another player who is not on an expiring contract. New York has his rights for one more year in 2027. It also means any draft compensation going to the team will need to be a little more because the other team isn't simply getting a rental.
McDonald has not been as productive this season as he has in years past as a pass rusher. While his run defense has objectively improved, it's gone from the worst in the league to still very bad. Incremental improvements for a four-year veteran are not enough to warrant being a pillar for a future organization.
New York could look to cut their losses with McDonald now knowing full well they are going to be drafting another edge rusher in the 2027 draft as well. They don't look like a team that's about to extend McDonald, so moving on makes sense. A lot of contending teams need pass rushers as well.

title: 3 2027 First-Round Prospects Should Be on Jets' Radar as Another Losing Season Seems Inevitable
full_text:
With losses piling up, it isn't too early to think about the Jets' 2027 NFL Draft outlook .
New York currently holds three first-round picks for next year's draft. As it stands, those three picks all fall within the first 12 selections , according to Tankathon . The Colts' pick from the Sauce Gardner trade is currently No. 7 , the Jets' own pick is No. 10 and the Cowboys' selection—coming from the Quinnen Williams trade—is No. 12.
The Jets have a chance to get high-level talent, and plenty of it, but with the way the season is going, Gang Green will look to shore up holes in the roster, making these options even more important.
The Jets are 2-5 after seven weeks, leaving the team and fans looking ahead to next year. As the Jets look to drift into another year of mediocrity, these three college prospects should be on general manager Darren Mougey's radar as potential first-round targets.
The Jets have a quarterback problem that has plagued them for generations. Geno Smith has looked serviceable on the stat sheet, but he isn't the long-term answer for success. Darian Mensah may be the answer for a team that has been looking for a franchise player at the position since the days of Joe Namath.
Mensah has been one of the nation's best players through the 2026 college football season. The 21-year-old has 2,155 yards and 22 touchdowns over seven games. Pro Football Focus also has the Miami Hurricanes' QB graded the best in the nation in that time . Mensah has produced everywhere he's been, which earned him a $6.5 million NIL deal with the Canes .
Mensah has shown that he can do it at every level in college football. Now the QB is thriving in Coral Gables. He has shown he can keep a number-one receiver like Malachi Toney sufficiently fed while spreading the ball around effectively. Mensah boasts inhuman accuracy and an arm strong enough to handle windy days at MetLife.
Whether he falls into New York's lap or they have to trade up, the Jets must look to bring in the player who looks like the best quarterback in the draft.
The Jets' defense has improved from the past season, but that does not mean that there aren't holes to be filled on that side of the ball. Guys like Demario Davis were brought back in the offseason, but the 37-year-old is in the tail end of his career.
With that in mind, Georgia linebacker Chris Cole could be a welcome addition to the defense come April.
The junior linebacker has 39 tackles, 2.5 sacks, and 3 passes defended this season. Cole has shown that he can play around the line while also being competent in coverage. He could fit into New York's linebacker room immediately, and the current Bulldog could learn from an aging superstar in Davis and could slot in with a resurging Jamien Sherwood .
Cole could be the next great linebacking for the Jets. A franchise that boasts the likes of David Harris and Bart Scott could use another freak at the position. Cole has the ability to make an impact as soon as he steps on an NFL field. New York should do its due diligence to see whether those first steps should be in Gotham green.
The Jets' secondary has still been a problem through the 2026 season, with the cornerback position being one of the most glaring issues . New York will likely look to bolster the position group through the offseason, which brings the spotlight onto a player like Ashton Hampton.
Hampton has been one of the lone bright spots for Clemson this season. The junior cornerback has been lockdown this season, recording nine passes defended to go along with one interception so far. He's also allowed only 40.6% of passes thrown his way to be completed, according to Pro Football Focus , resulting in a career-high 85.4 coverage grade— third-best among 108 CBs to take at least 400 snaps this season .
Hampton has thrived in man coverage. The Clemson product would fit in perfectly with the press-man scheme the Jets have run the past two seasons.
Gang Green has an opportunity that 31 other teams don't have in the upcoming draft. With three picks in Round 1, the Jets must do work to shore up a roster that seems better than their record suggests.
These three options should be high on the Jets' board as they continue to map out their draft plans between now and April.

title: One Jets WR's Outlook Couldn't Be Worse After Omar Cooper Jr.'s Breakout Continues
full_text:
First-year Jets wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. showed up and showed out again in Week 7's unfortunate loss to the Dolphins .
The rookie wide receiver finished his second full game in the NFL with 5 receptions, 115 yards, and a trip to the end zone. Cooper has made a name for himself , but his success means less work for other receivers looking to stake a claim in the Jets' WR room.
In fact, Isaiah Williams has been one of the casualties of Cooper's success.
The 25-year-old made a name for himself as one of the best punt returners in the league in 2025. Unfortunately for him, Williams has not been able to parlay his return ability into a cemented spot as a receiver for New York. Throw in his lackluster numbers and Cooper's recent performances, and Williams has been sent into even more of a background role.
So, what could his future in Gotham look like?
Williams slotted into the receiver core after Cooper got hurt in Week 1. The former Illinois receiver saw 137 pass snaps during the four weeks Cooper missed, according to Pro Football Focus . He has seen only 10 since the rookie's return. Williams ranks second among the Jets' receivers in snaps so far this season (255), trailing only Garrett Wilson (385).
That ranking seems fleeting as the Jets' receiver core gets healthier, though.
Clearly, Williams has become one of the odd men out in the Jets' receiver room. Even gadget plays that Williams once received have gone to Cooper instead. His future with the Jets is coming into question as Cooper continues to cement his role, and the team could be open to a split since Williams will become a restricted free agent in March.
Williams saw only seven passing snaps in the Week 7 game against Miami. This was a game that the Jets were trailing throughout, and Williams still could not get on the field. The former Pro Bowl alternate has still seen some special teams action, but even then, he has zero kick returns in the last two games, while his only punt return in that stretch went for seven yards.
The writing seems to be on the wall.
Williams has been frozen out of the target conversation as well. The third-year receiver has not seen a target since Week 5, which was a 16-yard gain. There is a clear correlation between Cooper's ascension and Williams's decline as an offensive asset.
The former Bengal and Lion saw 15 targets through the first five weeks of the season. Fourteen of those targets came in while Cooper wasn't lacing up on Sundays after he suffered a high ankle sprain against Tennessee in Week 1. Now the rookie has taken over Williams's spot in the pecking order, even outpacing Garrett Wilson in targets against the Dolphins.
Cooper has been a revelation for a struggling Jets team since returning from injury. He has looked to grab the starting role in the slot and isn't looking back. The Jets will benefit from his emerging stardom, but players like Williams will see their roles shrink. The promising returner is being reduced to just that as Cooper takes hold of the Jets' receiver room and fans alike.
With the trade deadline less than two weeks ago, Williams might not have much time remaining in Gotham.

title: Sauce Gardner Trade Keeps Aging Like Fine Wine for Jets After Quenton Nelson News
full_text:
The Colts are in fire-sale mode. After dropping to 2-5, they traded away All-Pro Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and look to continue to sell as their season falls apart. Although they weren't involved in this deal, the Jets might come out the biggest winner in all of the Colts' trades as the season continues.
Sauce Gardner was supposed to be the piece that pushed the Colts over the edge last season. That was one of the reasons the Jets were able to get two first-round picks for the cornerback. Instead, the Colts have fired their GM and are 2-5 this season.
As the weeks go on, the trade looks more and more like a Darren Mougey masterclass.
Gardner started his career hot. The former Jet was rookie of the year and had multiple All-Pro selections. That success hasn't followed Sauce to Indianapolis this season. The Colts have only won two games since acquiring the former All-Pro. To make matters worse, Gardner is having the worst year of his career in his first full year as a Colt.
Pro Football Focus has graded Gardner at 60.3 this season —the lowest mark in his career. This grade ranks lower than both Azareye'h Thomas and Brandon Stephens, despite struggles this season . Gardner was supposed to be a lockdown addition for the Colts.
Instead, he has been a thorn in the side of a struggling Indianapolis squad. The Jets seem to have gotten rid of Gardner at the perfect time. He is no longer a corner to be feared; he's become one to target.
Gardner has allowed a 113.6 passer rating and 21.7 yards per reception. New York has been on the better side of the trade for draft capital, and also on the field. As Gardner's performance has declined , this trade has the Jets making out like bandits.
The Jets got two first-round picks and Adonai Mitchell for Gardner. Mitchell has been fine for New York, and Kenyon Sadiq has been a welcome addition to the team. That said, the best part of the trade may be yet to come with the second first-rounder in the upcoming draft.
The Jets hold the Colts' first pick this season, which looks to be a top-10 selection (barring Indianapolis winning out the year).
The Colts' pick currently sits at No. 7 in the 2027 NFL Draft , according to Tankathon , and they have also lost three games straight. Indianapolis looks headed towards a rebuild, which means losing football games. A top-10 pick would be a welcome addition to a Jets team that still has holes in the roster.
New York landed a budding star in Sadiq with the Colts' pick last year, and they will have the chance to pick another if the Colts keep losing. The Jets also have their own first-rounder to use (currently No. 10), as well as whichever of the Cowboys' or Packers' picks is earlier, due to the Quinnen Williams trade. As of Tuesday, that would be the Dallas selection (No. 12).
Getting two first-round picks for any player is usually a good trade. That trade gets even better when the team you trade the player to underperforms. The Gardner deal just keeps getting better, with the Colts looking like a team with no identity and the Jets getting rid of Gardner's bloated contract.
In a season that hasn't gone as planned for New York, this trade continues to be one of the best things to happen to Gang Green in a long time, and time will tell just how much better it gets.

title: D'Angelo Ponds Could Force Jets to Rethink Jarvis Brownlee's Future Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
At first glance, it seemed like the Jets wanted to see what they had in second-round rookie cornerback D'Angelo Ponds when they gave him his first NFL start Sunday against the Dolphins .
It turns out that wasn't always the plan.
New York made previously starting cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. a healthy scratch going into the Week 7 AFC East showdown . Head coach Aaron Glenn clarified that the decision is one the team is handling internally with Brownlee.
In short, the Jets benched Brownlee for a reason outside of just injuries. So how did Ponds look in his debut start? Do the Jets still see Brownlee as part of their plans going forward?
It's time to break all of those questions down now.
Context is important when judging Ponds' first NFL start. Remember, this is a player who didn't get a training camp and had to learn a brand-new position at nickel on the fly. He received limited practice reps and has been thrust onto the field.
So it should come as no surprise that Ponds had a mixed day on Sunday.
Ponds was targeted three times, giving up one catch for five yards, according to Pro Football Focus . Still, he didn't have the best day tackling and was charged with a pass interference penalty in the end zone during Miami's touchdown drive before the half ended. PFF graded his game out to a respectable 64.6 on 30 defensive snaps, ranking 38th-best among 77 cornerbacks to play at least 20 snaps in Week 7.
The idea is that Ponds will get better with time and more reps.
And because of that, New York's other slot corner becomes even more expendable with each passing day.
The moment the Jets drafted Ponds in the 2026 NFL Draft's second round , it seemed like Brownlee's future was going to be in question.
The veteran CB was one of the unit's best players over the course of the last few weeks, but fast-forward to when he was benched after a miscommunication on a touchdown pass in New York's loss to New England, which opened the door for Ponds to play. It doesn't help that opposing QBs have a 78.6% completion rate when targeting Brownlee since Week 4, per PFF .
However, it's clear that the Jets want to see more out of Ponds. If they were focused solely on winning games, then it's clear Brownlee should be on the field some more. Teams have targeted New York's secondary more and more, and viable veterans are needed when that happens.
But that isn't the total end goal anymore. At least not after the team's loss to Miami.
Whatever the reason Brownlee was benched, it's clear he could be one of several players the Jets move for future draft capital ahead of the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Brownlee is under contract through 2027, according to Spotrac , with cap hits of $1.085 million this season and $1.19 million next . While the Jets should be rethinking their plans in the secondary, potential trades are still something that the team needs to focus on.
And that leaves Brownlee expendable for the future as Ponds gets more reps going forward.

title: 10 Best Aaron Glenn Replacement Options If Jets Fire Head Coach
full_text:
It seems like we have come to the inevitable following the Jets' Week 7 defeat at the hands of the previously winless Dolphins . It's hard to imagine head coach Aaron Glenn getting a third year with the team now 2-5.
And so, here we are again. On the precipice of a team seemingly in need of a new head coach once again.
This time, though, the Jets should focus on young offensive minds who understand how to elevate talent from a play-calling perspective, as well as someone who can get the most out of quarterbacks. Gone are the days when the team should focus on defensive-minded individuals or retread leaders. It's time for innovation and modernity.
Here's my "way too early but not really" list of 10 head coaching candidates the Jets should look to target once they turn the page on Glenn.
I'm definitely lower on Webb after his struggles in getting the Broncos' offense going at the beginning of the year. It's never a good thing for a team to have a head coach take back play-calling duties because the OC is not up to the task. I would argue Webb is the weakest candidate on this list.
Still, he fits the mold as a former quarterback with an understanding of how offenses should be run. For that reason, he makes the list.
I'm higher on Brian Johnson than most other people. The former offensive coordinator for Philadelphia had the unit as a top-10 offense in almost every category in 2023. He was scapegoated because of a poor defense and an overbearing head coach.
Since his departure, he helped develop Jayden Daniels in a historic rookie season, and now is working under Sean McVay in Los Angeles. He's someone who has play-calling and quarterback development experience and could be a dark-horse candidate.
If you checked in on Rees before Week 4, you could argue he was more likely to be fired than promoted to head coach. Since Atlanta got competent quarterback play, though, Rees has found plenty of deserving success. He has Atlanta's offense ranked sixth in yards and 10th in points. He understands the importance of the quarterback and can shift a scheme for one.
He's another dark-horse candidate.
The Commanders aren't a good football team, but I don't think that's because of their offensive play-caller. If anything, it seems like the rash of injuries suffered by their quarterback, offensive line and receiving corps highlights how solid Blough has been.
Washington was able to beat the Seahawks with a backup QB because of the design from Blough. He also happens to be one of the few offensive coordinators on this list with play-calling experience. I wouldn't look past this candidate because of the team he is on. He's doing a lot better than most would give credit for.
McCown has never called plays or led an offensive huddle as a coach. He's only been a passing game coordinator andf quarterbacks coach. Still, I can't help but think he could be the next Andy Reid-type coach—someone who knows how to do the top job without actually having experience at it.
As a former quarterback, McCown has had success as a leader and developer. He's someone who won't be a favorite for the top job, but someone who could end up getting it as a former Jet and who understands what the team needs.
Before Lamar Jackson got hurt, it looked like Declan Doyle was dominating as a play-caller and designer. Since the quarterback's injury, though, it's clear that while the design is good, Doyle is lacking experience as an adjuster.
That's okay, though. This is something that will be tested for him over the next few games this season. This will be a viable learning curve for the young play-caller before he inevitably gets a coaching job in the near future. As a designer, he could scheme some fun plays for New York's excellent weapons.
Unlike most people on this list, Scheelhaase is not someone who owns offensive coordinator duties alone. He shares that position with Dave Ragone. The latter, though, is older and has more of a history of coaching solely quarterbacks. Scheelhaase is younger, has worked under Sean McVay for longer, and understands the finer points of what the team's offense must be in the modern game.
It seems like this year is the time for him to get a top job.
Here's an option that will be debated plenty. Who gets credit for the rebound of Bryce Young? Is it just head coach Dave Canales or does offensive coordinator Brad Idzik deserve some flowers?
In reality, it's a little bit of both.
Idzik is a quality offensive mind that has taken on more responsibility this season. He's deserving of a top job considering he's someone currently calling plays and has found success in doing it.  If anything, the fact that he has found even more success as a play-caller with Young should lead many to see him as a legitimate option for a team like the Jets.
I love Udinski. So does Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen and quarterback Trevor Lawrence.
" He made a huge impact—just the amount of work he puts in, how smart he is ," Lawrence said of Udinski (h/t Jaguars). "He's really good at finding weaknesses in defenses, just breaking down the defenses and presenting them to us. He just brings a standard to the room. He never misses an opportunity to coach. He takes away a lot of the gray on Sunday and reduces the unknowns."
He may not be calling plays, but he's an offensive-minded coach with a philosophy that fits the modern game and a history of developing quarterbacks. I think Udinski and who's next on my list would be slam-dunk hires.
Unlike his brother, Kubiak doesn't have the same kind of play-calling experience that would make him a slam-dunk hire. However, the work he has done in helping Kyle Shanahan right the ship in San Francisco, despite so many injuries, cannot be overlooked.
The Kubiak coaching lineage has plenty of success. He doesn't have play-calling experience, but he knows how to do it and understands the importance of developing quarterbacks. As of this posting, he is my top choice for the Jets going into 2027.

title: Nick Sirianni Downplays One Big Eagles Concern After Monday Night Loss
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni pushed back Wednesday against suggestions that a lack of effort contributed to his team’s fifth straight setback, a 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on “Monday Night Football.”
“I did not see an effort issue on Monday night,” Sirianni explained. “Obviously, it was other things, which I’m sure you guys will ask me about. There were other things. But effort in no way, shape or form was an issue there.”
The comments came as the Eagles sit at 2-5, and in the midst of enduring their longest skid in the Sirianni era as well as the franchise’s first five-game losing streak since 2016.
The Cowboys controlled the line of scrimmage, rushing for 204 yards paced by Javonte Williams’ career-high 155 on the ground, while Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes.  Dallas' interior offensive line, particular guards Tyler Booker and Tyler Smith dominated against high-priced Eagles' defensive tackles Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis.
The Eagles’ defense as a while under coordinator Vic Fangio, finished without a sack, quarterback hit, or tackle for loss and allowed 416 total yards.
Sirianni explained that the staff grades every play for assignment, alignment, and effort . He acknowledged that no team bats 1.000 on effort, and that coaches highlight both positive standouts and negative ones for the team. But after reviewing the film, he said nothing stood out as an effort-driven breakdown explaining the result.
“I didn’t look at the tape and say, ‘Hey, this was an effort issue and this is why this play happened or that play happened,’” the coach said.
The questions over effort reflect a broader search for answers in Philadelphia.
The offense, missing starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, turned to Tanner McKee, who completed 23 of 35 passes for 211 yards, one touchdown, and one interception.
Saquon Barkley returned on a pitch count and scored early but was limited by his hamstring, as well as a back issue. Bright spots included rookie receiver Makai Lemon’s first career touchdown catch, but the added offense could not match Dallas after the Eagles briefly led 21-20 in the third quarter.
Sirianni did say he understands why outsiders focus on effort amid a losing streak.
“I get it. I would understand, everyone is looking for answers,” he said. He added that he keeps evaluations “tight to the vest” and grades film objectively based on process rather than solely on the outcome, stressing the importance of preparation from Monday through Saturday.
The remarks also land against recent comments from former Eagles quarterback Nick Foles, who said on his podcast that “culture” is an issue in Philadelphia, pointing to changes including the departure of longtime offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland.
Sirianni noted that Foles is not inside the building and that the organization must ignore outside noise, focusing instead on internal relationships and players who “deeply care.”
With two games left before the Eagles' bye week and the trade deadline approaching on Nov. 10, Sirianni and his team face mounting pressure.
Sirianni has framed the stretch – with games Sunday at Washington and Nov. 8 against the New York Giants - as an opportunity to control what they can control, improve daily, and stay locked in, leaning on past midseason turnarounds in 2021 and 2024.
Whether the film shows effort was not the problem—or whether execution, scheme, injuries, and other factors continue to overshadow it—will be tested further in the coming weeks.

title: 3 Eagles Who Should Be Untouchable Ahead of the Trade Deadline
full_text:
With how the 2026 NFL season has gone, the Philadelphia Eagles are expected to be "mild" sellers leading into next month's trade deadline, which makes sense. There's no reason why the Eagles shouldn't try to recoup some value for guys they don't view as long-term pieces .
But there are some players that the Eagles should absolutely hang onto, regardless of how poorly the season has gone.
It's worth noting that the players included below have all been mentioned, to some degree, in trade talks in recent weeks. There are a couple of other players who are obviously untouchable; the Eagles wouldn't even think about moving on from them, including cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and wide receiver DeVonta Smith.
Here are four Eagles who should be untouchable ahead of the trade deadline.
Cooper DeJean has struggled this season , especially compared to the All-Pro standard he set for himself in his first two seasons in the league. He's already allowed more receiving TDs this season than in his first two seasons combined.
According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Cooper DeJean has allowed 4 Rec TD on 40 targets this season after allowing 1 Rec TD on 125 targets in the 2024 and 2025 seasons combined. 😬 https://t.co/fSFHq8RS59
That's certainly not ideal. However, it's not a reason to bail on a 23-year-old defender who was seemingly on an elite trajectory and an integral part of a defense that won the Super Bowl two seasons ago, especially when the entire defense has struggled.
DeJean has played more safety this season compared to previous seasons due to a lack of depth at the position, and he has struggled with the transition at times , by his own admission. Moving forward, it might be in the Eagles' best interest to allow DeJean to focus on the slot corner role, where he has excelled, as opposed to bouncing him back and forth.
If they continue, DeJean's struggles could become a factor when it's time for him to ink an extension with the Eagles in the offseason. But trading a proven young player because of one stretch of relatively poor performances would be a mistake.
It's been a tough season for Saquon Barkley, as the star back has been heavily hampered by injury issues. He missed several weeks due to a hamstring injury. Barkley was limited in his return against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 due to a back issue. Plus, he's been running behind a makeshift offensive line all season when he has been on the field, so his output has been extremely limited.
But Barkley has still shown flashes of the explosive back who led the league in rushing just two years ago and totaled 3,145 rushing yards over his first two seasons in Philly.
Saquon on the move 💨 DALvsPHI on ESPN⁰Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0s6Ju1e0r8
The conditions have been far from ideal this season, but I believe Barkley can still be an elite back in the NFL. Plus, it's not like the Eagles have a star back in waiting. If they moved on from Barkley, they would have to address the position through the draft and free agency, and they already have plenty of areas like that. Factor in the dead cap hit the Eagles would take on by trading Barkley, and a potential move becomes even less attractive or likely.
B aun is another veteran who seems like a potential trade candidate heading into the deadline, but the Eagles shouldn't consider parting with the two-time Pro Bowler.
The veteran linebacker has been the heart of Philadelphia's defense since he signed with the Eagles before the 2024 season, and that remains the case. He's leading the team in tackles and tackles for a loss this season.
Baun's play hasn't declined, and at 29 years old, he should still have productive play ahead of him. The Eagles need linebackers, and getting rid of the best one they have wouldn't be wise.

title: 3 Potential Moro Ojomo Trade Destinations That Make Most Sense for Eagles
full_text:
A five-game losing streak and a laundry list of injuries put the Eagles in line to be sellers at the upcoming NFL trade deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10. It's not a familiar spot for general manager Howie Roseman to be in, but one he can use to put Philadelphia in position to compete for a Super Bowl in 2027 and beyond.
Trading away veteran players on expiring contracts is the easiest way to increase Philly's draft capital. That includes pros like cornerback Tariq Woolen and wide receiver Hollywood Brown . What's more intriguing is trading away a high-upside player on an expiring deal like defensive tackle Moro Ojomo.
Ojomo has risen from a seventh-round draft selection in 2023 to an impactful pass-rusher on a defensive line rotation that hoisted the Lombardi Trophy. He is entering his prime at 25 years old. The Nigerian native has logged 79 tackles, eight tackles for loss and six sacks through 49 career games.
Here are three trade destinations for Ojomo that make the most sense from the Eagles' perspective.
It would be logical to send Ojomo out of the NFC in hopes that he doesn't sign a long-term deal with a direct competitor of the Eagles. Jacksonville is no stranger to trades with Philly. Roseman acquired running back Tank Bigsby and offensive lineman Fred Johnson from the Jaguars just last year.
Jacksonville currently sits atop the AFC South with a 4-2 record. A menacing run defense has been the backbone of their success, giving up a league-leading 72.2 rushing yards per game. The same defensive line has struggled to frustrate quarterbacks, though, ranking 22nd in sacks per game (1.8).
Ojomo has posted a 17% pass-rush win rate , according to ESPN analytics. That has him ranked 17th among defensive tackles. It's only a matter of time before those strong reps turn into game-changing sacks. Pairing Ojomo with Arik Armstead would give the Jaguars a dangerous duo in the trenches.
The Browns were not expected to be buyers at the deadline entering the season; however, they boast a 5-2 record, with four of their next six games coming against teams with a losing record. There's a path to a playoff spot and opportunities to improve via trades. The Eagles should take advantage.
Cleveland's defensive line depth took a hit when Mason Graham suffered a left MCL sprain and an ankle sprain on Oct. 1. He returned to the field in Week 7, playing limited snaps and even limping off at one point. Head coach Todd Monken said it will be a while before Graham is 100% healthy (h/t Daryl Ruiter).
Acquiring Ojomo would be a way for Cleveland to give Graham and other defensive tackles crucial rest. Ojomo's quick first step and violent hands would fit in well on a disruptive defense. The Browns own a combined 18 picks in the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts. They can create quite an enticing offer.
There's an avenue Roseman can take other than simply selling Ojomo for draft capital. Acquiring a young player capable of helping the Eagles for years to come would be ideal. It would just take some finessing, like packaging Ojomo with an early or mid-round pick to a team in complete win-now mode.
The Lions' Super Bowl window is open with quarterback Jared Goff and running back Jahmyr Gibbs playing at an elite level. There have been reported contract disputes between Detroit and tight end Sam LaPorta. The Iowa product is in the final year of his rookie contract and is seeking a long-term deal.
LaPorta is exactly the kind of player Roseman should target and satisfy with a new deal. The 25-year-old has averaged 50.8 receiving yards and scored 23 touchdowns in 48 career games. LaPorta could form a compelling one-two punch with Eli Stowers, assuming the Eagles move on from Dallas Goedert.
As for Detroit, Ojomo would solidify a defensive line that already has Aidan Hutchinson tormenting opposing quarterbacks. The Lions could sign Ojomo to a multi-year deal if things work out, or earn a compensatory pick by letting him leave in free agency. It's a home run swing Howie should take.

title: Kracz: Eagles Facing a Harsh Saquon Barkley Reality After Loss to Cowboys
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Membership fees to the 2,000-yard rusher’s club are coming due for Saquon Barkley.
Perhaps that 2024 season is catching up to him . It was fun in the moment and a big reason the Eagles claimed their second Lombardi Trophy, but now it feels like playing 20 games that season, counting the playoffs—logging 446 carries and 2,504 yards—has taken its toll.
Barkley has played five games this season, and he has three different injuries: a stinger, a hamstring injury, and on Monday night, his back was added to the list. Not many players—maybe not any players—invest more time and money in their fitness regimen than Barkley.
But sometimes that isn’t even enough to fend off injuries, and he wouldn’t be the first running back to find the going more difficult after running for 2,000 yards.
“Every injury is its own injury,” Barkley said after the Eagles lost their fifth straight game on Monday. “For me, it's just unfamiliar territory. I've never really done anything like this to my hamstring. I've had little, small strains and stuff like, but all my other injuries have been, like, football, like someone tackling me or I tore my ACL.”
Now, this isn’t meant to pick on Barkley. Not in the least. He was one of the few who showed heart in what became a 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night. He knew his team needed a spark, and he tried to ignite it. He nearly did. His mind was willing; his body wasn’t.
Still, Barkley did what leaders do. They give effort then they take accountability.
While many of his teammates, such as Zack Baun, Jalen Carter, and Riq Woolen, declined to talk, Barkley was one of the few who stood tall in the locker room after their fifth straight loss to answer questions, something he did for nearly 15 minutes.
Barkley is battling with everything he has. Maybe he shouldn’t have played, but he tried. He laid it on the line. It added up to 10 snaps, and he touched the ball on nine of them, including the first two the Eagles’ offense ran. He turned a short throw into a 12-yard gain and then ripped off a 29-yard run. He capped it with an 8-yard scoring run that gave the Eagles their first touchdown of the first quarter this season and a 7-3 lead.
It was on that run when Barkley said he felt his hamstring grab. Then, he said, he tried to overcompensate, leading to his back locking up.
“Your back ever locked on you?” Barkley asked a swarm of reporters. “It's like, that's the only way I can explain it. Your body overcompensates. I'm not trying to get too much into the injury, but your body, that's how the body protects itself a little bit; something's a little banged up, so something's gotta work a little harder."
When Barkley has stayed healthy, he has shown he still has juice, a home run hitter in waiting. It’s just that those healthy moments appear to be diminishing.
Or maybe he comes back next year fully healthy, stays that way, and bangs out another 1,000-yard season.
But Barkley's 29 now, and typically NFL running backs don’t get better at that age unless they're a freak like Derrick Henry, who is in the 2,000-yard rushing club with Barkley, along with seven others.
Of the nine to rush for more than 2,000 yards in a season, Barkley and Adrian Peterson were the second oldest at the time of the feat.
Barkley ran his way into the club at the age of 27. Peterson was also 27 when he did it in 2012. Five of his next seven seasons were plagued with injury. Only Barry Sanders was older when he did it. Sanders was 29. He played one more year after his 2,000-yard masterpiece, then abruptly retired.
“It sucks when it's not going the way you want it to go,” Barkley said. “It's kinda like the school of thought I come from. I truly love this game, and I feel like if you're able to go, sometimes you gotta push your body to the limit, and I'm trying. It's just not responding the way I want it to respond right now, and it sucks because trying to be the best leader I wanna be, and it's hard when you're not able to be out there and perform for your team.”

title: McMullen: Potential Eagles Defensive Concerns Emerged After MNF Loss vs. Cowboys
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. - For one night, at least, the Eagles' offense looked like it had found something workable .
Tanner McKee went 23-of-35 for 211 yards and a touchdown in Monday's loss to Dallas; the unit put together a 17-play, 84-yard drive that ate nine-plus minutes to open the second half and briefly grab a 21-20 lead, and Saquon Barkley punched in a touchdown before his hamstring and back derailed things.
It wasn’t aesthetic or explosive outside of Barkley, and a late interception by the Cowboys' DeMarvion Overshown ended any real comeback hopes, but it was competent.
Given the injuries, the missing pieces, and the reality that McKee is a career backup, this may have been close to the top end of what this version of the offense can do right now.
And that still wasn’t enough. In fact, it wasn’t even close.
Dallas walked out of the Linc with a 38-21 win, 416 total yards, with 204 of those coming on the ground.
Javonte Williams went for a career-high 155 rushing yards and a score. Dak Prescott threw three touchdowns without being sacked or even meaningfully harassed for most of the night. The Eagles generated zero sacks, zero quarterback hits, no tackles for loss and essentially no consistent pressure on a Cowboys offense that had been struggling.
Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio’s unit, the one built with significant investment up front and expected to carry this team while the offense figured itself out, got pushed around on the interior and couldn’t get off the field.
This is the story of the 2-5 season in one night.
The offense—short-handed and operating with a limited ceiling—scraped together three touchdowns and kept the game within reach into the fourth quarter. The defense, the side that was supposed to be the identity, let a division rival run the ball at will and score on most of its possessions.
When the offense needs the defense to make a stand, force a turnover, or simply limit the damage, it has too often failed to show up. Monday night was one of the clearest examples yet.
McKee isn’t going to morph into a high-end starter overnight , and the skill-position group remains thinned out. If this is roughly the offensive floor-to-ceiling range for the foreseeable future, then the margin for error is small. An underachieving defense that can’t generate pressure or stop the run removes that margin entirely.
The Eagles are not just dealing with the absence of franchise QB Jalen Hurts . They’re dealing with a defensive unit that has the names, the salary commitments and the reputation, but not the results.
That’s the gap that is turning a tough season into a free fall.

title: Eagles Stock Report: Defensive Concerns Rising, Offense Showing Life Ahead of Week 8
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles offense showed as much life as it has all season, but the defense faltered by allowing 416 total yards in a 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night , Philadelphia's fifth consecutive setback after starting the season 2-0.
The Eagles (2-5)  went ahead 21-20 after an impressive touchdown drive to start the third quarter but were outscored 18-0 the rest of the way, including touchdowns by Cowboys' playmakers CeeDee Lamb, who tortured the Eagles' cornerbacks at times, and Javonte Williams, who ran for a career-high 155 yards.
Dallas (3-4) had come into the game, No. 31 in the NFL when it came to running the football, avergaing just 76.0 yards per game.
"It's never just one thing when you give up a bunch of yards like that," Eagles coach Nick Sirianni said when discussing the run game. "We've got to do a better job coaching. We've got to do a better job executing, getting off blocks, tackling. We had a couple missed tackles, but it's always going to be about block destruction, playing on their side of the line of scrimmage, and then us putting them in positions to succeed. I give them credit. They played a good game. "
The Eagles are now in third place in the NFC East, outpaced by the Giants (4-2-1) and the Cowboys. Washington, at 1-4-1, is at the bottom of the division and will host Philadelphia in Week 8. The Eagles will then finish a three-game stretch in the division by hosting the Giants on Nov. 8.
Here is the weekly stock market from the game:
The Saquon Barkley-led running game: Down their top two receivers—DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks—due to injury, the Eagles needed what had been a moribund running game of their own to get going. It did due to the return of Barkley to the backfield, as well as Drew Kendall and Landon Dickerson on the offensive line. However, on the second play of the game, a 29-yard run by Barkley, the dynamic runner felt a tweak in his hamstring, and his back locked up while he favored the injury.
Barkley tried to stay loose and in the game but each time he entered in the second half he left after one run, finishing with 62 yards and a touchdown on just seven carries. Backup Dameon Pierce was also somewhat effective, gaining 47 yards and a TD on 14 carries, although he was also forced to leave with an injury in the fourth quarter.
Tempo: Down 20-14 at halftime, the Eagles came out in the third quarter with tempo, getting Dallas in its nickel defense to strain a back seven that has had a lot of problems communicating this season. The result produced the best drive of the season for Sean Mannion's offense, a 17-play, 84-yard marathon that took over nine minutes off the clock. It was Philadelphia's first TD in the third quarter this season and Makai Lemon's first NFL score.
The drive also shortened the game against the more talented Cowboys but the Philadelphia could not finish the deal.
Makai Lemon: Without Smith and Wicks, necessity forced Mannion to use Lemon in better ways. Difficult catches over the middle of the field and run-after-catch opportunities on shallow crossing routes—things that Lemon excelled at in college at Southern California were a sight for the sore eyes of Eagles fans. Lemon finished with a career-high seven receptions for 67 yards and his first professional TD.
The Philly fans: There was some thought that Eagles fans might boo Jeffrey Lurie when the Eagles owner was inducted into the organization's Hall of Fame at halftime. That stemmed from the messaging and closed-door approach to the handling of Jalen Hurts's health . The popular QB1 had to be shut down after a superficial blood clot turned into pulmonary emboli, something neither Lurie nor general manager Howie Roseman has addressed to date.
Typically, when individuals are inducted into the team's HOF, they are made available to the media, and that was not the case with Lurie. Despite that obfuscation, Lurie is easily the best owner in franchise history and perhaps the history of Philadelphia sports.
The usually tough-minded Eagles fans were able to compartmentalize and show class while honoring Lurie.
Dirty kicks: After losing Britain Covey to a knee injury, the Eagles were forced to use Pierce and Elijah Mitchell on kickoff returns and each had a very difficult time handling Brandon Aubrey's kickoffs, often forcing a limited offense to take the long road too many times in the game.
The defensive front: The production simply doesn't match the reputation so far this season. Considering the expectations, there might be no more disappointing unit in the NFL than this Eagles defensive front.
Jalen Carter often flashes his enormous talent but is not consistent enough. Jordan Davis remains a two-down player despite being paid like a three-down star; Moro Ojomo has regressed recently and the edge rushers—Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith (out Monday night with a concussion)— have all battled injuries and haven't produced at the level expected when on the field.
Against the Cowboys, the front managed just five pressures as Dak Prescott got very comfortable en route to a three-touchdown performance.
Fiver: The last time the Eagles lost five straight games was during the 2016 season (Weeks 10 through 14) under then-first-year head coach Doug Pederson and then-rookie quarterback Carson Wentz. Philadelphia is not used to losing like this, and it will be interesting to see how the organization reacts to this kind of adversity with the trade deadline approaching on Nov. 10 .

title: 4 Winners & 4 Losers From Eagles' 38-21 Monday Night Football Loss to Cowboys
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – The Eagles took some baby steps toward turning around their season, but the fact is, they need to start taking giant steps if they want to extend their playoff streak to six straight seasons.
Sitting at 2-5 after their fifth straight loss, this one, 38-21, to the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football, they are now three games behind the NFC East Division-leading New York Giants in the loss column.
The last time the Eagles lost five in a row was 2016 in Weeks 11 through 15 when Carson Wentz was a rookie quarterback.
They will play two more games until the trade deadline—next Sunday night in primetime against the Washington Commanders on the road, and the following week at home against the Giants.
The Eagles offense operated better in Tanner McKee’s second straight start of the season, and that was one little step forward. So were third downs. The Eagles converted over 40 percent at 5-for-12 and was 2-for-3 on fourth downs.
Offensive coordinator Sean Mannion had some decent moments calling plays, and the offense managed to score their first touchdowns of the season in the first and third quarters.
The quarterback, however, threw a costly interception with the Eagles moving the ball into Cowboys territory down 10 with 7:47 to play.
Saquon Barkley returned, but his hamstring flared up, then his back acted up, and he played just 10 snaps. They were productive, though. He ran for 62 yards on seven runs (8.9 yards per carry) and had his first touchdown of the season with an 8-yard run in the first.
McKee settled in well enough to complete 23 passes in 35 attempts for 211 yards, a touchdown on a 4-yard strike to rookie Makai Lemon, and a pick. The QB finished with a 79.6 passer rating.
The defense was gashed all night, allowing the Cowboys to pile up 416 yards of offense and to convert 8-of-13 third downs.
Landon Dickerson was a big boost here. Getting the left guard back after missing the previous five games with a bone bruise was a big benefit. Pierce’s 5-yard touchdown run went through a hole Dickerson helped pave. The Eagles ran for 86 yards on the first half on 13 runs but fizzled a bit in the second half and ended with 109 yards on 21 runs.
The rookie sparked an 84-yard drive that used 9 minutes, 16 seconds, and spanned 17 plays, with a fourth-and-one catch for 15 yards, then made his first career TD catch on the same drive—a 4-yarder on third down that gave the Eagles a 21-20 lead with 5:49 to go in the third quarter. He finished with career highs in catches (7) and yards (67).
He has been with the Eagles for just two weeks, but he’s already ascended to the backup job, ahead of rookie Cole Payton, who served as the emergency quarterback. If McKee can’t find a way to win a game these next two weeks, Milton could rise to the starter when the Eagles emerge from their bye week to host the Pittsburgh Steelers on Nov. 22.
The owner was inducted into the Eagles Hall of Fame at halftime, and it was well-deserved. He has the second-most wins (317) and division titles (12) in the salary cap era that began the same year he bought the team, on May 6, 1994. His induction, however, was marred by another loss for his team.
It was invisible once again, even with Jonathan Greenard playing. It entered the game with eight sacks and left with the same number. Dak Prescott had all day to throw the ball and made the Eagles pay, especially on third downs. If you’re looking for an area the Eagles need to address in the first round of the draft, look no further than an edge rusher.
Entering the fourth quarter, the Eagles had just three pressures – two from Arnold Ebiketie and one from Greenard.
Defensive tackles Jordan Davis, Jalen Carter, and Moro Ojomo didn’t do much to stop the run. The Cowboys were ranked 30th in the league in running the ball, averaging just 76 yards per game. Against the porous Eagles, they pounded out 204 with Javonte Williams getting a career-high 155 on 25 carries.
The defensive back has taken a big step back this season, and he was victimized by CeeDee Lamb for a 9-yard TD on third-and-two to give Dallas a 10-7 lead with 5:32 to play in the first quarter. DeJean was also called for a pass interference penalty early in the fourth quarter to ignite another Cowboys drive.
The Eagles would probably be wise to trade him and get whatever they can . The cornerback hasn’t found the rookie year magic he had years ago.
His missed tackles were glaring and so were some of his busted coverages, like on the double move Lamb laid on him for a wide-open 30-yard catch to the 9-yard line with 12 seconds left that led to a field goal as time expired in the half. The 27-yard field goal from Brandon Aubrey made it 20-14 at halftime.
Woolen’s breakdown would have been a walk-in touchdown if Prescott had made a better throw. He also committed a costly holding penalty that gave the Cowboys a first down and kept a drive alive that led to the go-ahead touchdown after the Eagles took a 21-20 lead.
Woolen was beaten by Lamb and Prescott on a 16-yard throw with 1:30 to play in the third quarter to take a 28-21 lead after Prescott easily ran for the 2-point conversion.

title: Final Week 7 Injury Report Gives Desperate Eagles Offense a Huge Boost
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — It’s not exactly the cavalry riding to the Eagles’ offensive rescue for Monday night’s home game against the Cowboys , but it’s better than nothing.
Just hours before kickoff, Philly filled its three spots on the 53-man roster, adding:
Calcaterra and Stowers have yet to play this season after being placed on injured reserve before the season opener. What’s interesting about these three names is that Zach Ertz is not among them . The thinking had been that the Eagles made a deal with the veteran tight end to return to Philly in exchange for adding him to the roster at some point.
This feels like the point, yet it didn’t happen.
Ertz is out of practice squad elevations, so the only way he can play again for the Eagles is to be added to the roster. Clearly, the team is higher on Calcaterra and the rookie Stowers right now.
Speaking of the practice squad, the Eagles elevated outside linebacker Keyshawn James-Newby for a second straight game and running back Elijah Mitchell.
Meanwhile, Saquon Barkley is expected to return to the lineup after missing two games with a hamstring injury. Adding Mitchell gives the Eagles three running backs for Monday’s game, as he and Barkley join Dameon Pierce.
The return of Barkley and Dickerson should help the Eagles find some traction in the running game, and that would help Tanner McKee, who will make his second straight start in place of injured Jalen Hurts.
In last week’s loss to the Panthers, McKee attempted 45 passes while running the ball just 12 times against a Panthers defense that was one of the worst at stopping the run in the league. The Bay Buccaneers showed the Eagles how bad that run defense was on Sunday when the Bucs torched Carolina on the ground, with 49 runs for 258 yards. Baker Mayfield threw just 11 passes.
Yet, the Eagles insisted on letting McKee throw the ball and never took advantage of the Panthers’ inability to stop the run.
A more balanced attack against the Cowboys might help the Eagles snap a four-game losing streak. Having McKee throw the ball another 40-plus times doesn’t feel like a recipe for success, especially with the Eagles missing their top two playmakers—DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Tay Wicks (ankle).
That leaves the Eagles with a decimated receiver corps that includes rookie Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore.
Dickerson will be playing his first game since the season-opening win over the Washington Commanders. He was placed on injured reserve the day after the game with a bone bruise.
Cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee) was ruled out for the game against Dallas.
In addition to Smith and Wicks being ruled out in Saturday’s final injury report, the Eagles ruled out defensive back Michael Carter (abdomen) and OLB Nolan Smith (concussion).
Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was listed as questionable with an ankle injury, but he is expected to play. Outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) was questionable on the final injury report , but he has yet to be ruled out at the time of writing.

title: Insider Shares Steelers' Odds of Trading Patrick Queen
full_text:
Could the Pittsburgh Steelers trade Patrick Queen before the November 10 trade deadline?
While ranking the top 25 candidates to be dealt, ESPN's Matt Bowen and Jeremy Fowler ranked Queen at No. 20 while also declaring that the odds of him actually being moved are 20 percent.
"Rumors of a Queen trade persisted in the spring, with the Cowboys among teams that checked on his availability," they wrote . "He's also a 2027 free agent. But the Steelers' status as a 5-2 team likely keeps him in Pittsburgh."
It's no secret that Pittsburgh has dealt with a bit of an issue at inside linebacker over the last few seasons with Patrick Queen and Payton Wilson.
2025 was particularly rough for that duo, though Wilson has really bounced back and turned in a solid campaign before becoming extension-eligible next offseason in the final year of his rookie contract.
It's been tougher sledding for Queen, who has had some real low moments throughout the season thus far.
To be fair, however, the 27-year-old turned in what was perhaps the best outing of his Steelers career in the team's Week 7 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
In that contest, Queen ended New Orleans' final drive with a sack and also nearly came away with an interception in the first quarter while logging a team-leading 10 tackles.
That type of performance could convince Pittsburgh to keep Queen around, especially since it is 5-2, as Fowler and Bowen noted.
It may also be a flash in the pan, though, considering Queen's struggles leading up to that game whether it comes as a run defender or in coverage.
The Steelers would likely have to hold a ton of confidence in what Elandon Roberts could bring as Queen's replacement while coming up from the practice squad in order to trade the latter, and that simply might not be the case.
Pittsburgh will likely choose not to rock the boat and make a major change by moving Queen, especially if his turnaround is real, but it might still be at least a slim possibility.
As a two-time Pro Bowler with 108 starts under his belt, Queen could theoretically draw some interest given his pedigree.
As a rental who hasn't lived up to expectations during his three-year, $41 million pact with the Steelers , however, the price tag likely wouldn't be high.
Pittsburgh could probably find a way to land a sixth-rounder in exchange for Queen or potentially consider a player-for-player deal, but that's about the ceiling in terms of his value.

title: Steelers Legend Bill Cowher Helping College Team Find New Head Coach
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — Bill Cowher achieved so much with the Pittsburgh Steelers and has a legacy anyone would be proud of.
Cowher was successful in the other tenures of his career, including his time at NC State, where he was a linebacker from 1975-78.
NC State is searching for a new head coach after firing Dave Doeren this past week, and Cowher will serve as one of the advisors, per a letter from chancellor Kevin Howell and athletic director Boo Corrigan.
It's a big honor for Cowher, who will now have to help his alma mater get back on track and find its new leader for the future.
Cowher was a great player at NC State: a three-year starting linebacker, and still holds the record for most tackles in a season, 195, earning himself a spot in their Ring of Honor.
He is the only former Wolfpack player in the Pro Football Hall of Fame , thanks to his 15 seasons as head coach of the Steelers from 1992 to 2006, making him their most significant alumnus.
Schools generally have a wide variety of people involved in coaching searches, with the Chancellor and Athletic Director playing the biggest roles, but former players, coaches and important alumni also helping out.
Former Steelers cornerback Dewayne Washington, who played for NC State from 1990-93, is also serving in an advisory role in this coaching search.
Washington played for the Steelers for six seasons from 1998 to 2003 under Cowher, starting 92 of 96 games, making 19 interceptions and two pick-sixes, 74 passes defended, one forced fumble and four fumble recoveries, including one for a touchdown, plus 420 tackles (366 solo), 13 tackles for loss and one sack.
Cowher had an incredible 15 seasons as head coach of the Steelers, with a 149-90-1 record (.623) and consistently making the franchise one of the best in the NFL.
He led the Steelers to 10 postseason appearances, including his first six seasons, 1992-97, and four in five seasons, 2001-02, 2004-05.
Cowher won eight divisional titles, five AFC Central titles, including four straight from 1994-97, and two AFC North titles, 2001-02 and 2004.
He also led the Steelers to two Super Bowls, losing to the Dallas Cowboys in Super Bowl XXX (1995), 27-17, and defeating the Seattle Seahawks in Super Bowl XL (2005), 21-10, for the franchise's fifth Lombardi Trophy.
Cowher retired after the 2006 season to be with family and soon joined " The NFL Today " on CBS in 2007 and is in his 20th season in that role.
He works alongside former Steelers quarterback Russell Wilson , James Brown, Nate Burleson, Kyle Long and Adam Schein in 2026.
Dominic writes for Pittsburgh Pirates On SI, Pittsburgh Panthers Pn SI and also, Pittsburgh Steelers On SI. A Pittsburgh native, Dominic grew up watching Pittsburgh Sports and wrote for The Pitt News as an undergraduate at the University of Pittsburgh, covering Pitt Athletics. He would write for Pittsburgh Sports Now after college and has years of experience covering sports across Pittsburgh.

title: Steelers WR Situation Gets Some Positive News
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers finally received some positive injury news as it pertains to their wide receivers.
During practice on October 28, Ben Skowronek (calf) was back on the field while Roman Wilson (finger) was working off to the side for the first time since suffering his injury.
The players in yellow in this shot encompass the Steelers DB corps. I don’t see CB Brandon Echols in there. Echols missed Sunday’s game because of a hamstring injury suffered during the Bucs game the week prior. pic.twitter.com/neTy7uPtEQ
Skowronek has missed two games in a row while Wilson has been on the reserve/injured list for two games up to this point.
Considering Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) has also resided on IR since Week 5, the Steelers have been dealing with a lack of depth at receiver over their past few contests.
With Skowronek seemingly making progress while Wilson is potentially ahead of schedule, though, things are starting to look up for Pittsburgh .
When Pittman Jr. was initially placed on IR, the assumption was that Wilson would become rather indispensable for Pittsburgh's offense.
That was largely true for the first half of the team's Week 5 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts, as he logged 20 snaps before going down with his injury at the end of the second quarter.
Skowronek also suffered his injury in the first half of that contest, leaving the Steelers incredibly short-handed at receiver.
Germie Bernard stepped up in a big way though, finishing with 80 yards on six receptions in a 34-22 victory over Indianapolis.
The second-round rookie carried that momentum over to Pittsburgh's 26-19 comeback win in overtime over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Not only did Bernard log 87 yards across 11 catches, but he also scored what became the game-clinching touchdown in OT.
DK Metcalf had a monster day vs. Tampa Bay as well, posting 93 yards on 11 catches, and he followed that up by recording 56 yards in the Steelers' Week 7 win over the New Orleans Saints.
For as much as Metcalf and Bernard have rose to the occasion, however, none of Pittsburgh's other receivers have contributed, further highlighting the need for the organization to be aggressive at the trade deadline.
Skowronek's progress is major news for the Steelers, not just in terms of potentially inching closer to getting a depth receiver back but also for what he brings to the table as a special teamer.
As for Wilson, while he isn't eligible to be activated until Week 11, the fact that he's doing some work off to the side would appear to be a good sign in terms of his long-term prognosis.
Regardless, Pittsburgh could really use another proven receiver in addition to eventually returning both Skowronek and Wilson.
Pittman Jr. seems likely to remain out beyond his earliest possible return date, which would come in Week 10 after he misses the required four games while on IR, and it may stretch out quite a bit beyond that as well.
The Steelers' passing offense, while looking better under first-year head coach Mike McCarthy, still is not explosive.
Aaron Rodgers could use some additional help at the receiver position to help generate big plays in the passing game at a higher rate, which is exactly why acquiring a legit option before the November 10 trade deadline is imperative if Pittsburgh wants to reach its true ceiling.
Whether it's Brian Thomas Jr., Josh Downs , Ladd McConkey or another player, the Steelers can't put the phones down until they bring another weapon in.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Looking for Second Position at Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers aren't just looking for wide receiver help ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.
According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, the Steelers are also looking into the idea of adding a cornerback over the next two weeks or so.
NFL trade notes, per sources: • #Chargers have been hesitant to trade players for now. • #Steelers looking for WR/CB help. • #Vikings in the OL/DL market. • #Giants are looking for RB/DT. • #Bears remain active on the defensive side. • #Browns are “less likely” to… https://t.co/VcCrB4oocc pic.twitter.com/AIiAH1JgjK
Pittsburgh has a hole at the position after trading Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4, and with 18 total picks over the next two NFL Drafts, it has the necessary assets to make a move if it so chooses.
With Porter Jr. out of the door, Jamel Dean has stepped into the No. 1 cornerback role for the Steelers.
He missed the team's Week 5 game against the Indianapolis Colts with an ankle injury, though he returned against his former team, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, during Week 6 and was fantastic en route to a comeback victory for Pittsburgh.
Asante Samuel Jr. and Daylen Everette have taken on the brunt of the workload on the boundary, though the latter has logged just 14 combined defensive snaps over the past two games.
Samuel Jr. has been up and down and shown at times that he can handle the No. 2 corner duties for the Steelers , but he's not overly dependable.
Jalen Ramsey's done a pretty solid job in the slot, and Brandin Echols, Sean Murphy-Bunting and Terell Smith are all veteran depth options on Pittsburgh's 53-man roster who rarely, if ever, see the field on defense.
Given some of the secondary's shortcomings and the lack of another proven starter at cornerback on the boundary, it's no surprise the Steelers are considering the idea of acquiring one while sitting at 5-2.
Arguably the top cornerback on the trade market is Riq Woolen of the Philadelphia Eagles.
As a pure rental after signing a one-year deal worth $12 million in the offseason who has largely been quite good for a struggling Eagles team, Woolen is going to command a strong market.
He makes sense for the Steelers as a potential partner for Dean on the outside, and it certainly doesn't hurt that he played a big role for the Seattle Seahawks en route to a Super Bowl title last season.
Among the other names who could pique Pittsburgh's interest include Donte Jackson (Los Angeles Chargers), who played for the Steelers in 2024, and Alontae Taylor (Tennessee Titans), who has fallen out of favor quickly despite inking a three-year, $58 million deal with the team this past offseason as a free agent.
