title: Commanders News: Quinn Sees Bigger Role for Antonio Williams; Eagles Get Reinforcements | Burgundy Roundup
full_text:
With Terry McLaurin out for the season, it looks like Antonio Williams could be getting more opportunities in Washington's offense. Dan Quinn said Monday that he doesn't expect Stefon Diggs' workload to change much, instead pointing to Williams as someone who could see more targets. "I would say the natural progression is probably Antonio some more." That doesn't necessarily mean Williams will take McLaurin's spot, with Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown also being considered for that role. After leaving the door open for changes along the offensive line last week , Quinn had a little more to say about it Monday. According to the Commanders' head coach, the adjustments will be "more strategy than personnel," with an emphasis on getting better blocking downfield and finishing plays. That's a little different from the possibility of changing starters he discussed before the bye. Quinn also explained how Steve Wilks ended up joining Washington's defensive coaching staff . Apparently, the idea wasn't something that came up overnight, as Quinn and defensive coordinator Daronte Jones had discussed bringing in additional help during training camp. Other candidates were considered before Wilks was hired, and he'll be working with the staff during the early part of the week on defensive game planning rather than taking over Jones' game-day responsibilities. As for the bye week, Quinn called it "a much-needed reset in a lot of ways." Washington spent part of the break evaluating itself after a 1-4-1 start, with the head coach again emphasizing the need to put together four good quarters instead of the stretches of football we've seen through six games. The Philadelphia Eagles got some help back Monday, activating three players from injured reserve ahead of their game against Dallas. Three-time Pro Bowl guard Landon Dickerson returned after missing five games, while tight ends Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers were also activated. Saquon Barkley was back in the lineup after missing two games with a hamstring injury, although DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks remained out. Quarterback Jalen Hurts also remains on injured reserve, leaving Tanner McKee to start against Dallas. Washington gets Philadelphia on Sunday Night Football this week.

title: Commanders Expect Three Players Back at Practice, but Javon Kinlaw Needs More Time
full_text:
Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn delivered three pieces of good injury news and one piece of bad news during Monday's online press conference. Backup quarterback Marcus Mariota, defensive lineman Charles Omenihu, and receiver Treylon Burks will be returning to practice. Quinn didn't like the bad news any more than anyone else: "Javon Kinlaw is not trending as fast as we had hoped, so he'll continue to work, rehab with his knee." Omenihu couldn't play against the Giants and 49ers while he's been dealing with groin/ankle issues; getting him back is crucial to a defensive line that's been dealing with some injuries. Kinlaw, meanwhile, will continue rehabbing his knee after Quinn acknowledged he isn't progressing as quickly as the team had hoped. The news on Burks is good after he left the 49ers game with an injury. With Terry McLaurin out for the season with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee, Washington is looking for a spark from somewhere on the roster. Quinn added this little nugget about Stefon Diggs: "Stef is doing well. Workload shouldn't change as much; I think it'll be others that would climb up more." Quinn also spoke separately with WUSA9 about Washington's self-inflicted mistakes coming out of the bye.
Keep committing pre-snap penalties? Take a seat. Following the bye week, Commanders Head Coach Dan Quinn tells me the Commanders are cracking down on “self-inflicted wounds” If the mistakes continue, players could find themselves on the bench. pic.twitter.com/jzZ8DW15Nb
Getting Mariota back is more about the situation than anything. Washington certainly wasn't planning on needing Athan Kaliakmanis this early; it happened, the world didn't end, although the team still lost. Having Mariota back on the practice field at least gives Washington an experienced option behind Jayden Daniels. It should also be noted that returning to practice doesn't mean any of these players will suit up on Sunday, although returning is their next step in the process. Quinn also briefly touched on Jacory Croskey-Merritt's situation : "Because of the injuries we've had with his groin, we're going to make sure that this thing is fully healthy and fully strong to be able to really get going."
